reactions.enzyme_name: chloromuconate cycloisomerase
reactions.organism_context: Ralstonia eutropha JMP134 / Pseudomonas spp. degrading 1,4-dichlorobenzene via 3,6-dichlorocatechol and 2,5-dichloro-cis,cis-muconate
reactions.rationale: The 2,5-dichloromuconate / chlorolactone couple of the chlorocatechol ortho pathway is handled by chloromuconate cycloisomerase (EC 5.5.1.7, TfdD/ClcB), a single-activity Mn2+-dependent enolase-superfamily cycloisomerase that assembles as a homooctamer of one chain. Its dehalogenating behaviour is a consequence of the same cycloisomerization active site, not a second fused activity.

direction_conflict.note: The catabolic direction in vivo is cycloisomerization (muconate -> chlorolactone, then spontaneous chloride loss), i.e. the LLM's '<'; ModelSEED's '>' reflects the IUBMB ring-opening-lyase naming convention rather than pathway flux.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: carotenoid 4,4'-ketolase (beta-carotene ketolase, CrtW/CrtO type)
reactions.organism_context: Flavobacteriia/Bacteroidetes flexixanthin producers (e.g. Algoriphagus spp., Flexibacter)
reactions.rationale: The substrate is the C4 gem-diol intermediate of carotenoid ketolation, so the catalyst is most plausibly the single-polypeptide di-iron CrtW-type 4-ketolase (one oxygenase active site; its action at both C4 and C4' is substrate reuse, not a second activity), or the collapse is spontaneous. I could not confirm an enzyme assignment for MetaCyc RXN-19182 because biocyc.org was unreachable, so the identification is inferred from the chemistry.

direction_conflict.note: Dehydration of a gem-diol to the ketone is essentially irreversible in the written direction, which supports ModelSEED's '>' over the LLM's '<'.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: nitrile hydratase (NHase)
reactions.organism_context: Rhodococcus, Geobacillus pallidus, Ensifer and other nitrile-utilising bacteria
reactions.rationale: Butanamide / butyronitrile + H2O is exactly EC 4.2.1.84, nitrile hydratase, whose IUBMB systematic name is 'aliphatic-amide hydro-lyase (nitrile-forming)'. NHase is an alpha-beta heterodimer of two separate polypeptides sharing one non-heme Fe(III) or Co(III) centre, i.e. a two-subunit complex with a single catalytic activity rather than a fused bifunctional chain.

direction_conflict.note: Nitrile hydratase physiologically hydrates the nitrile to the amide (butyronitrile + H2O -> butanamide), so the LLM's '<' is the biological direction; ModelSEED's '>' merely inherits the IUBMB nitrile-forming systematic name.

reactions.enzyme_name: chlorophyllide a 31-hydratase (3-vinyl bacteriochlorophyllide hydratase, BchF)
reactions.organism_context: Rhodobacter sphaeroides/capsulatus, Chlorobaculum tepidum and other (bacterio)chlorophyll producers
reactions.rationale: EC 4.2.1.165 assigns precisely this reaction (Rhea 15069 / KEGG R09059) to BchF, a small single-polypeptide membrane hydro-lyase; hydration and dehydration are the two directions of one reversible activity, and the apparent C3-1 epimerisation reported in vitro is the same chemistry run twice, not a second activity.

direction_conflict.note: BchF's biosynthetic role is the hydration (chlorophyllide a -> 3-(1-hydroxyethyl)chlorophyllide a), i.e. the LLM's '<'; in vitro, however, the enzyme readily runs the written dehydration and the vinyl form is recovered as the major species, which is exactly why the thermodynamic call ('>') and the pathway call ('<') disagree here.

reactions.enzyme_name: chlorophyllide a 31-hydratase / 3-vinyl bacteriochlorophyllide hydratase (BchF)
reactions.organism_context: Rhodobacter spp. and Chlorobaculum tepidum bacteriochlorophyll a biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: This is the second reaction explicitly listed under EC 4.2.1.165 (Rhea 48772 / KEGG R09054): BchF acting on the bacteriochlorophyllide-level substrate. BchF is one polypeptide with a single hydro-lyase active site that accepts both the chlorophyllide and bacteriochlorophyllide series, which is substrate breadth rather than bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: The biosynthetic direction is hydration of the C3-vinyl group (the LLM's '<'), since the downstream BchC dehydrogenase pulls the 1-hydroxyethyl intermediate onward to the 3-acetyl group; the written dehydration ('>') is the in vitro reverse reaction.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: dicarboxylyl-CoA (adipyl-CoA) dehydrogenase, DcaA-type acyl-CoA dehydrogenase; a trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase in the reductive sense
reactions.organism_context: Acinetobacter sp. ADP1 dca dicarboxylate beta-oxidation; engineered reverse beta-oxidation in Corynebacterium glutamicum / E. coli
reactions.rationale: The adipyl-CoA / trans-2,3-dehydroadipyl-CoA couple is handled in native dicarboxylate beta-oxidation by the standalone acyl-CoA dehydrogenase DcaA, a homotetrameric flavoprotein with a single dehydrogenase activity, and in engineered reverse beta-oxidation by a standalone trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase. I could not resolve MetaCyc RXN-22975 itself (biocyc.org unreachable), so the protein assignment is inferred from the chemistry and pathway context.

direction_conflict.note: In native catabolism the flavoenzyme runs oxidatively (adipyl-CoA -> trans-2,3-dehydroadipyl-CoA), the LLM's '<'; the reductive sense written here is the reverse-beta-oxidation step and in practice requires a dedicated NAD(P)H-dependent trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase rather than the dehydrogenase itself.

reactions.name: fumarate reduction
reactions.enzyme_name: succinate dehydrogenase / succinate:ubiquinone oxidoreductase (respiratory complex II)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and other fungi, where ubiquinone-6 is the native quinone
reactions.rationale: Complex II is a four-subunit membrane complex (FAD flavoprotein Sdh1/SdhA, iron-sulfur Sdh2/SdhB, membrane anchors Sdh3/Sdh4); per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the catalytic flavoprotein subunit carries only the succinate/fumarate oxidoreductase activity. Called from established respiratory-chain biochemistry rather than a new literature search.

direction_conflict.note: The record is named 'fumarate reduction' but written as succinate oxidation; with ubiquinone-6 (Em' about +100 mV) the favoured direction is succinate -> fumarate ('>'), whereas fumarate reduction in vivo requires a low-potential quinone (menaquinone/rhodoquinone) and a distinct Frd-type enzyme, so the record's misleading name is the likely source of the LLM's '<'.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: acetylenecarboxylate hydratase (acetylenemonocarboxylate / propiolate hydratase)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas spp. (Yamada & Jakoby 1959, never sequenced); the tautomerase-superfamily protein Cg10062 of Corynebacterium glutamicum performs the same propiolate hydration
reactions.rationale: EC 4.2.1.71 was merged into EC 4.2.1.27, and the activity was only ever characterised as a purified pseudomonad hydratase with no gene or sequence, so its domain organisation is genuinely unknown. The closest molecularly defined catalyst for this chemistry, Cg10062, is a single-domain tautomerase-superfamily protein whose additional dehalogenase/decarboxylase chemistry is active-site promiscuity rather than a second fused domain.

direction_conflict.note: IUBMB states the reaction is effectively irreversible toward malonate semialdehyde: the enzyme hydrates propynoate to 3-hydroxypropenoate, which then tautomerises away, so the LLM's '<' is the real direction and ModelSEED's '>' (dehydration) runs against a tautomerisation-driven sink.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: unassigned; Neu5Ac2en is normally a sialidase (exo-/intramolecular trans-sialidase) elimination product rather than the product of a free-N-acetylneuraminate dehydratase
reactions.rationale: MetaCyc RXN0-7368 could not be resolved (biocyc.org unreachable) and the reaction carries no EC, KEGG or Rhea cross-reference. 2-deoxy-2,3-dehydro-Neu5Ac is generated as an elimination product by sialidases acting on sialosides, and no dedicated dehydratase acting on free N-acetylneuraminate is established, so neither the protein nor its domain organisation can be stated.

direction_conflict.note: No enzyme is known to hydrate Neu5Ac2en back to free Neu5Ac in vivo, so the written dehydration sense (ModelSEED's '>') is the only one with biochemical precedent.

reactions.name: cob(I)alamin:NAD+ oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00860 (Porphyrin and chlorophyll metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: cob(II)alamin reductase activity - no dedicated enzyme established; PduS is the one protein claimed for the job
reactions.organism_context: Salmonella enterica pdu microcompartment (PduS); otherwise free dihydroflavins and non-specific reduced flavoproteins
reactions.rationale: IUBMB deleted EC 1.16.1.4 in 2021 precisely because no specific enzyme catalysing this reduction had been identified and cob(II)alamin is efficiently reduced by free dihydroflavins and non-specific flavoproteins. The one protein claimed for it, PduS, was reported as a bifunctional cobalamin reductase (cob(III)->cob(II) plus cob(II)->cob(I)), so the functionality call swings entirely on which assignment one accepts - an honest 'unknown'.

direction_conflict.note: Reducing cob(II)alamin with NADH is strongly uphill (cob(II)/cob(I) Em' about -610 mV versus -320 mV for NAD+/NADH), so the thermodynamic call favours the LLM's '>' (cob(I) oxidation); the ModelSEED direction only runs in vivo because the cob(I)alamin is immediately captured by an ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase (PduO/CobA).

reactions.name: rxn00277
reactions.enzyme_name: hydrogen cyanide synthase (glycine dehydrogenase, HCN-forming), HcnABC
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas fluorescens CHA0, P. aeruginosa and other cyanogenic pseudomonads
reactions.rationale: The only established biochemistry linking glycine and HCN is HCN synthase, a membrane-bound flavoenzyme encoded as three separate polypeptides (HcnA/HcnB/HcnC, related to glycine and sarcosine oxidases); per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the assembly carries a single oxidative-decarboxylation activity. The ModelSEED record is an unbalanced, cofactor-stripped stub with no xrefs, hence medium rather than high confidence.

direction_conflict.note: HCN synthase performs an irreversible four-electron oxidative decarboxylation of glycine to HCN + CO2, so the LLM's '>' (glycine -> HCN) is the biological direction and ModelSEED's '<' is chemically backwards.

reactions.name: dichloromethane chloride-lyase (adding H2O; chloride-hydrolysing; formaldehyde-forming)
pathways: KEGG: rn00625 (Chloroalkane and chloroalkene degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: dichloromethane dehalogenase (glutathione S-transferase DcmA)
reactions.organism_context: Methylobacterium extorquens DM4 (METDI2656), Hyphomicrobium sp. DM2/MC8b, Methylorubrum spp.
reactions.rationale: EC 4.5.1.3 is DcmA, a glutathione-dependent theta-class GST homologue that works as a homo-oligomer of one ~33 kDa chain with a single GSH-conjugating/dehalogenating active site. No second catalytic activity is reported for it.

direction_conflict.note: The reaction is a GSH-mediated hydrolytic dehalogenation releasing two chlorides and is irreversible toward formaldehyde, so the LLM's '>' (dichloromethane + H2O -> formaldehyde + 2 HCl) is the only direction the enzyme runs; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing formaldehyde with chloride.

reactions.name: peroxidase, putative
reactions.enzyme_name: L-phenylalanine oxidase (deaminating and decarboxylating) / phenylalanine 2-monooxygenase
distinct_activities: oxidative deamination of L-phenylalanine to phenylpyruvate + NH3 + H2O2 (L-amino-acid oxidase, EC 1.4.3.2)
oxygenative decarboxylation of L-phenylalanine to 2-phenylacetamide + CO2 (phenylalanine 2-monooxygenase, EC 1.13.12.9)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. P-501; homodimer of two identical 68 kDa FAD-containing subunits
reactions.rationale: The enzyme that actually makes 2-phenylacetamide from L-phenylalanine is the Pseudomonas P-501 flavoprotein, which simultaneously runs an oxidase (deaminating) and a genuine monooxygenase (decarboxylating - 18O from O2 is incorporated into the amide carbonyl) with different pH and temperature optima on the same 68 kDa chain. ModelSEED's EC 1.11.1.7 'peroxidase, putative' label is a legacy mis-assignment (KEGG R00698 now points to a catalase-peroxidase, itself also bifunctional), which is why confidence is medium rather than high.

direction_conflict.note: Both activities consume O2 irreversibly and release CO2, so the reaction can only run L-phenylalanine -> 2-phenylacetamide (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of a stub record from which O2 and CO2 were stripped.

reactions.name: sn-Glycerol-3-phosphate:(acceptor) 2-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00564 (Glycerophospholipid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, FAD/quinone-linked (GlpD; anaerobic GlpABC; mitochondrial GPD2)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli aerobic GlpD (single chain) and anaerobic GlpABC (three subunits, KEGG K00111/K00112/K00113); mitochondrial GPD2
reactions.rationale: Aerobic GlpD and mitochondrial GPD2 are single-polypeptide FAD flavoenzymes with one dehydrogenase active site; GPD2's EF-hand calcium-binding module is regulatory, not catalytic, so it does not count as a second activity. The anaerobic E. coli isozyme GlpABC is a three-subunit complex, which per the protocol still scores monofunctional for the catalytic GlpA subunit.

direction_conflict.note: The FAD/quinone-linked enzyme is physiologically unidirectional, oxidising glycerol-3-phosphate and passing electrons into the quinone pool (the LLM's '>'); the reverse reaction (DHAP -> G3P) is carried out in vivo by the separate NAD(H)-linked enzyme GpsA/GPD1, so ModelSEED's '<' assigns a different enzyme's direction to this one.

reactions.name: L-cysteine hydrogen-sulfide-lyase (adding sulfite; L-cysteate-forming)
pathways: KEGG: rn00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism); rn00430 (Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: cysteine lyase (cysteine sulfite lyase, CL)
reactions.organism_context: Chicken/sauropsid embryo yolk sac; cysteine lyase arose in early amniotes as a paralogue of cystathionine beta-synthase
reactions.rationale: EC 4.4.1.10 is a pyridoxal-phosphate beta-replacement enzyme, and the sauropsid cysteine lyase is a single-domain CBS paralogue with one beta-replacement active site. Its ability to substitute other thiols for sulfite (forming lanthionine) is substrate promiscuity at that one site, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: This is the committed, effectively irreversible beta-replacement step of embryonic taurine biosynthesis (L-cysteine + sulfite -> L-cysteate + H2S), i.e. the LLM's '>'; ModelSEED's '<' would require H2S to displace a sulfonate, which PLP beta-replacement chemistry cannot do.

reactions.name: Propanoyl-CoA:(acceptor) 2,3-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00410 (beta-Alanine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: propionyl-CoA dehydrogenase / acryloyl-CoA reductase (PCD, in complex with electron-transferring flavoprotein)
reactions.organism_context: Clostridium propionicum acrylate pathway (PCD-EtfAB complex); the oxidative direction is also run by ordinary acyl-CoA dehydrogenases
reactions.rationale: The characterised catalyst for the acrylyl-CoA/propionyl-CoA couple at EC 1.3.99.3 is an enzyme complex of a propionyl-CoA dehydrogenase chain plus a separate electron-transferring flavoprotein (EtfA/EtfB) - per the protocol a multi-subunit assembly, not a fused bifunctional chain. The dehydrogenase chain itself carries only the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase / enoyl-CoA reductase activity.

direction_conflict.note: Both directions are physiological in different organisms: acyl-CoA dehydrogenases oxidise propionyl-CoA in beta-alanine/propionate catabolism (the LLM's '>'), while in Clostridium propionicum the same PCD-Etf complex runs reductively (acrylyl-CoA -> propionyl-CoA, ModelSEED's '<') as the electron-bifurcating step of the acrylate fermentation - a genuine organism-dependent direction conflict.

reactions.name: rxn00681
reactions.enzyme_name: (R)-2-hydroxyglutarate synthase (alpha-hydroxyglutarate synthase)
reactions.organism_context: Short-chain fatty acid-grown bacteria studied by Reeves and Ajl; the protein was never sequenced
reactions.rationale: The stub is EC 2.3.3.11 (propanoyl-CoA + glyoxylate + H2O -> (R)-2-hydroxyglutarate + CoA, KEGG R00932) with CoA and water stripped out. Wegener, Reeves and Ajl showed by differential heat inactivation and non-constant activity ratios that alpha-hydroxyglutarate synthase is a separate protein from malate synthase and the other glyoxylate-condensing enzymes, explicitly ruling out a single broad-specificity multifunctional condensing enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: The condensation is driven by hydrolysis of the propanoyl-CoA thioester and is effectively irreversible toward 2-hydroxyglutarate (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require regenerating a CoA thioester from a free acid, which this acyltransferase cannot do.

reactions.name: ATP:anthranilate N-adenylyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: cyclopeptine synthase (its anthranilate-activating adenylation domain)
distinct_activities: anthranilate adenylation (A domain; the former EC 2.7.7.55 anthranilate adenylyltransferase)
peptide bond formation / cyclization (condensation domain; overall EC 6.3.2.40)
reactions.organism_context: Penicillium cyclopium and related benzodiazepine-alkaloid-producing fungi
reactions.rationale: IUBMB deleted EC 2.7.7.55 (anthranilate adenylyltransferase) in 2013 on the grounds that the activity is a partial reaction of EC 6.3.2.40, cyclopeptine synthase - a non-ribosomal peptide synthetase whose single polypeptide carries two adenylation domains, carrier domains, an N-methyltransferase domain and a condensation/cyclization domain. The free adenylate shown here is an enzyme-bound intermediate of that megasynthetase, not the product of a standalone transferase.

direction_conflict.note: The adenylation half-reaction is reversible in isolation but is pulled forward in vivo by pyrophosphatase and by immediate transfer of the anthraniloyl group onto the NRPS carrier domain, so the physiological sense is ATP + anthranilate -> anthraniloyl-AMP + PPi (the LLM's '>').

reactions.name: D-Galactose:NAD+ 1-oxidoreductase
reactions.enzyme_name: aldose reductase (alditol:NAD(P)+ 1-oxidoreductase, AKR1B1); galactitol dehydrogenase in bacteria
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian lens, nerve and kidney aldose reductase; EC 1.1.1.21 is a broad-specificity aldo-keto reductase family
reactions.rationale: EC 1.1.1.21 enzymes are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 aldo-keto reductases with one NAD(P)-dependent carbonyl-reduction active site; the 'wide specificity' noted by IUBMB is promiscuity at that site, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Aldose reductase runs essentially irreversibly in the reductive sense (galactose + NAD(P)H -> galactitol, the basis of galactitol accumulation and cataract in galactosemia), matching the LLM's '>'; note that the ModelSEED record is redox-mangled - NAD+ sits on the galactose side and NADH on the galactitol side, the opposite of the EC equation - so neither stored direction is trustworthy as written.

reactions.name: Palmitoyl-CoA:oxygen 2-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00071 (Fatty acid degradation); rn01212 (Fatty acid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: very-long-chain / long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACADVL, ACADL); peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1) for the EC 1.3.3.6 variant
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial VLCAD (membrane-bound homodimer) and peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (homodimer); bacterial FadE
reactions.rationale: KEGG R01279 maps to EC 1.3.8.9/1.3.8.8/1.3.3.6, and both VLCAD and acyl-CoA oxidase are single-activity FAD flavoproteins that perform only the alpha,beta-dehydrogenation. The genuinely multifunctional beta-oxidation enzymes (peroxisomal MFE, mitochondrial trifunctional protein) act at the later hydratase/dehydrogenase/thiolase steps, not at this one.

direction_conflict.note: The flavoenzyme is effectively irreversible toward the 2-enoyl-CoA because electrons are passed on to ETF/quinone (or to O2 for acyl-CoA oxidase), so the LLM's '>' is the physiological direction; the reductive '<' sense is carried out in vivo by a different enzyme class (NADPH-dependent trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase).

reactions.name: 4-Chlorobenzoate chlorohydrolase
reactions.enzyme_name: 4-chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase (FcbB), the catalytic component of the three-enzyme 4-chlorobenzoate dehalogenase system
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain CBS-3, Arthrobacter sp. 4-CB1 and TM-1
reactions.rationale: EC 3.8.1.6 ('4-chlorobenzoate dehalogenase') was deleted as identical to EC 3.8.1.7, and the overall activity was resolved into three separate polypeptides - a CoA ligase (FcbA), the crotonase-superfamily dehalogenase (FcbB) and a thioesterase (FcbC). Per the protocol a multi-enzyme system is not bifunctional, and FcbB itself is a homotrimer carrying the single dehalogenation activity.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolytic aromatic dehalogenation via a Meisenheimer/aryl-enzyme intermediate is irreversible toward 4-hydroxybenzoate (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require chloride to displace a phenolate, which does not occur, and the stripped record is also missing the ATP/CoA that the real three-step system consumes.

reactions.name: ATP:propanoate adenylyltransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00640 (Propanoate metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: propionyl-CoA synthetase (PrpE) / acetyl-CoA synthetase (Acs, ACSS3)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella PrpE, mammalian ACSS3; ANL (acyl-CoA synthetase/NRPS-adenylation/luciferase) superfamily
reactions.rationale: KEGG notes that R01354 is the first of a two-step reaction of EC 6.2.1.17/6.2.1.1. Acyl-adenylate formation and thioesterification are two half-reactions of a single ANL-superfamily ligase active site operating by domain alternation, not two distinct catalytic activities, so the enzyme is monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The adenylation half-reaction is close to isoenergetic on its own and is pulled forward in vivo by inorganic pyrophosphatase and by the immediate second half-reaction with CoA, so the physiological sense is ATP + propionate -> propionyl-AMP + PPi (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' reflects the unfavourable standard free energy of the isolated half-reaction rather than pathway flux.

reactions.name: S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine:phosphate S-methyl-5-thio-alpha-D-ribosyl-transferase
pathways: MetaCyc: Amino-Acid-Biosynthesis (Amino Acid Biosynthesis); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); IND-AMINO-ACID-SYN (Proteinogenic Amino Acid Biosynthesis); METHIONINE-SYN (L-methionine Biosynthesis); Methionine-Salvage (L-methionine Salvage); Methylthioadenosine-Degradation (S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine Degradation); NUCLEO-DEG (Nucleoside and Nucleotide Degradation); PWY-6756 (S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine degradation II); PWY-7527 (L-methionine salvage cycle III)
KEGG: rn00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: S-methyl-5'-thioadenosine phosphorylase (MTA phosphorylase, MTAP)
reactions.organism_context: Human MTAP (homotrimer, PNP/NP-I fold); archaeal Sulfolobus solfataricus MTAP II; bacterial MtnP. Many bacteria instead use the hydrolytic MTA/SAH nucleosidase (MTN, EC 3.2.2.9), a different protein.
reactions.rationale: MTAP is a single-domain purine-nucleoside-phosphorylase-fold trimer with one catalytic activity, phosphorolysis of the N-glycosidic bond of MTA. Some orthologues (Sulfolobus MTAP II, 'MeSAdo/Ado phosphorylase') also accept adenosine, but that is broadened substrate specificity on the same chemistry, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: MTAP functions physiologically only in the phosphorolytic direction (MTA + Pi -> adenine + 5-methylthioribose-1-P) as the committed step of the methionine salvage cycle, which supports the LLM's '>' rather than ModelSEED's MTA-synthesising '<'.

reactions.name: Guanine aminohydrolase
pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); Energy-Metabolism (Generation of Precursor Metabolite and Energy); Fermentation (); Guanosine-Nucleotides-Degradation (Guanosine Nucleotide Degradation); NUCLEO-DEG (Nucleoside and Nucleotide Degradation); P164-PWY (purine nucleobases degradation I (anaerobic)); P165-PWY (superpathway of purines degradation in plants); PWY-5044 (purine nucleotides degradation I (plants)); PWY-5497 (purine nucleobases degradation II (anaerobic)); PWY-6353 (purine nucleotides degradation II (aerobic)); PWY-6595 (superpathway of guanosine nucleotides degradation (plants)); PWY-6606 (guanosine nucleotides degradation II); PWY-6608 (guanosine nucleotides degradation III); Purine-Degradation (Purine Nucleotide Degradation); Urate-Degradation (Urate Degradation)
KEGG: rn00230 (Purine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Guanine deaminase (guanase)
reactions.organism_context: Bacterial GuaD (e.g. Klebsiella pneumoniae, E. coli) in the allantoinase/guanine-deaminase gene cluster; mammalian GDA/cypin.
reactions.rationale: Guanine deaminase is a single-active-site amidohydrolase-fold (or cytidine-deaminase-fold) Zn enzyme with one catalytic activity, hydrolytic C2 deamination of guanine. Mammalian GDA/cypin additionally binds PSD-95 and promotes tubulin polymerisation, but those are moonlighting (non-catalytic) roles and are excluded by protocol.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolytic deamination with release of free ammonia is effectively irreversible and the enzyme has no documented aminating activity, so the catabolic direction guanine -> xanthine + NH3 ('>') is the one the enzyme can run; ModelSEED's '<' would require xanthine amination.

reactions.name: hypotaurine:NAD+ oxidoreductase
pathways: MetaCyc: PWY-5331 (taurine biosynthesis I); PWY-7850 (taurine biosynthesis II); S-CONTAINING-SECONDARY-CMPD-SYN (Sulfur-Containing Secondary Compound Biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis); Taurine-Biosynthesis (Taurine Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00430 (Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified (EC 1.8.1.3 'hypotaurine dehydrogenase' has never been purified, cloned or assigned a gene)
reactions.organism_context: EC 1.8.1.3 derives from an old rat-liver activity. The only molecularly identified hypotaurine -> taurine catalyst is flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 (FMO1), which is NADPH/O2-dependent, not NAD+-dependent.
reactions.rationale: No protein has ever been assigned to the NAD+-linked hypotaurine dehydrogenase activity, so the catalysing enzyme cannot be identified and its functionality is genuinely unknown. The nearest characterised enzyme, FMO1, is a monofunctional flavin monooxygenase running a different cofactor chemistry.

direction_conflict.note: Every characterised route from hypotaurine to taurine (FMO1, and non-enzymatic oxidation) is an irreversible oxidation, so if any enzyme runs this it is in the taurine-forming direction ('>'); there is no enzymatic precedent for reducing taurine back to hypotaurine with NADH.

reactions.name: acetyl-CoA:hydrogen-sulfide S-acetyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified (EC 2.3.1.10 'hydrogen-sulfide S-acetyltransferase' is a 1961 EC entry resting on a single 1954 report of enzymatic thioltransacetylation; no gene or protein has been assigned)
reactions.rationale: The KEGG/IUBMB EC 2.3.1.10 entry carries no organism, gene or sequence and only one 1954 reference (Brady & Stadtman, PMID 13221570), which I did not retrieve through the literature tools; literature searches for a hydrogen-sulfide S-acetyltransferase or a thioacetate-forming acetyl-CoA enzyme returned nothing. The catalysing protein is unknown, so no functionality call is defensible.

direction_conflict.note: The one historical assay measured acetyl transfer from acetyl-CoA onto sulfide (thioacetate formation), i.e. left-to-right as written ('>'), but with no identified enzyme neither direction has real enzymological support.

reactions.name: 3'-Phosphoadenylyl-sulfate:benzenamine N-sulfotransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: Arylamine N-sulfotransferase (cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase; SULT1A-type)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic SULTs (human brain/liver arylamine sulfotransferase). Note that bacterial 'arylamine sulfotransferase' (ASST, Eubacterium/Desulfitobacterium) is an unrelated periplasmic enzyme that uses aryl sulfate esters, not PAPS, so it is not the catalyst of this PAPS-dependent reaction.
reactions.rationale: The PAPS-dependent N-sulfonation of aniline is carried out by a cytosolic sulfotransferase, a single-domain alpha/beta SULT-fold protein with one PAPS-binding catalytic site and one activity. Enzyme identity is inferred from the cofactor and chemistry plus the purified human brain arylamine sulfotransferase, not from a paper on aniline specifically, hence medium confidence.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation is driven essentially irreversibly by the high group-transfer potential of the PAPS sulfuryl group (PAPS -> PAP), so the sulfonating direction ('>') is the only one cytosolic SULTs run; they cannot regenerate PAPS from PAP.

reactions.name: D-cysteine sulfide-lyase (deaminating; pyruvate-forming)
pathways: KEGG: rn00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: D-cysteine desulfhydrase (D-cysteine sulfide-lyase)
reactions.organism_context: Salmonella typhimurium and E. coli DcyD; Arabidopsis DCD; widespread in Methylobacterium alongside ACC deaminase.
reactions.rationale: DcyD is a fold-type II PLP enzyme (ACC-deaminase/tryptophan-synthase-beta family) with a single active site that performs one alpha,beta-elimination on D-cysteine; structural and mutational work on the Salmonella enzyme describes only this activity. It is encoded separately from, not fused to, the related ACC deaminase.

direction_conflict.note: The PLP-dependent beta-elimination releases H2S, pyruvate and ammonia irreversibly (the aminoacrylate intermediate hydrolyses spontaneously), so only the degradative direction ('>') is enzymatically accessible; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing H2S, pyruvate and NH3 into D-cysteine.

reactions.name: S-Adenosyl-L-methionine:guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: Amino-Acid-Degradation (Amino Acid Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); GLYCGREAT-PWY (creatine biosynthesis); GLYCINE-DEG (Glycine Degradation); Polyamine-Biosynthesis (Amine and Polyamine Biosynthesis); Proteinogenic-Amino-Acids-Degradation (Proteinogenic Amino Acid Degradation)
KEGG: rn00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism); rn00330 (Arginine and proline metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT)
reactions.organism_context: Vertebrate liver/pancreas (rat and human GAMT); conserved back to amphioxus.
reactions.rationale: Crystal structures of rat GAMT and its ternary complexes show a single Rossmann-like class-I SAM-methyltransferase domain with one active site and one activity, methyl transfer from SAM to the guanidino nitrogen of guanidinoacetate. No second catalytic activity is reported.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and GAMT has no demethylase activity, so the creatine-forming direction ('>') is the only one the enzyme runs; the reverse would require re-methylating SAH, which GAMT cannot do.

reactions.name: rxn01470
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme; geranyl diphosphate -> iridodial is a lumped multi-enzyme conversion (geraniol synthase -> geraniol 8-hydroxylase CYP76B6 -> 8-hydroxygeraniol oxidoreductase -> iridoid synthase)
reactions.organism_context: Catharanthus roseus, Gardenia jasminoides and other iridoid-producing plants; iridoid synthase (ISY) is a member of the progesterone 5beta-reductase family.
reactions.rationale: The reaction as written collapses at least four separate catalytic steps run by four unrelated proteins, so there is no single catalysing enzyme to classify; the terminal enzyme, iridoid synthase, is itself a monofunctional NADPH-dependent reductive cyclase. ModelSEED gives this reaction no EC number and no xrefs, consistent with it being a lumped placeholder.

direction_conflict.note: The committed step (iridoid synthase, NADPH-dependent reductive cyclisation of 8-oxogeranial) is irreversible toward iridodial, so the biosynthetic direction ('>') is the only plausible one, but the lumped reaction has no single catalyst to anchor a direction call.

reactions.name: ATP:thiamine phosphotransferase
reactions.reaction: (1) ATP[0] + (1) Thiamin[0] <= (1) ADP[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) Thiamine phosphate[0]
pathways: MetaCyc: Cofactor-Biosynthesis (Cofactor, Prosthetic Group, Electron Carrier, and Vitamin Biosynthesis); PWY-6896 (thiamine salvage I); Thiamin-Salvage (Thiamine Salvage); Thiamine-Biosynthesis (Thiamine Biosynthesis); Vitamin-Biosynthesis (Vitamin Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00730 (Thiamine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Thiamine kinase (ThiK / YcfN)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli and Salmonella enterica thiamine salvage; the eukaryotic salvage enzyme is instead thiamine pyrophosphokinase (EC 2.7.6.2), a different protein.
reactions.rationale: ThiK/YcfN was identified as the missing bacterial thiamine kinase and is a small-molecule kinase with a single activity, ATP-dependent phosphorylation of thiamine to thiamine monophosphate. Its secondary contribution to cobinamide salvage is the same phosphotransfer chemistry acting on another substrate, i.e. substrate promiscuity rather than a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: ATP-dependent phosphorylation of a hydroxyl is effectively irreversible under cellular ATP/ADP ratios and a kinase does not run the phosphatase reaction, so the phosphorylating direction ('>') matches the enzymology against ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.name: Guanosine aminohydrolase
pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); Guanosine-Nucleotides-Degradation (Guanosine Nucleotide Degradation); NUCLEO-DEG (Nucleoside and Nucleotide Degradation); P165-PWY (superpathway of purines degradation in plants); PWY-5044 (purine nucleotides degradation I (plants)); PWY-6595 (superpathway of guanosine nucleotides degradation (plants)); PWY-6607 (guanosine nucleotides degradation I); Purine-Degradation (Purine Nucleotide Degradation); Urate-Degradation (Urate Degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: Guanosine deaminase (GSDA)
reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana GSDA, a homodimeric cytidine-deaminase-fold Zn enzyme; the plant route generating xanthosine in purine nucleoside catabolism.
reactions.rationale: Cocrystal, mutational and dimer-asymmetry studies of AtGSDA describe one zinc active site carrying out a single activity, hydrolytic deamination of guanosine (and 2'-deoxyguanosine, the same chemistry on a related substrate). No second catalytic domain is reported.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolytic deamination releasing free ammonia is irreversible and GSDA is a purely catabolic enzyme feeding xanthosine into purine degradation, so the deaminating direction ('>') is the enzymatically supported one.

reactions.name: Feruloyl-CoA:quinate O-(hydroxycinnamoyl)transferase
reactions.enzyme_name: Hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase (HQT; the closely related HCT acts on shikimate)
reactions.organism_context: Plant BAHD acyltransferase family: Solanum lycopersicum and S. tuberosum HQT, Lonicera japonica HQT, Cynara (globe artichoke) HQT-like enzymes; chlorogenic/caffeoylquinic acid biosynthesis.
reactions.rationale: HQT is a single-chain BAHD acyltransferase with one HXXXD catalytic motif and one activity, transfer of a hydroxycinnamoyl group from CoA to the quinate hydroxyl. Gene-editing and silencing studies treat it as a single-activity enzyme; no second catalytic domain is described.

direction_conflict.note: BAHD hydroxycinnamoyl transfer between a CoA thioester and an ester acceptor is genuinely reversible in vitro, so the direction here is set by the acyl-CoA/CoA pool rather than by the enzyme; in planta the ester-forming ('>') direction dominates, which is consistent with the LLM call and makes ModelSEED's hard '<' hard to justify.

reactions.name: L-Pipecolate:(acceptor) 1,6-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00310 (Lysine degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: L-pipecolate oxidase / dehydrogenase (sarcosine-oxidase-family FAD amine oxidase; PIPOX)
reactions.organism_context: Human peroxisomal L-pipecolic acid oxidase (PIPOX) and the Arabidopsis peroxisomal sarcosine/pipecolate oxidase; both are monomeric-sarcosine-oxidase homologues. Bacterial/mitochondrial L-pipecolate dehydrogenases pass electrons to an acceptor other than O2, as written here.
reactions.rationale: PIPOX is a single covalently flavinylated amine-oxidase domain that oxidises both L-pipecolate and sarcosine; that is one catalytic chemistry (flavin-dependent oxidation of a secondary amine) applied to two substrates, which is broad specificity, not bifunctionality. Confidence is medium because the exact protein running the acceptor-linked (EC 1.5.99.3) version of this reaction in a given organism is not pinned down.

direction_conflict.note: Flavin-dependent oxidation of pipecolate to the cyclic imine delta-1-piperideine-6-carboxylate is physiologically irreversible (the imine is consumed downstream in lysine degradation), so the oxidative direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

reactions.name: Stearoyl-CoA:malonyl-CoA C-acyltransferase (decarboxylating,
reactions.reaction: (2) NADH[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) Malonyl-CoA[0] + (1) strcoa[0] <= (2) NAD[0] + (1) CO2[0] + (1) Icosanoyl-CoA[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme; the C18->C20 acyl-CoA elongation is run by the four-component fatty acid elongase system (condensing enzyme KCS/ELOVL, 3-oxoacyl-CoA reductase, 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratase, enoyl-CoA reductase). The acyltransferase step named here is the condensing enzyme.
reactions.organism_context: Plant (FAE1/KCS) and animal (ELOVL) endoplasmic-reticulum elongase systems; also a membrane elongase complex in fungi such as Magnaporthe oryzae.
reactions.rationale: EC 2.3.1.119 (icosanoyl-CoA synthase) was deleted by IUBMB in 2015 precisely because it is not one enzyme: it is now covered by EC 2.3.1.199, 1.1.1.330, 4.2.1.134 and 1.3.1.93, four separate monofunctional polypeptides that associate as a membrane elongase complex. Per protocol this is a multi-subunit system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the condensing subunit that carries the named acyltransferase step is scored monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: Condensation is driven irreversibly by decarboxylation of malonyl-CoA and the cycle is completed by two irreversible NAD(P)H reductions, so elongation runs only toward icosanoyl-CoA ('>'); note also that elongases use NADPH, so this NADH-linked variant is the non-physiological twin of rxn01592.

reactions.name: Stearoyl-CoA:malonyl-CoA C-acyltransferase (decarboxylating,
reactions.reaction: (2) NADPH[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) Malonyl-CoA[0] + (1) strcoa[0] <= (2) NADP[0] + (1) CO2[0] + (1) Icosanoyl-CoA[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme; the C18->C20 acyl-CoA elongation is run by the four-component fatty acid elongase system (condensing enzyme KCS/ELOVL, 3-oxoacyl-CoA reductase, 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratase, enoyl-CoA reductase). The acyltransferase step named here is the condensing enzyme.
reactions.organism_context: Plant (FAE1/KCS) and animal (ELOVL) endoplasmic-reticulum elongase systems; also a membrane elongase complex in fungi such as Magnaporthe oryzae.
reactions.rationale: Same system as rxn01591 but with the physiological NADPH cofactor. EC 2.3.1.119 was deleted and split into EC 2.3.1.199, 1.1.1.330, 4.2.1.134 and 1.3.1.93, i.e. four separate monofunctional proteins forming a membrane complex, which the protocol treats as a complex rather than a fused bi/polyfunctional enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylative condensation plus two NADPH-dependent reductions make the elongation cycle irreversible toward icosanoyl-CoA ('>'); there is no enzyme that reverses it (beta-oxidation is a separate pathway with different chemistry), so ModelSEED's '<' is not enzymatically supported.

reactions.name: N-Formimino-L-glutamate formiminohydrolase
pathways: MetaCyc: Amino-Acid-Degradation (Amino Acid Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); HISDEG-PWY (L-histidine degradation I); HISTIDINE-DEG (L-histidine Degradation); Proteinogenic-Amino-Acids-Degradation (Proteinogenic Amino Acid Degradation)
KEGG: rn00340 (Histidine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Formimidoylglutamase (formiminoglutamase, HutG)
reactions.organism_context: Trypanosoma cruzi formiminoglutamase (structurally characterised); bacterial HutG in the Bacillus/Pseudomonas histidine utilisation (hut) operons.
reactions.rationale: Formiminoglutamase is an arginase-like binuclear manganese metalloenzyme of the ureohydrolase superfamily with a single active site and one activity, hydrolysis of the formimidoyl amide of N-formimino-L-glutamate. It is a standalone protein in the hut operon, not fused to the other histidine-degradation enzymes.

direction_conflict.note: Amide hydrolysis releasing formamide is irreversible and HutG is a purely catabolic step of histidine degradation, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the enzymatic one; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing glutamate with formamide.

reactions.name: 5-Formiminotetrahydrofolate ammonia-lyase (cyclizing)
pathways: MetaCyc: Amino-Acid-Degradation (Amino Acid Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); Energy-Metabolism (Generation of Precursor Metabolite and Energy); Fermentation (); HISTIDINE-DEG (L-histidine Degradation); NUCLEO-DEG (Nucleoside and Nucleotide Degradation); P164-PWY (purine nucleobases degradation I (anaerobic)); PWY-5030 (L-histidine degradation III); PWY-5497 (purine nucleobases degradation II (anaerobic)); Proteinogenic-Amino-Acids-Degradation (Proteinogenic Amino Acid Degradation); Purine-Degradation (Purine Nucleotide Degradation)
KEGG: rn00670 (One carbon pool by folate)
reactions.enzyme_name: Formimidoyltetrahydrofolate cyclodeaminase domain of formiminotransferase-cyclodeaminase (FTCD)
reactions.organism_context: Fused as one polypeptide in vertebrates (pig and human liver FTCD, a circular Golgi-associated homo-octamer). In Clostridium cylindrosporum the two activities sit on separate proteins, so the fusion is lineage-specific.
reactions.rationale: FTCD is a single ~58 kDa chain carrying two genuinely distinct catalytic activities on two separable domains: an N-terminal glutamate formimidoyltransferase (EC 2.1.2.5) and a C-terminal formimidoyltetrahydrofolate cyclodeaminase (EC 4.3.1.4); the isolated domains fold and dimerise independently, and the crystal structure of the bifunctional octamer shows both active sites. This reaction is run by the cyclodeaminase domain.

direction_conflict.note: This is exactly the bifunctional-architecture case the protocol flags: the two domains are arranged around a circular octamer so that 5-formimino-THF made by the transferase domain is channelled directly into the cyclodeaminase domain, which drives flux unidirectionally to 5,10-methenyl-THF + NH3 ('>'); the reverse (ammonia addition across methenyl-THF) does not occur in vivo, so ModelSEED's '<' conflicts with the channelling architecture.

reactions.name: 3'-phosphoadenylyl sulfate:2-aminoacrylate C-sulfotransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified (KEGG flags R08699 as an incomplete reaction with an unidentified donor; no EC number and no KO are assigned)
reactions.organism_context: The characterised biological route to L-cysteate is cysteate synthase acting on O-phospho-L-serine plus sulfite in methanogens, not a PAPS-dependent C-sulfotransferase.
reactions.rationale: KEGG itself annotates R08699 as an incomplete reaction with an unidentified donor and assigns it neither an EC number nor an orthology group, and literature searching turned up no PAPS:2-aminoacrylate C-sulfotransferase. No catalysing protein exists to classify.

direction_conflict.note: With the donor step explicitly unidentified in KEGG, neither direction has enzymological support; the real cysteate-forming chemistry uses a different donor (sulfite) and a different enzyme, so this reaction should probably not be carrying a direction constraint at all.

reactions.name: Quercitrin 3-L-rhamnohydrolase
reactions.enzyme_name: Quercitrinase (alpha-L-rhamnosidase acting on quercetin 3-O-alpha-L-rhamnoside)
reactions.organism_context: Classically a secreted fungal activity (Aspergillus flavus); the modern molecular equivalents are GH78/GH106 alpha-L-rhamnosidases from fungi (Alternaria), bacteria (Novosphingobium RHA-P) and gut Bifidobacterium/Bacteroides.
reactions.rationale: No gene has ever been cloned under the name 'quercitrinase'; the activity is carried by alpha-L-rhamnosidases, which are single-catalytic-domain glycoside hydrolases with one activity (several carry additional non-catalytic carbohydrate-binding or beta-sandwich domains, which do not count). Confidence is low because the enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry and from rhamnosidase literature rather than from a paper on this exact reaction.

direction_conflict.note: Glycoside hydrolysis in bulk water is effectively irreversible, so the aglycone-releasing direction ('>') is the only one a hydrolase runs; ModelSEED's '<' would require a transglycosylation/synthase reaction these enzymes do not perform at physiological rhamnose concentrations.

reactions.name: Glutaryl-CoA:(acceptor) 2,3-oxidoreductase (decarboxylating)
reactions.reaction: (1) FAD[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) Glutaryl-CoA[0] <=> (1) CO2[0] + (1) Crotonyl-CoA[0] + (1) FADH2[0]
pathways: KEGG: rn00071 (Fatty acid degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: Glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GCDH)
distinct_activities: acyl-CoA dehydrogenation of glutaryl-CoA to glutaconyl-CoA (EC 1.3.8.6)
decarboxylation of the glutaconyl-CoA intermediate to crotonyl-CoA + CO2
reactions.organism_context: Human mitochondrial GCDH (homotetramer of one polypeptide); bacterial decarboxylating GCDHs. Non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenases, which perform only the dehydrogenation, exist in anaerobic aromatic degraders such as Desulfococcus multivorans.
reactions.rationale: One polypeptide performs two chemically distinct catalytic steps, FAD-dependent alpha,beta-dehydrogenation and then decarboxylation of the glutaconyl-CoA intermediate; the crystal structures are explicitly described as giving the 'structural bases of dehydrogenation and decarboxylation reactions', and a decarboxylating GCDH can be converted into a non-decarboxylating one by site-directed mutagenesis, showing the two activities are separable. Caveat behind the medium confidence: both steps occur in a single active site within one catalytic cycle rather than on two fused domains, so a stricter reading would score this monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The decarboxylation half of the bifunctionality is what makes the overall reaction irreversible: loss of CO2 pulls it to crotonyl-CoA ('>'), and no enzyme carboxylates crotonyl-CoA back to glutaryl-CoA, so ModelSEED's '<' is not enzymatically achievable.

reactions.name: 2-phenylacetamide amidohydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism); rn00643 (Styrene degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: Amidase (amidase-signature family wide-spectrum amidase hydrolysing 2-phenylacetamide; e.g. Pseudomonas aeruginosa AmiE-type and Rhodococcus amidases)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa amidase (the acetanilide/phenylacetamide-utilising system) and Rhodococcus erythropolis amidases; amidase-signature (AS) superfamily, which is also widespread in plants.
reactions.rationale: These are single-domain Ser-cisSer-Lys amidase-signature hydrolases with one catalytic activity, hydrolysis of the amide C-N bond. The acyl-transfer side reaction (transfer to hydroxylamine giving hydroxamates) proceeds through the same acyl-enzyme intermediate with a different acceptor nucleophile and is therefore not a second catalytic activity. Medium confidence because ModelSEED names only a generic 'probable amidase' rather than one characterised protein.

direction_conflict.note: Amide hydrolysis to the carboxylate plus ammonia is irreversible in water, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the one the enzyme runs; the reverse amide synthesis requires non-physiological ammonia levels and proceeds by acyl transfer, not by reversal.

reactions.name: CTP:choline-phosphate cytidylyltransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00440 (Phosphonate and phosphinate metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified cytidylyltransferase for 2-trimethylaminoethylphosphonate (ModelSEED assigns EC 2.7.7.15, choline-phosphate cytidylyltransferase, but the substrate here is a C-P phosphonate, not choline phosphate)
reactions.organism_context: Phosphonolipid-producing bacteria and protists; bacterial phosphonate pathways are known to use dedicated CTP/other nucleotidyltransferases to activate phosphonates.
reactions.rationale: No protein has been shown to make CMP-2-trimethylaminoethylphosphonate; the EC 2.7.7.15 assignment is a chemistry-based transfer from choline-phosphate cytidylyltransferase, whose real substrate this is not. The nominal EC 2.7.7.15 enzyme (CCT/Pcyt1) is itself a monofunctional nucleotidyltransferase whose extra amphipathic-helix membrane-binding segment is regulatory, not catalytic, but that does not establish the catalyst of this reaction.

direction_conflict.note: All CTP-dependent cytidylyltransferases are pulled forward in vivo by pyrophosphatase hydrolysis of the released PPi, so the CMP-adduct-forming direction ('>') is the physiological one even though the isolated nucleotidyl transfer is near-equilibrium.

reactions.name: Coniferin beta-D-glucosidase
pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); LIGNIN-SYN (Lignin Biosynthesis); PHENYLPROPANOID-DERIVATIVE-DEG (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Degradation); PHENYLPROPANOID-SYN (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Biosynthesis); PWY-116 (coniferin metabolism); Phenolic-Compounds-Degradation (Phenolic Compound Degradation); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-DEGRADATION (Secondary Metabolite Degradation)
KEGG: rn00940 (Phenylpropanoid biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: Coniferin beta-glucosidase (CBG)
reactions.organism_context: Pinus contorta (lodgepole pine) xylem CBG, cloned and heterologously expressed; Arabidopsis BGLU45/BGLU46 hydrolyse monolignol glucosides; also characterised in Picea and Pinus sylvestris xylem.
reactions.rationale: Coniferin beta-glucosidase is a family GH1 retaining beta-glucosidase, a single (beta/alpha)8-barrel catalytic domain with one activity, hydrolysis of the beta-glucosidic bond of coniferin to release coniferyl alcohol. No second catalytic activity is described.

direction_conflict.note: GH1 glucoside hydrolysis is irreversible under cellular water activity and the physiological role is to release coniferyl alcohol for lignification, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

reactions.name: 3'-Phosphoadenylylsulfate:quercetin-3-sulfate 3'-sulfotransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: FLAVONOID-SYN (Flavonoid Biosynthesis); FLAVONOL-SYN (Flavonol Biosynthesis); PHENYLPROPANOID-SYN (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Biosynthesis); PWY-6199 (quercetin sulfate biosynthesis); PWY-6266 (superpathway of flavones and derivatives biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00944 (Flavone and flavonol biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: Flavonol 3'-sulfotransferase (quercetin-3-sulfate 3'-sulfotransferase)
reactions.organism_context: Flaveria chloraefolia and Flaveria bidentis; one of a set of position-specific plant cytosolic flavonol sulfotransferases (3-ST, 3'-ST, 4'-ST) that act sequentially.
reactions.rationale: The Flaveria flavonol sulfotransferases were purified and cloned as separate, strictly position-specific single-domain cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases; the 3'-ST carries one catalytic activity and acts only on quercetin 3-sulfate. Medium confidence because the published purification and mutagenesis work focuses on the 3-sulfotransferase, with the 3'-enzyme characterised as a distinct member of the same monofunctional family.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation runs irreversibly in the sulfo-transfer direction (PAPS consumed to PAP) and these plant STs act in an obligate 3- then 3'- sequence, so the bissulfate-forming direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

reactions.name: isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase
pathways: MetaCyc: Amino-Acid-Degradation (Amino Acid Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); Proteinogenic-Amino-Acids-Degradation (Proteinogenic Amino Acid Degradation); VALDEG-PWY (L-valine degradation I); VALINE-DEG (L-valine Degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACAD8)
reactions.organism_context: Human mitochondrial ACAD8 (homotetramer), the valine-degradation acyl-CoA dehydrogenase; plant/Arabidopsis homologue in branched-chain amino acid catabolism.
reactions.rationale: ACAD8 is a classical homotetrameric FAD acyl-CoA dehydrogenase: one subunit type, one active site, one activity (alpha,beta-dehydrogenation of isobutyryl-CoA to methacrylyl-CoA). Its documented substrate promiscuity across short branched-chain acyl-CoAs is specificity breadth, not a second catalytic activity, and unlike GCDH it does not decarboxylate.

direction_conflict.note: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases hand electrons to ETF rather than to free FAD, and ETF/ETF-QO coupling pulls the reaction irreversibly toward the enoyl-CoA ('>'); the near-zero free energy that the free-FAD/FADH2 couple in this written equation implies is an artefact of the cofactor representation, which plausibly explains why ModelSEED lands on '<'.

reactions.name: R02721
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme; KEGG annotates R02721 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC and no KO. The real route to the thiamine thiazole goes via DXP synthase (pyruvate + G3P -> 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate) and then thiazole synthase ThiG with ThiH/ThiO and ThiS-thiocarboxylate (bacteria) or THI4 (yeast/plants).
reactions.organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli/Bacillus ThiGHS or ThiGOS) and fungi/plants (suicide enzyme THI4).
reactions.rationale: KEGG explicitly flags R02721 as unclear and gives it no enzyme, orthology or pathway link, and the reaction as written lumps at least two committed steps carried out by unrelated proteins, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.

direction_conflict.note: The real thiazole-forming steps (ThiGH, or the suicide enzyme THI4, which is consumed in a single turnover) are strictly irreversible biosynthetic reactions, consistent with '>' as written, but no single catalyst exists to justify a direction constraint on this lumped reaction.

reactions.name: R02895
pathways: KEGG: rn00330 (Arginine and proline metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unknown (no characterised linatine synthase)
reactions.organism_context: Linum usitatissimum (flaxseed) is the source of linatine, a gamma-glutamyl-1-amino-D-proline vitamin B6 antagonist
reactions.rationale: No enzyme has been assigned to this condensation; KEGG itself annotates R02895 as 'unclear reaction / incomplete reaction' (no water or cofactor balance), and literature searches return no linatine biosynthetic enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: The reaction as encoded is not a real elementary step (D-proline + Gln -> linatine with only protons released), so neither direction call rests on enzymology; the disagreement is an artefact of an incomplete KEGG stub.

reactions.name: R02979
reactions.enzyme_name: sphingolipid C4-hydroxylase/Delta4-desaturase (DES2/DEGS2); paralogue DES1/DEGS1 is desaturase-only

reactions.rationale: PGA has one catalytic activity, hydrolysis of the phenylacetyl amide bond of penicillin G; the alpha/beta heterodimer arises by Ntn-hydrolase autoproteolytic self-maturation of one precursor chain, which is self-processing rather than a second metabolic activity, and a circularly permuted single-chain variant is fully active.

direction_conflict.note: The equilibrium lies far toward hydrolysis (penicillin G + H2O -> phenylacetate + 6-APA, left-to-right as written); industrial penicillin synthesis with PGA is kinetically controlled from activated acyl donors (esters/amides), not thermodynamic reversal, so ModelSEED's '<' does not correspond to how the enzyme works.

reactions.organism_context: Rattus norvegicus liver cytosol; expressed as a single recombinant polypeptide
reactions.rationale: AST IV was purified from rat liver cytosol and bacterially expressed as one polypeptide with a single activity, PAPS-dependent O-sulfonation of phenolic and tyrosine-ester acceptors; its reaction-product self-inactivation by N-hydroxy-2-acetylaminofluorene sulfate is enzyme inactivation, not a second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and effectively irreversible toward the sulfated product (PAPS + L-tyrosine methyl ester -> PAP + the 4-sulfate, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' reverses a committed transfer step; the LLM's '>' matches the enzymology.
