reactions.organism_context: Synechocystis PCC6803 ChlM; Rhodobacter capsulatus BchM; Arabidopsis and rice CHLM
reactions.rationale: ChlM is a small class-I (seven-stranded beta-sheet) SAM-dependent methyltransferase with one activity, methyl esterification of the C13 propionate of Mg-protoporphyrin IX; its physical association with Mg-chelatase subunits is a protein-protein interaction and its role in plastid-to-nucleus signalling is regulatory moonlighting, neither of which counts as a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible in the methylation direction (SAM + Mg-proto IX -> SAH + Mg-proto IX monomethyl ester, left-to-right as written) and commits the porphyrin to the chlorophyll branch, so ModelSEED's '<' is not physiological.

reactions.name: R04252
pathways: KEGG: rn00440 (Phosphonate and phosphinate metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unassigned (KEGG R04252 is explicitly flagged 'incomplete reaction')
reactions.rationale: KEGG R04252 (2-aminoethylphosphonate/ciliatine <=> ciliatocholate) carries no EC number, no KO and no enzyme assignment and is annotated 'incomplete reaction'; ciliatocholate is the 2-aminoethylphosphonate conjugate of cholic acid first described in bovine bile, so the real chemistry is bile-acid (de)conjugation, but no protein has ever been assigned to it.

direction_conflict.note: As written the reaction is mass-unbalanced (the cholate moiety is simply dropped), so both the thermodynamic estimates and the direction calls are meaningless; read as bile-acid deconjugation, hydrolysis releasing free ciliatine would be the favoured direction, which is ModelSEED's '<' rather than the LLM's '>'.

reactions.name: 3-Hydroxy-3-(4-methylpent-3-en-1-yl)-glutaryl-CoA-lyase
reactions.enzyme_name: beta-Hydroxy-beta-isohexenylglutaryl-CoA lyase (3-hydroxy-3-(4-methylpent-3-en-1-yl)glutaryl-CoA:acetate lyase)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas, acyclic terpene (citronellol/geraniol) degradation
reactions.rationale: Seubert and Fass purified this lyase from Pseudomonas separately from the preceding beta-isohexenylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase, showing the hydratase and lyase steps sit on distinct proteins rather than a fused bifunctional chain; only the acetate-releasing retro-aldol activity was found on the lyase. The protein has not been cloned, hence medium rather than high confidence.

direction_conflict.note: In citronellol/geraniol catabolism this lyase runs in the cleavage direction (3-hydroxy-3-isohexenylglutaryl-CoA -> acetate + 7-methyl-3-oxooctanoyl-CoA, left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would require a C-C condensation that the degradative pathway never performs, so the LLM's '>' is correct.

reactions.name: citrate:N6-acetyl-N6-hydroxy-L-lysine ligase (ADP-forming)
reactions.reaction: (2) H2O[0] + (4) ATP[0] + (1) Citrate[0] + (2) N6-Acetyl-N6-hydroxylysine[0] <= (4) ADP[0] + (1) Aerobactin[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Aerobactin synthetases IucA and IucC (NIS synthetases)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae iuc operon
reactions.rationale: The lumped EC 6.3.2.27 'aerobactin synthase' reaction is not one enzyme: two separate NRPS-independent siderophore (NIS) synthetases, IucA and IucC, sequentially couple N6-acetyl-N6-hydroxylysine to the two carboxylates of citrate, each a distinct polypeptide performing one ATP-dependent adenylation/amidation; neither carries a second fused activity.

direction_conflict.note: Each condensation is driven by ATP cleavage and is irreversible toward aerobactin (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would amount to regenerating 4 ATP by hydrolysing the siderophore, which is thermodynamically impossible, so the LLM's '>' is correct.

reactions.name: S-Adenosyl-L-methionine:zymosterol C-methyltransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: ERGOSTEROL-SYN-PWY (superpathway of ergosterol biosynthesis I); Ergosterol-Biosynthesis (Ergosterol Biosynthesis); Lipid-Biosynthesis (Fatty Acid and Lipid Biosynthesis); PWY-6075 (ergosterol biosynthesis I); Sterol-Biosynthesis (Sterol Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00100 (Steroid biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: Sterol 24-C-methyltransferase (Erg6p / SMT1)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Candida Erg6p; plant, Mucor and protist SMT orthologues
reactions.rationale: Erg6p is a single-domain SAM-dependent C-methyltransferase whose only activity is C-24 methylation of zymosterol to fecosterol; organisms that need more than one SMT activity duplicate the gene (e.g. the multiple SMTs of Mucor lusitanicus) rather than fusing extra catalytic domains.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-alkylation via a high-energy carbocation intermediate is irreversible toward the methylated sterol (zymosterol -> fecosterol, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' is not an enzymatically accessible direction.

reactions.name: 3'-Phosphoadenylylsulfate:UDP-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine-4-sulfate 6-sulfotransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfate 6-O-sulfotransferase (microsomal avian oviduct activity; protein never purified or cloned)
reactions.organism_context: Quail/hen oviduct tubular gland microsomes
reactions.rationale: The only characterisation of EC 2.8.2.7 is a microsomal 'sulfotransferase-sulfatase' multienzyme system in quail oviduct, in which a PAPS-dependent 6-O-sulfotransferase makes UDP-GalNAc 4,6-bissulfate and a physically separate 4-sulfatase then removes the 4-sulfate; the sulfotransferase itself was never purified, so its domain organisation and even its identity are unknown.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation is essentially irreversible toward the sulfated sugar nucleotide (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would regenerate PAPS from a sulfate ester, which no sulfotransferase does, so the LLM's '>' is the defensible call even though the protein is unidentified.

reactions.name: 2-Hydroxy-2-hydropyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate lyase (decyclizing)
pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); P184-PWY (protocatechuate degradation I (meta-cleavage pathway)); PWY-6338 (superpathway of vanillin and vanillate degradation); Protocatechuate-Degradation (Protocatechuate Degradation); Vanillin-Degradation (Vanillin Degradation)
KEGG: rn00362 (Benzoate degradation); rn00627 (Aminobenzoate degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: none - spontaneous ring-chain (hemiketal) tautomerisation; the EC 5.5.1.1 tag in ModelSEED is a mis-assignment
reactions.organism_context: Protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage (meta) pathway of Sphingomonas/Pseudomonas
reactions.rationale: KEGG R04489 carries no EC and no KO and is annotated 'tautomeric equilibrium': the interconversion of 4-carboxy-2-hydroxymuconate-6-semialdehyde with its intramolecular hemiketal (2-hydroxy-2-hydropyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate) is spontaneous, and the enzymatic step in this pathway is the downstream LigC dehydrogenase acting on the cyclic form. EC 5.5.1.1 is muconate cycloisomerase and does not belong to this chemistry.

direction_conflict.note: The equilibrium lies on the cyclic hemiketal side and pathway flux runs semialdehyde -> hemiketal -> (LigC) 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate, i.e. right-to-left as the ModelSEED equation is written; here ModelSEED's '<' is the correct direction and the LLM's '>' is not, consistent with eQuilibrator's +21 kJ/mol for the left-to-right (decyclizing) sense.

reactions.name: ATP:4-amino-2-methyl-5-phosphomethylpyrimidine phosphotransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: Cofactor-Biosynthesis (Cofactor, Prosthetic Group, Electron Carrier, and Vitamin Biosynthesis); HMP-PP-Biosynthesis (4-amino-2-methyl-5-diphosphomethylpyrimidine biosynthesis); PWY-6890 (4-amino-2-methyl-5-diphosphomethylpyrimidine biosynthesis); PWY-6895 (superpathway of thiamine diphosphate biosynthesis II); PWY-6897 (thiamine salvage II); PWY-6910 (hydroxymethylpyrimidine salvage); PWY-7282 (4-amino-2-methyl-5-diphosphomethylpyrimidine biosynthesis (yeast)); PWY-7356 (thiamine salvage IV (yeast)); PWY-7357 (thiamine formation from pyrithiamine and oxythiamine (yeast)); THISYN-PWY (superpathway of thiamine diphosphate biosynthesis I); THISYNARA-PWY (superpathway of thiamine diphosphate biosynthesis III (eukaryotes)); Thiamin-Salvage (Thiamine Salvage); Thiamine-Biosynthesis (Thiamine Biosynthesis); Vitamin-Biosynthesis (Vitamin Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00730 (Thiamine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Hydroxymethylpyrimidine kinase / phosphomethylpyrimidine kinase (ThiD, thiDIJ)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli ThiD, a single gene that complements both thiJ and thiD mutations; the yeast orthologues THI20/THI21 add a third, TenA-type aminopyrimidine aminohydrolase (thiaminase II) activity and are effectively polyfunctional
reactions.rationale: A single purified E. coli ThiD polypeptide converts HMP to its monophosphate and the monophosphate to its pyrophosphate, so two distinct kinase activities sit on one chain; in Saccharomyces the same protein family carries an additional hydrolase domain.

direction_conflict.note: This ATP-dependent second phosphorylation is the committed step supplying HMP-PP to thiamine phosphate synthase, and the enzyme's other (HMP kinase) activity pushes flux the same way, so the biosynthetic/salvage direction is left-to-right as written and ModelSEED's '<' reverses it; the bifunctionality here reinforces rather than explains the conflict.

reactions.name: R04547
reactions.enzyme_name: Branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase (di/trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase, ACOX2)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and kidney peroxisomes (rat has a distinct trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase alongside pristanoyl-CoA oxidase)
reactions.rationale: The human peroxisomal branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase was purified to near homogeneity as a single ~70 kDa monomeric protein with one activity, FAD-dependent alpha,beta-desaturation, acting on both 3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy- and 3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoyl-CoA; the following hydratase and dehydrogenase steps live on a separate multifunctional protein (MFP-2), not on the oxidase.

direction_conflict.note: The physiological enzyme is an O2-dependent oxidase that dumps the electrons as H2O2, making the desaturation irreversible left-to-right as written; ModelSEED's FAD/FADH2 formulation hides that irreversibility and its '<' call would reduce the 24-ene back, which peroxisomal bile-acid synthesis never does.

reactions.name: R04592
reactions.enzyme_name: Branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase (trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase, ACOX2)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and kidney peroxisomes; in rat liver a separate trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase performs the same step
reactions.rationale: The same single ~70 kDa monomeric human branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase oxidises 3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoyl-CoA (THCA-CoA) as well as 2-methyl-branched acyl-CoAs; it has one catalytic activity and no fused hydratase/dehydrogenase domains.

direction_conflict.note: As an O2-consuming, H2O2-producing acyl-CoA oxidase the step is irreversible toward the 24-enoyl-CoA (left-to-right as written) on the way to cholic acid; ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of writing the half-reaction with FAD/FADH2 instead of O2/H2O2.

reactions.name: 3,4-Dihydroxy-L-phenylalanine:oxygen 4,5-oxidoreductase (recyclizing)
pathways: KEGG: rn00350 (Tyrosine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Stizolobate synthase (L-DOPA 4,5-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.29) - catalysing protein never isolated
reactions.organism_context: Etiolated Stizolobium hassjoo (Mucuna) seedlings
reactions.rationale: The only enzymology is a crude, oxygen-labile ammonium-sulfate fraction from Stizolobium hassjoo seedlings that converts L-DOPA to stizolobic acid in the presence of O2 and NAD(P)+; Saito and Komamine themselves speak of 'an enzyme system(s)', KEGG notes R04598 is 'possibly a two-step reaction', and no protein has been purified or cloned, so mono- versus bifunctionality cannot be judged.

direction_conflict.note: The biosynthesis requires NAD(P)+ as oxidant, i.e. the ring-opened muconate semialdehyde + NAD+ -> stizolobate + NADH (left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' runs the plant biosynthetic step backwards and the LLM's '>' matches the only experimental evidence.

reactions.name: 3,4-Dihydroxy-L-phenylalanine:oxygen 2,3-oxidoreductase (recyclizing)
pathways: KEGG: rn00350 (Tyrosine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Stizolobinate synthase (L-DOPA 2,3-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.30) - catalysing protein never isolated
reactions.organism_context: Etiolated Stizolobium hassjoo (Mucuna) seedlings
reactions.rationale: Same crude preparation as for stizolobic acid: a single partially purified, oxygen-labile Stizolobium hassjoo fraction makes both stizolobinic and stizolobic acid from L-DOPA with O2 and NAD(P)+, and it was never resolved into individual proteins, so whether one, two or more polypeptides are involved is unresolved.

direction_conflict.note: NAD(P)+ is the oxidant in the demonstrated biosynthesis (semialdehyde + NAD+ -> stizolobinate + NADH, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' reverses the only direction the cell-free system was shown to run.

reactions.name: 2-Amino-4-hydroxy-6-(erythro-1,2,3-trihydroxypropyl) dihydropteridine triphosphate hydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00790 (Folate biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: GTP cyclohydrolase I (FolE / GCH1)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli FolE homodecamer; human GCH1 (folate and tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthesis)
reactions.rationale: This ModelSEED entry is the final cyclization partial-step of GTP cyclohydrolase I; the E. coli enzyme is a homodecamer whose single active site, formed at subunit interfaces, carries out the whole GTP -> dihydroneopterin triphosphate conversion (imidazole ring opening, formate release, Amadori rearrangement, pterin ring closure) as one catalytic activity, not several fused ones. A literature search for a bifunctional GTP cyclohydrolase I returned nothing.

direction_conflict.note: Folate/pterin biosynthetic flux runs from the open formamidopyrimidine intermediate to 7,8-dihydroneopterin 3'-triphosphate with loss of water, i.e. right-to-left as this equation is written; here ModelSEED's '<' agrees with the enzyme and the LLM's '>' (hydrolytic re-opening of the pterin ring) does not.

reactions.name: rxn03189
reactions.enzyme_name: none - a lumped multi-enzyme sterol C-4 demethylation plus Delta24 reduction, not a single enzyme
reactions.organism_context: Fungal (ERG25/ERG26/ERG27/ERG4) and mammalian (SC4MOL/MSMO1, NSDHL, HSD17B7, DHCR24) post-squalene sterol pathways
reactions.rationale: No single protein converts 14-demethyllanosterol to 4alpha-methylcholest-8-en-3beta-ol: removing one C-4 methyl requires the three sequential, separately encoded C-4 demethylation enzymes (sterol C4-methyl oxidase, C-3 sterol dehydrogenase/C-4 decarboxylase, 3-ketosteroid reductase) and the Delta24 bond must additionally be reduced by a sterol Delta24-reductase; the entry is also not mass-balanced as written (a carbon is lost with no CO2 product).

direction_conflict.note: Sterol biosynthesis runs in the demethylating sense (14-demethyllanosterol -> 4alpha-methyl sterol, left-to-right as written) and every component step is irreversible (O2- and NAD(P)H-consuming, CO2-releasing), so ModelSEED's '<' is unachievable; but because the entry lumps several enzymes and is unbalanced, no direction call on it is really meaningful.

reactions.name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine:(S)-coclaurine-N-methyltransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00950 (Isoquinoline alkaloid biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Coclaurine N-methyltransferase (CNMT)
reactions.organism_context: Coptis japonica, Papaver somniferum, Thalictrum flavum (benzylisoquinoline alkaloid biosynthesis)
reactions.rationale: The CNMT crystal structure shows a single class-I SAM-binding methyltransferase domain with one active site that N-methylates (S)-coclaurine and related 1-benzyltetrahydroisoquinolines; its broad substrate scope is promiscuity at that one site, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-to-SAH N-methylation is effectively irreversible toward (S)-N-methylcoclaurine (left-to-right as written) and is a committed step toward reticuline, so ModelSEED's '<' is not an enzymatic direction.

reactions.name: S-Adenosyl-L-methionine:(RS)-1-benzyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinolie N- methyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: (RS)-1-Benzyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline N-methyltransferase (the CNMT-type benzylisoquinoline alkaloid N-methyltransferase)
reactions.organism_context: Coptis japonica / Papaver somniferum CNMT and its paralogues; EC 2.1.1.115 activity measured on generic 1-benzyl-THIQ substrates
reactions.rationale: EC 2.1.1.115 on an unspecified 1-benzyltetrahydroisoquinoline is the same CNMT-family class-I SAM methyltransferase characterised structurally for coclaurine, a single-domain enzyme with one N-methylation activity and broad acceptor tolerance; medium confidence because the ModelSEED substrate is generic rather than a named natural product.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible toward the N-methylated alkaloid (left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' does not correspond to any methyltransferase chemistry.

reactions.name: Hexanoyl-CoA:(acceptor) 2,3-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00071 (Fatty acid degradation); rn01212 (Fatty acid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD, ACADM)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria (pig/human MCAD homotetramer); hexanoyl-CoA is a core MCAD substrate, with short-chain ACADS overlapping at C6
reactions.rationale: MCAD is a homotetrameric FAD enzyme whose crystal structures show one catalytic site per identical subunit performing a single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation; the electron-transfer flavoprotein that reoxidises it is a separate protein, which the protocol's complex exclusion keeps out of the bifunctional category.

direction_conflict.note: beta-Oxidation dehydrogenation is pulled by ETF/ETF-QO and runs only toward the 2-enoyl-CoA (hexanoyl-CoA -> (2E)-hexenoyl-CoA, left-to-right as written); the reverse reduction is done by a different enzyme (trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase in fatty-acid elongation), so ModelSEED's '<' misassigns the chemistry.

reactions.name: Decanoyl-CoA:(acceptor) 2,3-oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00071 (Fatty acid degradation); rn01212 (Fatty acid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD, ACADM; long-chain ACADL/ACADVL overlap at C10)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria; decanoyl-CoA sits at the MCAD/LCAD chain-length boundary
reactions.rationale: Decanoyl-CoA dehydrogenation is carried out by homotetrameric ACAD-family flavoenzymes (MCAD, with LCAD/VLCAD overlapping at C10), each a single-activity dehydrogenase with one catalytic site per subunit and no fused second domain.

direction_conflict.note: As with all ACADs the step is drained to ETF and is physiologically unidirectional toward (2E)-decenoyl-CoA (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would be an enoyl-CoA reductase activity that this enzyme does not have.

reactions.name: Selenomethionine methanethiol-lyase (deaminating)
pathways: KEGG: rn00450 (Selenocompound metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: L-Methionine gamma-lyase (methioninase, MGL); the co-listed EC 4.4.1.1 points instead to cystathionine gamma-lyase
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas putida and Trichomonas vaginalis MGL; in mouse liver the alpha,gamma-elimination of selenomethionine is attributed to cystathionine gamma-lyase
reactions.rationale: MGL is a homotetrameric PLP enzyme with one active site; its alpha,gamma-elimination, gamma-replacement and beta-elimination/replacement reactions are all variants of the same PLP chemistry at that single site, i.e. catalytic promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains. The same applies to cystathionine gamma-lyase.

direction_conflict.note: Selenomethionine is an even better alpha,gamma-elimination substrate than methionine and the products include volatile methaneselenol, making the reaction effectively irreversible left-to-right as written; MGL's gamma-replacement chemistry can insert selenols into homocysteine derivatives but does not reassemble selenomethionine from 2-oxobutyrate + NH3, so ModelSEED's '<' has no enzymatic basis.

reactions.name: R04877
pathways: KEGG: rn00340 (Histidine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Ergothionase (ergothioneine trimethylamine-lyase)
reactions.organism_context: Burkholderia sp. HME13 and other ergothioneine-utilising bacteria, including human gut anaerobes; homotetramer of identical 55 kDa subunits, distantly related to histidine/phenylalanine ammonia-lyase
reactions.rationale: KEGG R04877 is annotated 'ergothionase'; the purified Burkholderia HME13 enzyme is a single-activity C-N lyase that eliminates trimethylamine from ergothioneine and was inactive on D/L-histidine, tyrosine and phenylalanine. No second catalytic activity is reported.

direction_conflict.note: Ergothionase is purely catabolic (ergothioneine is instead synthesised by the unrelated EgtA-EgtE route), so the physiological flux is ergothioneine -> trimethylamine + thiourocanate, i.e. the LLM's '>' rather than ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.name: R04925
pathways: KEGG: rn00440 (Phosphonate and phosphinate metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified 2-(methylamino)ethylphosphonate N-methyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Phosphonolipid-producing eukaryotes (Tetrahymena, molluscs) and bacteria; no protein assigned
reactions.rationale: KEGG flags R04925 as an 'incomplete reaction (methylation)' with no EC number and no ortholog, and literature searches returned no characterised methylaminoethylphosphonate N-methyltransferase; the catalysing protein is simply not known.

direction_conflict.note: The underlying biology is a SAM-dependent N-methylation (monomethyl -> dimethyl aminoethylphosphonate), which is biosynthetically one-way and corresponds to the LLM's '>'; the ModelSEED equation omits SAM/SAH, so its thermodynamic direction call is not meaningful.

reactions.name: R04934
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified selenocysteine Se-alkylation/Se-oxidation activity
reactions.organism_context: Selenium-accumulating plants (Allium, Brassica) by analogy with the sulfur alk(en)ylcysteine sulfoxide pathway; no protein assigned
reactions.rationale: KEGG marks R04934 as an 'incomplete reaction' with no EC, no ortholog and no pathway, and it lumps Se-alkylation plus Se-oxidation into one step; no enzyme catalysing it has been reported.

direction_conflict.note: In Se-accumulating plants the biosynthetic flux runs from selenocysteine toward Se-alkyl-selenocysteine Se-oxides, which favours the LLM's '>', but this is a lumped multi-step stub rather than a reversible single-enzyme reaction.

reactions.name: rxn03399
reactions.enzyme_name: Enterobactin synthetase (EntF non-ribosomal peptide synthetase, acting with EntE and EntB)
distinct_activities: amide-bond condensation of 2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl onto seryl-S-PCP (C domain)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli and other Enterobacteriaceae; EntF is a 142 kDa four-domain (C-A-PCP-TE) single polypeptide
reactions.rationale: The chain that builds enterobactin from the two adenylates is EntF, one 142 kDa polypeptide carrying condensation, adenylation, carrier and thioesterase domains (three genuine catalytic activities plus a carrier). Its partner EntB is separately a fused bifunctional isochorismatase-aryl carrier protein; the overall reaction is run by a three-protein assembly line (EntB/EntE/EntF), not a single enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: NRPS assembly-line chemistry is driven by ATP-derived aminoacyl/aryl-adenylates and terminated by irreversible TE-catalysed trilactonisation, so the step is physiologically unidirectional toward enterobactin ('>'), never back to the adenylates.

reactions.name: beta-D-Glucosyl-2-coumarinate glucohydrolase
pathways: MetaCyc: COUMARIN-SYN (Coumarin Biosynthesis); PHENYLPROPANOID-SYN (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Biosynthesis); PWY-5176 (coumarin biosynthesis (via 2-coumarate)); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00940 (Phenylpropanoid biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: beta-Glucosidase (beta-D-glucosyl-2-coumarinate glucohydrolase, EC 3.2.1.21)

reactions.name: (-)-Isopiperitenone reductase

reactions.name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine:dTDP-4-oxo-2,6-dideoxy-L-mannose 3-C-methyltransferase

direction_conflict.note: Physiologically this is a committed nucleotide-sugar biosynthetic step running toward dTDP-L-megosamine (the LLM council's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' points back up the pathway, and the equation is missing the amino donor and SAM, so the dGP/GC calls are made on an unbalanced reaction.

reactions.name: rxn04319

reactions.name: chalcone and stilbene synthase family protein

reactions.name: R06727

reactions.name: R06742

reactions.name: R06762

reactions.name: R06772

reactions.name: rxn04594

reactions.organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum and related species

reactions.name: R06849

direction_conflict.note: Reductive dechlorination is a respiratory half-reaction driven by an external electron donor and chloride release, so it only ever runs in the dechlorinating (written-forward, TCB->DCB) direction; the ModelSEED equation omits both the electron donor and the chloride product, so the ΔG′° behind the '<' call does not describe the real reaction.

reactions.organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis NMT1/NMT3, spinach, wheat) and nematodes (Haemonchus contortus HcPMT1/HcPMT2, C. elegans) carry two tandem methyltransferase domains on a single ~475-aa chain; Plasmodium falciparum PfPMT is a single-domain enzyme doing all three methylations.

direction_conflict.note: This reaction is the MT2 domain's job and MT2 also performs the third methylation, so flux is pulled from P-MEA straight through to phosphocholine; SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible in vivo, which supports the forward (methylating) direction over ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.name: R06880

reactions.name: R06898

reactions.name: rxn04710

reactions.rationale: CrtM is one squalene-synthase-fold polypeptide that condenses two farnesyl diphosphates head-to-head and rearranges the presqualene-diphosphate intermediate to dehydrosqualene without releasing it, which is a single catalytic activity rather than two. direction_conflict.note: The real reaction is 2 FPP -> dehydrosqualene + 2 PPi and is made irreversible by diphosphate loss; ModelSEED kept only one FPP and no PPi (status MI:C:15/H:22/O:-7/P:-2, CI:2), destroying that driving force and with it the basis for the reverse call.

reactions.enzyme_name: Long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (E. coli FadE; mammalian ACADL/ACADVL)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli fatty-acid beta-oxidation (BiGG ACOAD8f); the same step in mammalian mitochondria is run by ACADL/ACADVL.
reactions.rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases are monofunctional flavoproteins carrying out only the alpha,beta-desaturation; in E. coli the multifunctional partner is FadB (hydratase/3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase/epimerase/isomerase), which catalyses the following steps, not this one. Called from well-established knowledge.

direction_conflict.note: The physiological acceptor is electron-transfer flavoprotein (ETF) feeding the quinone pool, not free FADH2; with ETF/quinone reoxidation the beta-oxidation desaturation is irreversible, so ModelSEED's reverse-only assignment is an artefact of the free-FAD stand-in.

reactions.name: N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine(anhydrous)N-Acetylmuramyl-tripeptide beta -1,4-N-acetylglucosaminidase
reactions.enzyme_name: NagZ, cytoplasmic beta-N-acetylglucosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.52)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Pseudomonas peptidoglycan recycling; NagZ removes GlcNAc from GlcNAc-anhMurNAc-peptides imported by AmpG.
reactions.rationale: NagZ is a single-domain GH3 exo-glycosidase whose only activity is hydrolysis of the beta-1,4 GlcNAc-anhMurNAc bond; its role in AmpC induction is regulatory consequence, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Exo-glycosidase hydrolysis of the recycling intermediate is irreversible; the reverse would require NagZ to act as a glycosyl transferase onto anhydro-MurNAc-tripeptide, which it does not.

reactions.name: L-aspartate oxidase
reactions.enzyme_name: L-Aspartate oxidase, NadB (EC 1.4.3.16)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli de novo NAD biosynthesis; NadB is a soluble FAD flavoprotein homologous to the succinate/fumarate reductase flavoprotein subunit.
reactions.rationale: NadB carries one catalytic activity (oxidation of L-aspartate to iminoaspartate); it uses O2 aerobically and fumarate anaerobically as acceptor, which is substrate versatility rather than a second activity.

direction_conflict.note: The BiGG model substitutes menaquinone-8 for NadB's real acceptors (O2 -> H2O2 aerobically, fumarate anaerobically), so the computed dG does not describe the real couple; in vivo the unstable iminoaspartate is consumed immediately by quinolinate synthase NadA, pulling the reaction forward.

reactions.name: Glycolate oxidase
reactions.enzyme_name: Glycolate oxidase / glycolate dehydrogenase GlcDEF complex (catalytic FAD subunit GlcD)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli glc operon; the membrane-associated glycolate-oxidising activity requires GlcD, GlcE and GlcF together.
reactions.rationale: This is a three-subunit complex of separate polypeptides (GlcD FAD catalytic subunit, GlcE FAD, GlcF Fe-S), not a fused multifunctional chain; per protocol the catalytic subunit GlcD is recorded as monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: Glycolate oxidation is the entry step of glycolate catabolism and is drained forward by glyoxylate consumption (malate synthase GlcB in the same operon); the enzyme has no physiological role reducing glyoxylate with menaquinol.

reactions.name: GTP amine hydrolysis (spontaneous)
reactions.enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (hydrolytic/nitrosative) deamination of GTP to XTP
reactions.organism_context: Nucleotide-pool damage chemistry; the resulting XTP is cleared by house-cleaning ITPases (RdgB/ITPA).
reactions.rationale: ModelSEED/BiGG itself names the entry 'GTP amine hydrolysis (spontaneous)'; no enzyme is known to deaminate GTP, and the existence of dedicated XTP/ITP-hydrolysing house-cleaning enzymes is the standard evidence that XTP arises non-enzymatically from GTP.

direction_conflict.note: Deamination with NH3 loss is chemically one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would have the cell aminate XTP back to GTP, for which there is no chemistry or enzyme.

reactions.name: core oligosaccharide lipid A:hexadecanoate transferase (n-C16:0) (extracellular membrane)
reactions.reaction: (1) H+[0] + (1) Palmitate[0] + (1) core oligosaccharide lipid A[0] <= (1) H2O[0] + (1) hepta-acylated core oligosaccharide lipid A[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: PagP, outer-membrane lipid A palmitoyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.251)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella outer membrane; an eight-stranded beta-barrel enzyme induced by PhoP/PhoQ.
reactions.rationale: PagP has one catalytic activity, palmitoyl transfer to the lipid A 2-acyl position, selected by an internal 'hydrocarbon ruler'; its ability to acylate other acceptors (e.g. phosphatidylglycerol in Klebsiella) is the same chemistry on a different acceptor, not a second activity.

direction_conflict.note: The real acyl donor is a glycerophospholipid (released as lyso-PL), not free palmitate plus loss of water as written; with the activated ester donor restored the acylation is thermodynamically downhill, so the near-zero dG that drove ModelSEED's reverse call is an artefact of the stripped donor.

reactions.name: Lipid A:hexadecanoate transferase (n-C16:0) (extracellular membrane)
reactions.reaction: (3) H+[0] + (1) Palmitate[0] + (1) kdo2-lipid a[0] <= (1) H2O[0] + (1) hepta-acylated KDO(2)-lipid (A)[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: PagP, outer-membrane lipid A palmitoyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.251)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella outer membrane; same enzyme as rxn08789 acting on Kdo2-lipid A.
reactions.rationale: Single-activity beta-barrel acyltransferase; palmitoylation of Kdo2-lipid A to the hepta-acylated species is its canonical reaction.

direction_conflict.note: Same defect as rxn08789 - free palmitate stands in for the glycerophospholipid donor and the lyso-phospholipid co-product is missing, so neither the dG nor the 3-H+ stoichiometry describes the real transfer.

reactions.name: murein D,D-endopeptidase (murein5px4p) (periplasm)
reactions.reaction: (2) H2O[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) two disacharide linked murein units, pentapeptide crosslinked tetrapeptide (A2pm->D-ala) (middle of chain)[0] <= (1) two linked disacharide pentapeptide and tetrapeptide murein units (uncrosslinked, middle of chain)[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Murein D,D-endopeptidase (MepS/Spr, MepM/YebA, MepH, MepA, PBP4/DacB, PBP7/PbpG)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli periplasm; a redundant set of at least six D,D-endopeptidases cleaves the D-Ala-mDAP 4->3 cross-link.
reactions.rationale: The dedicated space-making endopeptidases (MepS, MepM, MepH) are single-catalytic-domain peptidases; PBP4/DacB does show both D,D-carboxypeptidase and D,D-endopeptidase activity, but at one active site as broad specificity, not as two fused domains, so monofunctional is the right call for whichever enzyme runs this reaction.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis of the peptide cross-link is irreversible and is a prerequisite for sacculus expansion; cross-link formation is done by a transpeptidase using the energy of a D-Ala-D-Ala bond, never by running this hydrolase backwards.

reactions.name: murein L,D-endopeptidase (murein3px3p) (periplasm)
reactions.reaction: (2) H2O[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) two disacharide linked murein units, tripeptide crosslinked tripeptide (A2pm->A2pm) (middle of chain)[0] <= (1) two linked disacharide tripeptide murein units (uncrosslinked, middle of chain)[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: MepK, murein L,D-endopeptidase cleaving mDAP-mDAP (3->3) cross-links
reactions.organism_context: E. coli periplasm; MepK is the hydrolase specific for the LD-transpeptidase-made 3->3 cross-links.
reactions.rationale: MepK is a single-domain M15-family metallopeptidase with the one cross-link-cleaving activity; it is the only E. coli enzyme shown to cleave mDAP-mDAP cross-links, and no second catalytic function is reported.

direction_conflict.note: Peptide-bond hydrolysis is irreversible; 3->3 cross-links are re-made by YcbB/LdtD transpeptidation, not by reversing this hydrolase.

reactions.name: Proline dehydrogenase
pathways: KEGG: rn00330 (Arginine and proline metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Proline dehydrogenase domain of proline utilization A (PutA)
reactions.organism_context: Bifunctional/trifunctional PutA in E. coli and other Gram-negatives; the activities are on separate proteins in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (PruB/PruA) and humans (PRODH/ALDH4A1). The extra N-terminal DNA-binding domain of trifunctional PutAs is a regulatory (moonlighting) role, not a third catalytic activity.
reactions.rationale: PutA is a single polypeptide carrying both the FAD-dependent PRODH domain that runs this reaction and an NAD+-dependent P5CDH domain, with a tunnel channelling P5C between them; that is two genuine catalytic activities on one chain.

direction_conflict.note: PutA's FAD is a bound prosthetic group reoxidised by the membrane quinone pool and the P5C product is channelled straight into the P5CDH domain - both pull the PRODH half irreversibly toward P5C, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call (which comes from treating FADH2 as a free, re-usable reductant) is wrong.

reactions.name: quinol monooxygenase (Ubiquinol-8)
reactions.enzyme_name: none - one-electron autoxidation of ubiquinol-8 by O2 (the protein annotated 'quinol monooxygenase', YgiN, catalyses a different reaction)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli respiratory chain ROS leakage; YgiN was characterised as a menadiol-oxidising quinol monooxygenase, not as a superoxide-generating enzyme.
reactions.rationale: As written (quinol + 2 O2 -> quinone + 2 superoxide + 2 H+) nothing is monooxygenated, so this is quinol/semiquinone autoxidation rather than an enzymatic monooxygenase reaction; no protein is known to catalyse it, and the enzyme whose name the model borrowed (YgiN) performs a different, oxygen-incorporating oxidation.

direction_conflict.note: Physiologically the flux is quinol -> quinone + superoxide (ROS leakage kept one-way by SOD removal of O2-); nothing reduces the quinone pool with superoxide, so ModelSEED's '<' is not a real process.

reactions.name: UDP-L-Ara4N formyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: ArnA (PmrI), bifunctional UDP-L-Ara4N formyltransferase / UDP-GlcA oxidative decarboxylase
distinct_activities: UDP-glucuronic acid oxidative decarboxylase / dehydrogenase (C-terminal domain, EC 1.1.1.305)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella Ara4N-lipid A modification pathway conferring polymyxin resistance.
reactions.rationale: ArnA is one polypeptide with two separate catalytic domains - the N-terminal 10-formyl-THF-dependent transformylase that runs this reaction and an independent C-terminal NAD+-dependent UDP-GlcA decarboxylase domain.

direction_conflict.note: Both the formyl acceptor UDP-L-Ara4N and the product UDP-L-Ara4FN have been dropped, leaving only the folate half-reaction; the real transfer consumes 10-formyl-THF (i.e. the forward direction as written) and the stripped equation cannot support any meaningful dG-based direction call.

reactions.name: Aspartate oxidase
reactions.enzyme_name: L-Aspartate oxidase, NadB (EC 1.4.3.16)
reactions.organism_context: De novo NAD biosynthesis; BiGG ASPOcm/U99 variant with the aspartate couple placed in a second compartment.
reactions.rationale: Same single-activity FAD flavoprotein as rxn08167 - it only oxidises L-aspartate to iminoaspartate; the acceptor flexibility (O2 or fumarate) is not a second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: NadB's FAD is a bound prosthetic group reoxidised by O2 (making H2O2) or by fumarate; writing free FAD/FADH2 as a soluble couple removes the driving force, and in vivo the labile iminoaspartate is immediately pulled on by NadA.

reactions.name: a-galactosidase (galactomannan)
reactions.enzyme_name: alpha-Galactosidase (EC 3.2.1.22; GH27/GH36)
reactions.organism_context: Bacterial and fungal mannan-degrading systems; alpha-galactosidase removes alpha-1,6-galactosyl side chains from galactomannan, acting alongside separate beta-mannanase and beta-mannosidase enzymes.
reactions.rationale: GH27/GH36 alpha-galactosidases are single-activity exo-glycosidases; the other mannanolytic activities needed to degrade galactomannan sit on separate proteins, so this is a multi-enzyme system rather than a multifunctional chain.

direction_conflict.note: The debranched polysaccharide co-product is missing - galactomannan is written as being wholly consumed to one galactose - which is where the ~150-370 kJ/mol 'dG' comes from; the actual glycoside hydrolysis is irreversible in the releasing direction.

reactions.name: 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase
reactions.enzyme_name: 6-phospho-beta-glucosidase (GH1 salicin-6-phosphate glucohydrolase)
reactions.organism_context: Bacteria with PTS beta-glucoside systems: E. coli AscB/BglB, Streptococcus pneumoniae BglA-2, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
reactions.rationale: GH1 6-phospho-beta-glucosidases are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 retaining glycosidases with one active site. Reported activity on both phosphorylated and unphosphorylated beta-glucosides is substrate promiscuity at that same site, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis is the only direction a GH1 glycosidase runs in vivo; ModelSEED's '<' would require glucoside synthesis from glucose-6-phosphate plus saligenin, which is a glycosyltransferase reaction, not this enzyme.

reactions.name: Heme D synthase
reactions.enzyme_name: Catalase HPII (hydroperoxidase II) - self-catalysed conversion of its own protoheme IX to cis-heme d
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli; HPII is a clade-2 large monofunctional catalase
reactions.rationale: There is no separate 'heme D synthase': HPII catalase converts its own bound protoheme to cis-heme d as a peroxide-driven self-modification. HPII is explicitly a monofunctional catalase, in contrast to the bifunctional catalase-peroxidases (KatG) that carry both catalase and peroxidase activity.

direction_conflict.note: Oxidative heme b to heme d modification is irreversible, but the written '3 O2 -> 2 H+' has the wrong oxidant (H2O2 in vivo) and does not balance (H 30 vs 36, O 10 vs 6, charge -2 vs +4).

reactions.name: Lumped reaction for synthesis of pime
reactions.reaction: (2) H2O[0] + (1) Pyruvate[0] + (1) Oxaloacetate[0] + (1) H+[0] <= (3) O2[0] + (1) Pimelate[0]
reactions.rationale: A model pseudo-reaction (abbreviation X00002) that collapses pimelate biosynthesis into one entry; no enzyme converts pyruvate plus oxaloacetate into pimelate. The real pimeloyl-thioester route to biotin runs through fatty-acid synthase with malonyl-ACP, BioC/BioH (or BioI), and NADPH.

direction_conflict.note: Mass-balancing forced O2 onto the product side, so the LLM's forward direction would evolve molecular oxygen while ModelSEED's reverse direction is oxidative pimelate breakdown; neither describes the biotin pathway the entry is named for.

reactions.name: fatty acid oxidation (Butanoyl-CoA )
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) NAD[0] + (1) FAD[0] + (1) Butyryl-CoA[0] <= (1) NADH[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) Acetoacetyl-CoA[0] + (1) FADH2[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Butyryl-CoA beta-oxidation: acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE) plus the multifunctional fatty acid oxidation protein FadB
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli FadB, the alpha subunit of the FadBA complex; eukaryotes use the analogous mitochondrial/peroxisomal trifunctional proteins
reactions.rationale: No single enzyme runs this three-step lump: the FAD-dependent step is FadE, a separate acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, while the hydratase and NAD-dependent dehydrogenase steps both sit on the single FadB polypeptide, which carries four catalytic activities on one chain.

direction_conflict.note: Beta-oxidation is the physiological direction; the free FAD/FADH2 pair in the equation also stands in for ETF-coupled electron transfer, which is what actually makes the dehydrogenase step irreversible.

reactions.name: Fatty acid oxidation (n-C16:0)
reactions.enzyme_name: Complete palmitate beta-oxidation spiral: acyl-CoA synthetase (FadD), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE), multifunctional FadB, thiolase FadA
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli FadBA/FadD/FadE; the polyfunctional chain is FadB
reactions.rationale: Seven turns of the beta-oxidation spiral plus CoA activation are collapsed into one entry spanning at least four proteins, so no single enzyme catalyses it; of those, FadB is genuinely polyfunctional with four activities on one polypeptide (FadA thiolase is a separate subunit of the same complex).

direction_conflict.note: Forward is degradative beta-oxidation and is made effectively irreversible by the ATP-to-AMP+PPi activation step and subsequent pyrophosphate hydrolysis; ModelSEED's '<' would mean synthesising palmitate from acetyl-CoA via the degradative enzymes, which is not how fatty acid synthesis works.

reactions.name: Fatty acid oxidation (octadecanoate)
reactions.enzyme_name: Complete octadecanoate beta-oxidation spiral: acyl-CoA synthetase (FadD), acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (FadE), multifunctional FadB, thiolase FadA
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli FadBA/FadD/FadE; the polyfunctional chain is FadB
reactions.rationale: Eight turns of the spiral plus CoA activation lumped into one entry, spanning four proteins, so no single enzyme catalyses it; FadB alone is polyfunctional, carrying hydratase, dehydrogenase, epimerase and isomerase activities on one chain.

direction_conflict.note: The ATP-to-AMP+PPi activation plus pyrophosphatase pull makes the degradative (forward) direction irreversible, so ModelSEED's reverse call is wrong regardless of the group-contribution numbers.

reactions.name: sulfoethylcysteine synthase
reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified NAD(P)H-dependent reductase of 2-(sulfomethyl)thiazolidine-4-carboxylate (proposed coenzyme M biosynthesis step)
reactions.organism_context: Methanogenic archaea (Methanocaldococcus jannaschii, Methanosarcina); hypothetical step
reactions.rationale: The sulfoethylcysteine route to coenzyme M was a proposal and no protein was ever assigned to the thiazolidine-reduction step. White (2019) showed the methanogen enzyme ComF (MJ1681) converts sulfoacetaldehyde directly to 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate, bypassing sulfoethylcysteine entirely.

direction_conflict.note: If the step exists at all it is the reductive, biosynthetic direction toward sulfoethylcysteine (NADH consumed); the ModelSEED '<' has no enzymological support, but neither does the pathway, which is now superseded.

reactions.name: rxn11118
reactions.enzyme_name: Cytoplasmic cystine reductase activity - no single assigned protein (E. coli CydDC; thioredoxin/glutaredoxin systems; flavoprotein cystine reductase EC 1.8.1.6; mammalian TRP14/TXNDC17)
reactions.organism_context: Reaction entry is anonymous (rbs_386) with no EC; candidate systems span bacteria, fungi, plants and mammals
reactions.rationale: Several unrelated proteins reduce cytoplasmic cystine - the heterodimeric CydDC complex in E. coli, TRP14 in mammals, a flavoprotein cystine reductase in yeast/pea/Histoplasma - so the catalysing protein for this entry cannot be pinned down. CydDC would in any case be a two-subunit complex, which the protocol excludes from bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: The reductant (NAD(P)H, thioredoxin or glutathione) is absent - the equation supplies 2 H+ and no electrons - and it is that reductant pool, not the protein, that keeps cytoplasmic cystine reduced to cysteine.

reactions.name: choline ABC transporter permease and substrate binding protein
reactions.enzyme_name: Choline/glycine-betaine ABC importer (substrate-binding protein + permease + ATPase; ChoXWV / OpuB / OpuC / ProU type)
reactions.organism_context: Rhizobium leguminosarum model entry (rll_92); characterised homologues in Sinorhizobium/Rhizobium (ChoXWV), Bacillus subtilis (OpuB/OpuC), Brucella abortus
reactions.rationale: An ABC importer is a multi-subunit complex (binding protein, membrane permease, nucleotide-binding ATPase), which under the protocol's exclusion is not a bifunctional enzyme; the one catalytic activity is ATP hydrolysis on the nucleotide-binding subunit.

direction_conflict.note: The extracellular substrate is written as chorismate (cpd00216) while the cytoplasmic product is choline (cpd00098), so the entry is not a transport of one species at all; ATP-driven import is nonetheless strictly unidirectional in the forward sense.

reactions.name: dihydrodipicolinate reductase
reactions.enzyme_name: Dihydrodipicolinate reductase / 4-hydroxy-tetrahydrodipicolinate reductase (DapB)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus, Sinorhizobium meliloti; homotetramer
reactions.rationale: DapB has a single NAD(P)H-dependent reductase activity; its two structural domains (dinucleotide-binding and substrate-binding) form one active site between them rather than carrying two activities.

direction_conflict.note: DapB's real product is 2,3,4,5-tetrahydrodipicolinate, not delta1-piperideine-6-carboxylate (a lysine-catabolism compound), and the equation loses a carboxyl carbon (C7 to C6); the NADPH-consuming reductive sense it is written in is nevertheless the correct one.

reactions.name: rxn11324
reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified proton-coupled cysteine transporter
reactions.organism_context: Anonymous Rhizobium leguminosarum model entry (rll_530)
reactions.rationale: The entry carries no gene, EC or cross-reference, and bacterial cysteine movement is handled by several unrelated systems (exporters EamA/YdeD, Bcr, YfiK; cystine importers TcyP/TcyJLN; the CydDC complex), none of which is identified here.

direction_conflict.note: A H+-coupled secondary carrier is intrinsically bidirectional - direction is set by the proton-motive force and the cysteine gradient, not by the protein; note also that the extracellular species is ModelSEED's generic/D-cysteine alias (cpd00547, KEGG C00736) while the cytoplasmic one is L-cysteine.

reactions.name: beta-D-glucuronoside glucuronosohydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00944 (Flavone and flavonol biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: beta-glucuronidase (EC 3.2.1.31); KEGG assigns ortholog K01195, the GusA-type GH2 beta-glucuronidase
reactions.organism_context: KEGG rn00944 flavone/flavonol biosynthesis (plant flavone glucuronides, Scutellaria-type); the assigned ortholog is the bacterial GH2 enzyme
reactions.rationale: beta-Glucuronidases are single-active-site retaining glycosidases (GH2, or GH79 in plants); E. coli GusA is a homotetramer of identical one-activity chains and no second catalytic activity is reported.

direction_conflict.note: Glycoside hydrolysis is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would turn the glucuronidase into a glucuronosyltransferase, a different enzyme family that requires UDP-glucuronate rather than free glucuronate.

reactions.name: R08137
pathways: KEGG: rn00981 (Insect hormone biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: 3-dehydroecdysone 3beta-reductase (3DE 3beta-reductase), an NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase; KEGG annotates the step as a 3beta-hydroxysterol dehydrogenase
reactions.organism_context: Insects - Spodoptera littoralis haemolymph enzyme, Bombyx mori; the ecdysteroid 'black box' of the Halloween pathway
reactions.rationale: The 3-oxo to 3beta-ol reduction in the ecdysteroid series is run by 3-dehydroecdysone 3beta-reductase, a single-activity member of the aldo-keto reductase superfamily; the epimeric 3alpha-reduction is done by a different protein (an SDR-family 3alpha-reductase), so the two activities are not fused.

direction_conflict.note: NADPH is replaced by '2 H+', leaving a 2-electron reduction with no electron donor (atoms balance but charge is off by 2); the reductive forward direction is the biosynthetic one toward 2,22,25-trideoxyecdysone.

reactions.name: R04879
pathways: KEGG: rn00340 (Histidine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Presumed N-formylisoglutamine deformylase/amidohydrolase (unassigned)
reactions.organism_context: KEGG histidine metabolism (rn00340), isoglutamine branch; no organism or gene attached
reactions.rationale: KEGG R04879 carries no EC number, no orthology and no enzyme name, and PubMed has no record of a characterised formylisoglutamine deformylase; the isoglutamine branch of histidine degradation rests on old literature with no cloned protein.

direction_conflict.note: Formate, the obligatory second product of deformylation, is absent from both KEGG's and ModelSEED's equation (C6 to C5); read as a formamide hydrolysis, the forward direction is the irreversible one.

reactions.name: R05840
pathways: KEGG: rn00750 (Vitamin B6 metabolism)
reactions.organism_context: KEGG vitamin B6 metabolism (rn00750); no organism attached
reactions.rationale: KEGG R05840 lumps 'glycolaldehyde + 2-oxobutanoate + alanine -> pyridoxine' with no EC and no orthology; it encodes precursor-incorporation results rather than a catalysed step, since the real routes are PdxA/PdxJ (DXP-dependent) or the Pdx1/Pdx2 glutamine amidotransferase complex (DXP-independent).

direction_conflict.note: Net flux in B6 metabolism is toward pyridoxine so the forward sense is right in spirit, but three substrates condensing with a carbon unaccounted for (C9 to C8) means no single enzyme's directionality is being described.

reactions.name: RXN-9309.c
pathways: MetaCyc: C30-Carotenoids-Biosynthesis (C<sub>30</sub> Carotenoid Biosynthesis); CAROTENOID-SYN (Carotenoid Biosynthesis); PWY-5875 (staphyloxanthin biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis); TRITERPENOID-SYN (Triterpenoid Biosynthesis); Terpenoid-Biosynthesis (Terpenoid Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: CrtO, glycosyl-4,4'-diaponeurosporenoate acyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus crtOPQMN operon; staphyloxanthin biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: CrtO is a single-activity acyltransferase that esterifies the C6'' hydroxyl of the glucosyl moiety with 12-methyltetradecanoate as the final step of staphyloxanthin biosynthesis; the other four pathway activities sit on separate proteins (CrtM, CrtN, CrtP, CrtQ).

direction_conflict.note: MetaCyc writes the acyl donor as the free fatty acid, so the activated thioester (acyl-CoA/ACP) whose hydrolysis drives an EC 2.3.1.- acyl transfer is missing; that omission is exactly why the computed dG comes out at +46 to +49 kJ/mol and flips the direction against biosynthesis.

reactions.name: rxn11707
reactions.enzyme_name: 3'-N-debenzoyltaxol N-benzoyltransferase (DBTNBT), a BAHD-family acyl-CoA-dependent acyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Taxus cuspidata / T. baccata; final acylation step of Taxol biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: DBTNBT is a single-activity BAHD N-acyltransferase that benzoylates the C13 side-chain amine; it is one of a set of separate, distinct Taxus acyltransferases (TAT, TBT, DBAT, BAPT), not a multidomain protein.

direction_conflict.note: Benzoyl-CoA and the released CoA are both missing, so the written reaction is a bare acylation with no energy source; the thioester is what makes the forward direction toward paclitaxel irreversible.

reactions.name: rxn11708
reactions.enzyme_name: Baccatin III: 3-amino-3-phenylpropanoyl-CoA transferase (BAPT), a BAHD-family acyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Taxus cuspidata; C13 side-chain attachment step of Taxol biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: BAPT is a single-activity CoA-dependent acyltransferase that esterifies the C13 hydroxyl of baccatin III with the beta-phenylalanoyl group; the subsequent 2'-hydroxylation and N-benzoylation are catalysed by different proteins.

direction_conflict.note: beta-Phenylalanoyl-CoA and released CoA are absent from the equation, which is why the computed dG is +83 kJ/mol; with the real thioester donor the biosynthetic forward direction is the one that runs.

reactions.name: R08251
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) Isoniazid[0] <= (1) H+[0] + (1) Hydrazine[0] + (1) Isonicotinic acid[0]
pathways: KEGG: rn00983 (Drug metabolism - other enzymes)
reactions.enzyme_name: Hepatic amidase / carboxylesterase acting as isoniazid amidohydrolase; KEGG assigns K01044 carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), EC 3.1.1.1 / 3.5.1.-
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian liver microsomes (human, rat, rabbit)
reactions.rationale: Direct hydrolysis of isoniazid to isonicotinic acid plus hydrazine is carried out by a liver amidase blocked by the carboxylesterase/amidase inhibitor BNPP. Esterase plus amidase activity in a carboxylesterase is one serine-hydrolase active site acting on two bond types, i.e. promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains.

direction_conflict.note: Amide hydrolysis is thermodynamically irreversible in the forward sense; no amidase resynthesises isoniazid from hydrazine and isonicotinate.

reactions.name: SN38 glucuronide glucuronosohydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00983 (Drug metabolism - other enzymes)
reactions.enzyme_name: beta-glucuronidase (GUS), gut bacterial GH2 enzyme (E. coli GusA and Lactobacillus/Bacteroides homologues); human lysosomal GUSB also acts
reactions.organism_context: Human gut microbiota - reactivation of SN-38 from SN-38G drives irinotecan-induced diarrhoea
reactions.rationale: GH2 beta-glucuronidases carry one retaining-glycosidase active site per chain (homotetramer in E. coli); no second catalytic activity is reported for any of the characterised gut-bacterial or human enzymes.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis is the only direction; re-glucuronidation of SN-38 is a separate UGT1A1 reaction that requires UDP-glucuronate, not free glucuronate.

reactions.name: R08284
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: None identified - non-enzymatic decomposition/hydrolysis of oxazaphosphorine metabolites
reactions.organism_context: Human cyclophosphamide metabolism (KEGG rn00982)
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08284 carries no EC, no orthology, and is flagged both 'unclear reaction' and 'incomplete reaction'; nornitrogen mustard arises by spontaneous hydrolysis of phosphoramide mustard, not by an enzyme acting on carboxyphosphamide, which is itself the ALDH-derived dead-end detoxification product.

direction_conflict.note: The equation also loses most of the molecule (C7 to C4) with no products named, but whatever the real chemistry it is an irreversible breakdown - carboxyphosphamide cannot be reassembled from nornitrogen mustard.

reactions.name: R08290
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: NAD(P)H-dependent aldehyde/carbonyl reductase (aldo-keto reductase), by analogy with the aldophosphamide-to-alcophosphamide step
reactions.organism_context: Human/mammalian cytosol; ifosfamide metabolism (KEGG rn00982)
reactions.rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from chemistry, not confirmed: KEGG assigns no enzyme to R08290, but the matching cyclophosphamide step (aldophosphamide to alcophosphamide) is run by an NADPH-dependent cytosolic carbonyl/aldo-keto reductase, and aldo-keto reductases are single-activity monomeric enzymes.

direction_conflict.note: NAD(P)H is replaced by '2 H+' so the 2-electron reduction has no donor (KEGG itself flags the entry 'unclear' and 'incomplete'); the aldehyde-to-alcohol reduction direction is nevertheless the one that occurs physiologically.

reactions.name: rxn11836
reactions.enzyme_name: None - spontaneous beta-elimination of carbamic acid from 3-carbamoyl-2-phenylpropionaldehyde (CPPA)
reactions.organism_context: Human/rat felbamate bioactivation
reactions.rationale: In felbamate bioactivation CPPA loses its carbamate non-enzymatically to give atropaldehyde (2-phenylpropenal); the enzymatic steps in that pathway are the upstream esterase and alcohol dehydrogenase reactions, not this elimination.

direction_conflict.note: The carbamate leaving group is missing from the products (C10 to C9); the elimination is irreversible and runs only forward, after which atropaldehyde is trapped by glutathione via GSTs.

reactions.name: R08314
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: Microsomal epoxide hydrolase (mEH, EPHX1)
reactions.organism_context: Human and mammalian liver endoplasmic reticulum; the main route clearing carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide
reactions.rationale: mEH is a single alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold catalytic domain with one Asp-His-Glu triad and one activity; its reported role as a sodium-dependent bile-acid transport protein is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: Epoxide hydration is irreversible; mEH cannot re-cyclise the trans-10,11-diol back to the epoxide, so ModelSEED's '<' is not a reaction any epoxide hydrolase performs.

reactions.name: R08318
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: CYP3A4 (cytochrome P450 3A4), confirmed as the main catalyst converting 2-hydroxycarbamazepine to 2-hydroxyiminostilbene
reactions.organism_context: Human liver microsomes; carbamazepine bioactivation
reactions.rationale: CYP3A4 has one monooxygenase active site - its enormous substrate range is promiscuity, not a second activity - and its electron donor, NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, is a separate protein (unlike self-sufficient fused P450s such as P450 BM3, which genuinely are bifunctional).

direction_conflict.note: KEGG flags R08318 'incomplete reaction' and the equation drops the carbamoyl leaving group (C15 to C14) along with O2 and NADPH; the real route is a CYP3A4 oxidation to the iminoquinone followed by NADPH-mediated reduction, so the catabolic forward sense is correct but the entry collapses two steps.

reactions.name: R08321
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: Cytosolic carbonyl-reducing enzymes (aldo-keto reductases AKR1C1-AKR1C4 and carbonyl reductase 1) reducing oxcarbazepine to its 10-monohydroxy derivative (GP 47779 / licarbazepine)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver cytosol; oxcarbazepine is a prodrug whose active species is the 10-monohydroxy derivative
reactions.rationale: Ichida et al. quantified oxcarbazepine ketone reduction in human liver as essentially entirely cytosolic, partitioned among AKR1C1-4 and CBR1, each a single-domain NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase. The broad substrate range of AKR1C enzymes (including hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity) is one oxidoreductase chemistry on many substrates, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: The enzymology runs ketone to alcohol (oxcarbazepine to GP 47779), so ModelSEED's '<' points backwards; the apparent near-equilibrium comes from NADPH having been abstracted to a bare 2 H+, and KEGG itself labels R08321 'unclear/incomplete'.

reactions.name: R08340
pathways: KEGG: rn00982 (Drug metabolism - cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: Cytochrome P450 3A4 (unspecific monooxygenase, EC 1.14.14.1) performing the second N-demethylation of the methadone metabolite EDDP to EMDP
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and intestinal microsomes; CYP2B6/CYP2C19 contribute to the first methadone N-demethylation
reactions.rationale: KEGG annotates R08340 as CYP3A4 N-demethylation, and Moody et al. and Oda & Kharasch confirmed CYP3A4 catalyses the successive N-demethylations of methadone to EDDP and EMDP. CYP3A4 is a single heme-thiolate monooxygenase domain; its obligate partner NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase is a separate polypeptide, not a fused second activity.

direction_conflict.note: Written as a bare EDDP/EMDP isomerisation, but a CH2 unit (released as formaldehyde) plus O2 and NADPH are all absent; stripping the O2-consuming oxidation removes everything that makes this step one-way EDDP to EMDP.

reactions.name: alpha-Bisabolene synthase
reactions.enzyme_name: (-)-alpha-Bisabolol synthase (MrBBS), a class I sesquiterpene synthase (the ModelSEED label 'alpha-bisabolene synthase' is wrong for this product: cpd06515 levomenol is alpha-bisabolol, not bisabolene)
reactions.organism_context: Matricaria recutita (German chamomile); the same single-enzyme step is used in engineered yeast/E. coli alpha-bisabolol strains
reactions.rationale: Tai et al. characterised alpha-bisabolol synthase converting FPP directly to alpha-bisabolol; it is a single class I terpene-synthase alpha-domain with one Mg2+-dependent ionisation active site. Multiproduct behaviour in terpene synthases is substrate-cation promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Class I terpene synthases are made irreversible by diphosphate departure; ModelSEED's equation omits PPi entirely, which is why both estimators return a nonsensical ~+400 kJ/mol and force a '<' call.

reactions.name: humulene cyclase
reactions.enzyme_name: alpha-Humulene synthase (humulene cyclase), a class I sesquiterpene synthase cyclising FPP to alpha-humulene
reactions.organism_context: Zingiber zerumbet ZSS1 (first committed step of zerumbone biosynthesis); humulene-forming TPSs also known from Abies grandis and many angiosperms
reactions.rationale: Xu et al. characterised the zerumbone pathway sesquiterpene synthase that makes alpha-humulene from FPP, paired with a separate short-chain dehydrogenase; the synthase is a single class I terpene-synthase domain with one active site. No fused second catalytic activity is reported for humulene synthases.

direction_conflict.note: Diphosphate, the leaving group that makes the cyclisation irreversible, is missing from the equation, so the +440 kJ/mol dGPredictor value and the resulting '<' are artifacts.

reactions.name: R08393

direction_conflict.note: Both constituent steps run biosynthetically toward neral; the '<' call comes from a ~+420 kJ/mol estimate produced by the missing diphosphate and missing NAD+ couple.

reactions.name: rxn11905
reactions.enzyme_name: (+)-3-Carene synthase, a class I monoterpene synthase cyclising geranyl diphosphate to car-3-ene
reactions.organism_context: Conifers (Picea abies, Pinus spp.) and some angiosperms; the gene family is the plant TPS-b/TPS-d monoterpene synthases
reactions.rationale: The enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry (GPP to car-3-ene is by definition a 3-carene synthase) rather than confirmed for this ModelSEED entry, which carries no name, EC or xref. Class I monoterpene synthases are single-active-site enzymes; multiproduct carene synthases are still one catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: The diphosphate leaving group that makes terpene cyclisation one-way is absent from the equation, so the +424 to +457 kJ/mol estimates and the '<' direction they imply are artifacts.

reactions.name: rxn11906
reactions.enzyme_name: Geraniol synthase (GES), a class I monoterpene synthase that ionises geranyl diphosphate and quenches the cation with water to give geraniol
reactions.organism_context: Catharanthus roseus (CrGES, first step of the iridoid/MIA pathway), Ocimum basilicum, Valeriana, Cymbopogon
reactions.rationale: GPP to geraniol is the defining single-enzyme reaction of geraniol synthase, a single class I TPS domain; this is a well-established monofunctional terpene synthase and is called largely from established knowledge plus the Christianson cyclase review.

direction_conflict.note: Both the water co-substrate and the diphosphate product are missing; with PPi release deleted the estimators see a ~+425 kJ/mol uphill step and vote '<', the opposite of the real one-way hydrolytic ionisation.

reactions.name: R08397

reactions.rationale: KEGG's COMMENT marks this a multi-step, incomplete entry, so there is no single catalysing protein to classify; the chemistry requires at least a terpene synthase plus a separate reductase.

reactions.name: R08399
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified; KEGG flags R08399 as multi-step and incomplete (GPP to geraniol/citronellol then oxidation to (R)-(+)-citronellal)
reactions.rationale: KEGG marks the entry multi-step and incomplete, so no single protein can be named or classified; at minimum a terpene synthase, a double-bond reductase and an alcohol dehydrogenase are involved.

reactions.name: R08402
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified; the ginkgolide pathway downstream of levopimaradiene runs through levopimaradiene hydroxylase (CYP720B-type) and several further, mostly uncharacterised cytochrome P450s
reactions.organism_context: Ginkgo biloba root bark and leaf
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08402 is flagged 'multi-step reaction' and spans the whole oxidative elaboration of levopimaradiene into ginkgolide A; only two of the required Ginkgo P450s have been functionally identified to date, so no single catalysing enzyme exists for this entry.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED has additionally mis-mapped the substrate: cpd03629 is copalyl diphosphate (KEGG C06089), whereas KEGG R08402 starts from levopimaradiene (C11879), and nine oxygens plus the lost diphosphate are unaccounted for, so no direction read from this equation is meaningful.

reactions.name: Glycolate:(FAD) 2-oxidoreductase
reactions.enzyme_name: Glycolate dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.99.14), the GlcD/GlcE/GlcF three-subunit FAD- and Fe-S-containing membrane-associated oxidase of the glc operon; GlcD is the FAD-linked catalytic subunit
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli glc operon (b2979/b4468/b4467); homologues throughout bacteria and in the plant/algal glycolate dehydrogenase
reactions.rationale: Pellicer et al. showed the E. coli glc locus encodes three separate subunits of glycolate oxidase/dehydrogenase; per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the catalytic FAD subunit GlcD carries one activity, glycolate 2-oxidoreduction (it also accepts (R)-lactate, which is substrate breadth, not a second activity).

direction_conflict.note: IUBMB defines EC 1.1.99.14 with an unknown physiological acceptor; ModelSEED substitutes free FAD/FADH2 for the enzyme-bound FAD that passes electrons through Fe-S to the quinone pool, so the +15 kJ/mol 'reverse' call is the FAD couple's, not the real one. Physiologically the enzyme only oxidises glycolate to glyoxylate (it is how E. coli grows on glycolate), matching the LLM's forward call.

reactions.name: rxn11940
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) NAD[0] + (1) Mg-Protoporphyrin IX 13-monomethyl ester[0] <= (1) NADH[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) 13(1)-Hydroxy-Mg-protoporphyrin IX 13-monomethyl ester[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Mg-protoporphyrin IX monomethyl ester oxidative cyclase: the anaerobic radical-SAM form BchE (which matches the H2O-dependent chemistry written here) or the aerobic di-iron form AcsF/ChlE/CRD1-CHL27 with its Ycf54 partner; this entry is only the first (13(1)-hydroxylation) of the cyclase's three successive oxidations
reactions.organism_context: Anoxygenic phototrophic proteobacteria (BchE), cyanobacteria, algae and plants (AcsF/CHL27; barley Xantha-l, maize ZmCRD1)
reactions.rationale: The cyclase performs three sequential oxidations of one bound substrate at a single active site (radical-SAM in BchE, di-iron in AcsF) rather than carrying several fused catalytic domains, so it is iteratively monofunctional; the aerobic enzyme's dependence on a separate Ycf54 subunit is a complex, not a fusion.

direction_conflict.note: Free NAD+/NADH stands in for the real oxidant (O2 for AcsF, or SAM plus reduced ferredoxin for BchE); chlorophyll biosynthesis flows one way toward the isocyclic E ring, so the forward direction is the physiological one and the dGPredictor-driven '<' is an artifact of the substituted couple.

reactions.name: R08412
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified; dolichotheline is N-isovalerylhistamine, so the chemistry requires histidine decarboxylation to histamine followed by isovaleryl-CoA-dependent N-acylation, and no enzyme of either step has been characterised in the producing cactus
reactions.organism_context: Dolichothele sphaerica / Mammillaria (Cactaceae) imidazole alkaloids
reactions.rationale: KEGG flags R08412 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction' and no enzyme has been cloned for dolichotheline biosynthesis; searches returned no enzymology, so 'unknown' is the honest call rather than inventing an acyltransferase.

direction_conflict.note: Free isovalerate stands in for isovaleryl-CoA and the CO2 lost in decarboxylation is absent, so the +99 to +137 kJ/mol used to call '<' is not the real step's free energy; biosynthetic flux runs toward dolichotheline.

reactions.name: R08415

reactions.organism_context: Indolizidine alkaloid-producing plants (Leguminosae/Convolvulaceae); pathway known only from classical feeding studies

direction_conflict.note: The missing acetate/malonyl extender and the lost water make the +51 to +63 kJ/mol estimate meaningless; alkaloid biosynthesis flows away from pipecolate, not back to it.

reactions.name: R08422
pathways: KEGG: rn00960 (Tropane, piperidine and pyridine alkaloid biosynthesis)

reactions.organism_context: Sedum acre / Lobelia piperidine alkaloids; pathway inferred from precursor feeding only
reactions.rationale: KEGG flags R08422 'multi-step reaction / incomplete reaction' and a literature search returned no characterised enzyme for sedamine biosynthesis, so no single protein can be classified.

direction_conflict.note: Free cinnamate replaces the activated cinnamoyl-CoA and the condensation water is absent, so the thermodynamics behind ModelSEED's '<' does not describe the real chemistry; flux runs toward the alkaloid.

reactions.name: R08423

reactions.organism_context: Lobelia inflata and relatives (Campanulaceae); pathway known only from feeding experiments
reactions.rationale: KEGG flags R08423 as a 'multi-step reaction' combining two separate acyl condensations onto piperideine; searches for Lobelia alkaloid enzymology returned nothing, so there is no single catalysing protein to classify.

reactions.name: R08424

reactions.name: R08426
pathways: KEGG: rn00960 (Tropane, piperidine and pyridine alkaloid biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)

reactions.organism_context: Nicotiana tabacum / N. benthamiana root nicotine pathway

reactions.name: (R)-phenyllactyl-CoA:tropine O-phenyllactyltransferase

reactions.name: S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine:Norgalanthamine N-methyltransferase
