reactions.organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) phenylpropylamino alkaloid pathway; related chemistry in Ephedra sinica
reactions.rationale: KEGG itself decomposes the entry into two reactions, so no single enzyme catalyses it; the khat EST/transcriptome studies by Hagel and Groves list only candidate transaminases and have not confirmed a catalysing protein.

direction_conflict.note: Phenylalanine is the pathway entry point and cathinone the product, so the biosynthetic direction is forward; the '<' comes from a +48 to +61 kJ/mol estimate on an equation that omits the pyruvate/CO2 and the amino donor of the two real steps.

reactions.name: R08464
pathways: KEGG: rn00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: NADPH-dependent cathinone reductase (unidentified ketoreductase of khat/Ephedra)
reactions.organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) and Ephedra spp.; only candidate aldo-keto/short-chain reductase sequences from EST and transcriptome surveys, no cloned enzyme
reactions.rationale: The (S)-cathinone -> (1S,2S)-cathine reduction is well documented metabolically in maturing khat leaves, but the reductase itself has never been purified or cloned; only the downstream N-methyltransferase of the ephedrine pathway has been characterised, so mono- vs bifunctionality cannot be judged.

direction_conflict.note: Physiological flux is cathinone -> cathine (reduction), which is the left-to-right ('>') side the council chose; KEGG R08464 writes this two-electron step with bare H+ and no NAD(P)H (ModelSEED flags CI:-2), so the eQuilibrator/GC sign that drives ModelSEED's '<' is computed on a redox-incomplete equation.

reactions.name: R08466
pathways: MetaCyc: ALKALOIDS-SYN (Alkaloid Biosynthesis); N-CONTAINING-SECONDARY-CMPD-SYN (Nitrogen-Containing Secondary Compound Biosynthesis); PWY-5883 (ephedrine biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: NADPH-dependent cathinone reductase (unidentified ketoreductase; MetaCyc RXN-9339 of ephedrine biosynthesis)
reactions.organism_context: Ephedra sinica and Catha edulis; MetaCyc PWY-5883 lists the step without an assigned protein
reactions.rationale: Same uncharacterised ketoreductase problem as R08464: (S)-cathinone -> (1R,2S)-norephedrine is biochemically established in Ephedra and khat but no gene product has been assigned, so functionality is genuinely unknown rather than monofunctional by default.

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthesis runs cathinone -> norephedrine (the '>' side); the equation carries bare H+ instead of NADPH/NADP+ (ModelSEED CI:-2), so no thermodynamic direction computed from it is meaningful.

reactions.name: R08471
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (acridone prenyltransferase + O-methyltransferase + cyclase steps of acronycine formation)
reactions.organism_context: Rutaceae (Ruta graveolens, Sarcomelicope spp.) acridone alkaloid metabolism
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08471 itself is annotated 'multi-step reaction (methyltransfer, prenyltransfer and cyclizing); incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED carries it mass-unbalanced by C6H8 (the prenyl and methyl donors are absent), so there is no one protein to classify.

direction_conflict.note: The only flux that exists in vivo is biosynthetic (1,3-dihydroxy-N-methylacridone -> acronycine, the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' would demand acronycine de-prenylation, which is not a known pathway, but the call rests on a pathway, not an enzyme.

reactions.name: R08472
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (acridone prenyltransferase + cyclase steps of rutacridone formation)
reactions.organism_context: Ruta graveolens acridone alkaloid metabolism
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08472 is flagged 'multi-step reaction (prenyltransfer and cyclizing); incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it short by C5H6 (the dimethylallyl donor), so no single catalysing protein exists for the entry as written.

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthetic flux is 1,3-dihydroxy-N-methylacridone -> rutacridone (the '>' side); the direction is a pathway property, not an enzyme property, and the ModelSEED equation omits the prenyl donor that makes it irreversible.

reactions.name: R08473
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme; nearest real catalyst is a type III polyketide synthase (quinolone synthase) acting on anthraniloyl-CoA + malonyl-CoA
reactions.organism_context: Rutaceae quinolone alkaloid plants; functionally equivalent fungal type III PKSs (AthePKS, FerePKS) make 2-quinolones from anthranilate derivatives in vitro
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08473 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED is short by C2 and one charge because the CoA activation and the malonyl-CoA extender are both omitted; the chalcone-synthase-like PKS that does the real condensation is monofunctional but does not catalyse the written transformation.

direction_conflict.note: Anthranilate is the precursor and 4-hydroxy-2-quinolone the product in every described pathway (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' implies quinolone catabolism to anthranilate, for which there is no enzymology.

reactions.name: R08477
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (hypothetical anthranilate + 1-pyrroline route to vasicine/peganine)
reactions.organism_context: Peganum harmala / Justicia adhatoda quinazoline alkaloid biosynthesis, inferred from labelling studies only
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08477 is flagged 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and remains a precursor-feeding hypothesis with no enzyme assigned to any step; ModelSEED also carries it unbalanced (O:-1, CI:1).

direction_conflict.note: The only direction with any support is condensation of the two precursors into vasicine (the '>' side), but it is a pathway hypothesis rather than a characterised enzyme reaction.

reactions.name: R08478
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (alternative hypothetical N-acetylanthranilate + L-aspartate route to vasicine/peganine)
reactions.organism_context: Peganum harmala quinazoline alkaloid biosynthesis; competing labelling-based hypothesis to R08477
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08478 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED's own balance check reports C:-2/H:-1/O:-6 plus a charge error, so the entry is a pathway sketch with no protein behind it.

direction_conflict.note: Flux, if any, is biosynthetic toward vasicine (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' comes from a group-contribution value (+292 kJ/mol) computed on a badly unbalanced equation.

reactions.name: R08487
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: strictosamide-forming lactamase of camptothecin biosynthesis (unidentified; possibly partly spontaneous)
reactions.organism_context: Ophiorrhiza pumila and Camptotheca acuminata; O. pumila routes camptothecin through strictosamide, C. acuminata through strictosidinic acid
reactions.rationale: The strictosidine -> strictosamide lactamisation is an accepted step of the O. pumila camptothecin route but no catalysing protein has been isolated; KEGG marks R08487 'incomplete reaction' and the ModelSEED equation drops the methanol co-product (MI:C:-1/H:-5/O:-1).

direction_conflict.note: Lactamisation runs strictosidine -> strictosamide (the '>' side) and is driven by loss of methanol, exactly the species the ModelSEED equation omits, so its thermodynamic '<' is computed on the wrong chemistry.

reactions.name: R08490
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (several oxidation/ring-rearrangement steps from deoxypumiloside to camptothecin)
reactions.organism_context: Ophiorrhiza pumila / Camptotheca acuminata; the late camptothecin steps are still only candidate genes
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08490 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it C6H12O4 short; recent multi-omics work still only prioritises candidate genes for these late oxidations, so no single enzyme can be named.

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthesis is deoxypumiloside -> camptothecin (the '>' side); direction here is a pathway fact, and the equation is too incomplete for thermodynamics to settle it.

reactions.name: Strychnine synthesis
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (the strictosidine-to-strychnine pathway: SGD, geissoschizine synthase, Wieland-Gumlich aldehyde steps, malonyltransferase, prestrychnine decarboxylation)
reactions.organism_context: Strychnos nux-vomica; the full route was reconstituted in Nicotiana benthamiana by Hong et al. 2022
reactions.rationale: Strictosidine -> strychnine is a ten-plus enzyme pathway (deglycosylation, reduction, oxidations, malonylation, then decarboxylative cyclisation of prestrychnine), so no protein catalyses the ModelSEED entry; KEGG has since withdrawn R08495 entirely and replaced it with the stepwise reactions R13334/R13336.

direction_conflict.note: KEGG no longer serves R08495 at all, so ModelSEED is carrying a reaction its source has retired; the real pathway runs strictosidine -> strychnine (the '>' side) and is pulled irreversibly by the CO2-releasing prestrychnine step.

reactions.name: R08496
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (strictosidine deglycosylation plus several rearrangement/oxidation steps toward corynantheal)
reactions.organism_context: Strychnos / Corynanthe-type monoterpene indole alkaloid plants
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08496 is flagged all three ways - 'unclear reaction', 'multi-step reaction', 'incomplete reaction' - and ModelSEED carries it C8H12O8 short (the glucose moiety), so there is no single catalysing protein.

direction_conflict.note: Strictosidine is upstream of corynantheal in every described route (the '>' side); the ModelSEED equation loses the glucose released by strictosidine beta-glucosidase, which is the step that makes the sequence irreversible.

reactions.name: R08500
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified (secoiridoid steps from secologanin to gentiopicroside)
reactions.organism_context: Gentiana spp. secoiridoid glycoside metabolism
reactions.rationale: KEGG explicitly labels R08500 an 'unclear reaction' and an 'incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED carries it CH4O short; no enzyme has been assigned to the secologanin -> gentiopicrin conversion.

direction_conflict.note: Secologanin is the biosynthetic precursor of gentiopicroside (the '>' side), but KEGG itself disowns the entry as unclear, so neither direction call rests on real enzymology.

reactions.name: 3D-(3,5/4)-Trihydroxycyclohexane-1,2-dione acylhydrolase (decyclizing)
pathways: MetaCyc: Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); P562-PWY (myo-inositol degradation I); PWY-7237 (myo-, chiro- and scyllo-inositol degradation); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-DEGRADATION (Secondary Metabolite Degradation); SUGAR-ALCOHOLS-DEG (Sugar Alcohol Degradation); Sugar-Derivatives (Sugar Derivative Degradation)
KEGG: rn00562 (Inositol phosphate metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: 3D-(3,5/4)-trihydroxycyclohexane-1,2-dione acylhydrolase (decyclizing), IolD (EC 3.7.1.22, KEGG K03336)
reactions.organism_context: Bacillus subtilis myo-inositol catabolism; orthologues in Salmonella, Sinorhizobium meliloti and many soil and commensal bacteria
reactions.rationale: IolD is a single ThDP-dependent hydrolase that performs one C-C bond cleavage, ring-opening DKDI to 5-deoxy-D-glucuronate; Yoshida et al. reconstituted the whole B. subtilis iol pathway with one discrete enzyme per step and found no second activity on IolD.

direction_conflict.note: The enzyme is a decyclising hydrolase operating in the catabolic direction (DKDI + H2O -> 5-deoxy-D-glucuronate, the '>' side); ring-opening hydrolysis is not reversed in vivo, so ModelSEED's '<' is wrong even though the equation itself is balanced.

reactions.name: R08509
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme (polyketide synthase condensation to 5-oxo-octanal plus transamination/cyclisation to gamma-coniceine)
reactions.organism_context: Conium maculatum (poison hemlock) and Sarracenia flava; PKS candidates isolated, downstream transaminase still unassigned
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08509 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it unbalanced (N:+1/O:-2, CI:2) because the amine donor and malonyl-CoA extenders are missing; only part of the coniine route has been characterised, so no single protein can be classified.

direction_conflict.note: Octanoate/octanoyl units feed forward into gamma-coniceine (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' would be alkaloid catabolism to a fatty acid, which is not described.

reactions.name: 4- (phosphohydroxy)-l-threonine dehydrogenase
reactions.enzyme_name: 4-hydroxythreonine-4-phosphate dehydrogenase, PdxA (EC 1.1.1.262)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli and other gamma-proteobacteria; deoxyxylulose-dependent PLP biosynthesis (also a drug target in Acinetobacter baumannii)
reactions.rationale: PdxA is a homodimeric NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase with a single active site that oxidises 4-phosphohydroxy-L-threonine; the subsequent decarboxylation to 3-amino-2-oxopropyl phosphate is spontaneous/non-enzymatic, not a second catalytic domain, and PdxA partners PdxJ as a separate protein.

direction_conflict.note: The enzyme runs oxidatively toward 3-amino-2-oxopropyl phosphate (the '>' side) and is pulled irreversibly by CO2 loss; ModelSEED's equation omits NADH and CO2 entirely (its own check reports C:-22/H:-27/N:-7/O:-16/P:-2), which is why the ~400-600 kJ/mol 'reverse' estimate appears.

reactions.name: pimeloyl-coa dehydrogenase
reactions.enzyme_name: pimeloyl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.1.62; KEGG orthologues K04118 large subunit + K28556 small subunit)
reactions.organism_context: Denitrifying pimelate-degrading bacteria (Gallus & Schink isolates), Rhodopseudomonas palustris and other anaerobic benzoate degraders
reactions.rationale: This is a two-subunit acyl-CoA-dehydrogenase-family enzyme carrying one alpha,beta-desaturation activity; a two-polypeptide complex is not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the catalytic subunit is monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: Physiological flux is beta-oxidative, pimeloyl-CoA -> 6-carboxyhex-2-enoyl-CoA (the '>' side); ModelSEED substitutes free FAD/FADH2 for the enzyme's real NAD+/ETF-quinone acceptor, and the free-flavin couple is what produces eQuilibrator's +19 kJ/mol and hence the spurious '<'.

reactions.name: GLUTARYL-COA-DEHYDROG-RXN
reactions.enzyme_name: non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GdhA/GcdH-type, EC 1.3.8.6 family)
reactions.organism_context: Obligately anaerobic aromatic degraders (Desulfococcus multivorans, Syntrophus, Geobacter), where glutaconyl-CoA is handed to a separate biotin-dependent glutaconyl-CoA decarboxylase
reactions.rationale: The enzyme that stops at glutaconyl-CoA is the non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a homotetrameric acyl-CoA dehydrogenase with a single dehydrogenation activity; Wischgoll et al. showed the decarboxylating/non-decarboxylating split is a single active-site residue, and the decarboxylating (human GCDH-like) variant would give crotonyl-CoA + CO2, not this product.

direction_conflict.note: The dehydrogenase runs glutaryl-CoA -> glutaconyl-CoA (the '>' side), electrons going to ETF and thence to the membrane quinone pool; writing free FAD/FADH2 as the acceptor is what makes eQuilibrator read +19 kJ/mol and drives ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.name: d-lactate dehydrogenase, fad
reactions.enzyme_name: FAD-dependent D-lactate dehydrogenase, Dld (EC 1.1.2.4/1.1.2.5)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli membrane-associated Dld, yeast mitochondrial Dld1p, Treponema pallidum TP0037 and newly mined bacterial FAD-D-LDHs
reactions.rationale: Dld-type FAD-D-LDH is a single-chain flavoprotein with one catalytic activity, oxidising D-lactate and passing electrons from its tightly bound FAD to the quinone pool or cytochrome c; its membrane association is a binding property, not a second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: The enzyme is a respiratory D-lactate oxidase (D-lactate -> pyruvate, the '>' side) and is effectively irreversible because the electrons leave to quinone; ModelSEED models the acceptor as free FAD/FADH2, whose low potential inverts the computed sign.

reactions.name: salicylacetate esterase
reactions.enzyme_name: salicylacetate (salicyl acetate) esterase - specific protein not identified
reactions.organism_context: none established; the generic activity (aspirin hydrolysis) is carried in mammals by carboxylesterases CES1/CES2, butyrylcholinesterase and albumin pseudo-esterase, none of which is the ModelSEED gene association
reactions.rationale: ModelSEED pairs the name 'salicylacetate esterase' with aspirin (acetylsalicylate) as substrate but saligenin (salicyl alcohol) as product, which cannot both be true - aspirin hydrolysis yields salicylate, and saligenin would require salicyl acetate as the ester; with the substrate ambiguous no catalysing protein can be identified.

direction_conflict.note: Any esterase runs hydrolytically (ester + H2O -> acid + alcohol, the '>' side) and is not reversed in water; ModelSEED's own check reports H:+2/O:-1, confirming the aspirin/salicyl-acetate mix-up that produces the large positive 'reverse' dG.

reactions.name: 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenase
reactions.enzyme_name: 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenase, PaaH (NAD+-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase of the phenylacetate catabolon)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli paa operon and orthologous paa clusters in Pseudomonas and Rhodococcus; distinct from the fused bifunctional FadB of classical beta-oxidation
reactions.rationale: In the paa beta-oxidation module the hydratase (PaaF/PaaG), the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (PaaH) and the thiolase (PaaJ) are separate single-activity proteins that interact as a complex; only if this reaction is instead assigned to FadB would a genuinely fused hydratase/dehydrogenase/epimerase be involved.

direction_conflict.note: Net catabolic flux is oxidative, 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA -> 3-oxoadipyl-CoA (the '>' side), pulled by the downstream thiolase, although NAD+-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenases are intrinsically reversible; the ModelSEED entry writes molecular H2 in place of NAD+/NADH, which is chemically meaningless and fully determines the computed sign.

reactions.name: Heme D synthase
reactions.enzyme_name: catalase HPII (KatE) - the protoheme-to-cis-heme d conversion is a self-catalysed modification of its own prosthetic group; no dedicated 'heme D synthase' is known
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli HPII (a clade-2 monofunctional catalase, unlike the genuinely bifunctional catalase-peroxidase KatG); the chemically identical heme d of cytochrome bd oxidase has no assigned biosynthetic enzyme at all
reactions.rationale: Loewen et al. showed HPII itself converts bound protoheme to cis-heme d using H2O2, i.e. an autocatalytic prosthetic-group modification inside the catalase active site rather than a separate turnover activity, so HPII stays monofunctional and there is no standalone heme D synthase to classify.

direction_conflict.note: Heme -> heme d is an irreversible oxidation (the '>' side) requiring H2O2/O2, but the ModelSEED equation writes it as a bare hydration with no oxidant, so the +115 kJ/mol dGPredictor value behind ModelSEED's '<' describes a reaction that does not exist.

reactions.name: Glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, mitochondrial
reactions.enzyme_name: FAD-linked mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (Gut2p in yeast; GPD2/mGPDH in mammals, EC 1.1.5.3)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Gut2p on the outer face of the inner mitochondrial membrane; mammalian mGPDH, the metformin target
reactions.rationale: A single flavoprotein chain with one catalytic activity, oxidising glycerol-3-phosphate and reducing ubiquinone; the mammalian enzyme's EF-hand Ca2+-binding region is regulatory, not a second catalytic site, so it does not count as bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: mGPDH/Gut2p is the oxidative arm of the glycerophosphate shuttle (G3P -> DHAP, the '>' side) and is irreversible because electrons leave to CoQ; the cytosolic NAD-linked Gpd1p runs the opposite way as a separate enzyme, and modelling the acceptor as free FAD/FADH2 is what makes eQuilibrator return +11 kJ/mol and ModelSEED choose '<'.

reactions.name: Dihydroxy-acid dehydratase, mitochondrial
reactions.enzyme_name: dihydroxy-acid dehydratase (Ilv3p/IlvD, EC 4.2.1.9)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae mitochondrial Ilv3p; bacterial and plant IlvD orthologues (a herbicide/antimicrobial target)
reactions.rationale: DHAD is a single [Fe-S]-cluster dehydratase with one catalytic activity (dehydration of 2,3-dihydroxy-3-methylbutanoate to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate); no second activity is reported in the structural or inhibitor literature.

direction_conflict.note: DHAD is the committed, effectively irreversible dehydration step toward 2-oxoisovalerate (the '>' side); the ModelSEED entry names the ketol-acid reductoisomerase intermediate 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate as substrate and omits both NADPH and water (its own check reports O:-1), so it is not actually the DHAD reaction.

reactions.name: glucan 1,4-alpha-glucosidase, vacuole
reactions.enzyme_name: glucan 1,4-alpha-glucosidase (glucoamylase), vacuolar Sga1p (EC 3.2.1.3)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae sporulation-specific vacuolar glucoamylase; GH15 family, as in Aspergillus GlaA
reactions.rationale: A single exo-acting glycoside hydrolase activity releasing glucose from the non-reducing end; the starch-binding module carried by many fungal glucoamylases is a non-catalytic CBM, so it does not make the enzyme bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: Glycosidic hydrolysis runs one way in vivo (glycogen + H2O -> glucose, the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of the glycogen pseudo-compound (C24H42O21) being consumed whole without a shortened-polymer product (its own check reports C:-18/H:-32/O:-16), which is exactly what inflates the dG to +220 to +532 kJ/mol.

reactions.name: glycogen phosphorylase
reactions.enzyme_name: glycogen phosphorylase (EC 2.4.1.1; bacterial maltodextrin phosphorylase MalP, yeast Gph1p, animal PYGL/PYGM/PYGB)
reactions.organism_context: Broadly conserved; the PLP cofactor acts as a general acid/base rather than in transamination
reactions.rationale: One catalytic activity, phosphorolysis of the alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond; the allosteric AMP/glucose-6-phosphate sites and the Ser14 phosphorylation site are regulatory, and the debranching enzyme's genuinely bifunctional transferase/glucosidase is a different protein.

direction_conflict.note: Phosphorylase sits near equilibrium (dG'o around +3 kJ/mol) and its in vivo direction is set by the Pi:glucose-1-phosphate ratio, not by the enzyme - though the physiological net flux is phosphorolytic, so of the two options the council's '>' is the better one; ModelSEED's '<' is driven by the same unbalanced glycogen pseudo-compound (C:-18/H:-32/O:-16) that gives the nonsensical +225 to +525 kJ/mol.

reactions.name: sirohydrochlorin dehydrogenase
reactions.enzyme_name: Siroheme synthase (CysG) / precorrin-2 dehydrogenase
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella CysG is a single chain carrying all three activities; yeast Met8p is bifunctional (dehydrogenase + chelatase, no methyltransferase); Bacillus megaterium SirC and alpha-proteobacterial Sirohydrochlorin ferrochelatase are separate monofunctional proteins.
reactions.rationale: The precorrin-2 -> sirohydrochlorin dehydrogenation is run by the C-terminal module of siroheme synthase CysG, which in enterobacteria also carries SUMT methyltransferase and sirohydrochlorin ferrochelatase activity; the dehydrogenase and chelatase even share one active site. Lineages that split the pathway use the monofunctional SirC dehydrogenase.

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthetic flux is strictly precorrin-2 -> sirohydrochlorin (the LLM direction); note the ModelSEED entry writes NADP(H) where the enzyme is NAD+-dependent, which biases any thermodynamic direction call toward the reductive side.

reactions.name: carboxyphosphonoenolpyruvate phosphonomutase
reactions.enzyme_name: Carboxyphosphonoenolpyruvate (CPEP) phosphonomutase
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF1293 (bialaphos producer); homologues in phosphinothricin-tripeptide and phosalacine producers.
reactions.rationale: Hidaka et al. purified this single 32.8 kDa / 295-residue protein from the bialaphos pathway and showed it performs only the CPEP -> phosphinopyruvate + CO2 rearrangement that forms the C-P bond; no second catalytic activity is reported.

direction_conflict.note: The C-P-bond-forming rearrangement is coupled to decarboxylation and is physiologically irreversible toward phosphinopyruvate; ModelSEED balances this entry with a fictitious 0.5 H2 where the duplicate entry rxn14022 correctly uses H+, inventing a reductant that corrupts the thermodynamic direction call.

reactions.name: nicotinate-nucleotide-dimethylbenzimidazole phosphoribosyltransferase
reactions.reaction: (1) Nicotinate ribonucleotide[0] + (1) Dimethylbenzimidazole[0] <= (1) H+[0] + (1) alpha-Ribazole 5'-phosphate[0] + (1) NAC[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Nicotinate-nucleotide:dimethylbenzimidazole phosphoribosyltransferase (CobT)
reactions.organism_context: Salmonella enterica / E. coli CobT is a homodimer with a single PRTase activity; the functionally equivalent archaeal and cyanobacterial system ArsAB is a two-protein complex, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
reactions.rationale: CobT carries one catalytic activity, transfer of the phosphoribosyl group of NaMN onto 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole to give alpha-ribazole-5'-P plus nicotinate. The alternative ArsAB enzyme of methanogens/cyanobacteria is a separate-subunit complex, which does not count as bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: In cobamide biosynthesis CobT runs toward alpha-ribazole-5'-phosphate (the LLM direction); ModelSEED's own status flags this entry short by C11H14N (status MI:C:11/H:14/N:1), so its thermodynamics are not trustworthy.

reactions.name: Proline dehydrogenase
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) FAD[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) L-Proline[0] <= (1) L-Glutamate5-semialdehyde[0] + (1) FADH2[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Proline utilization A (PutA), proline dehydrogenase module
reactions.organism_context: Gram-negative bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella, Bradyrhizobium); in Mycobacterium tuberculosis and in eukaryotes PRODH and P5CDH are separate monofunctional proteins.
reactions.rationale: PutA fuses two genuine catalytic activities, FAD-dependent PRODH and NAD+-dependent P5CDH, on one polypeptide with a substrate channel between them; the additional DNA-binding transcriptional-repressor domain of trifunctional PutAs is moonlighting (nucleic-acid binding), not a third catalytic activity, so this stays bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: PRODH is physiologically a one-way catabolic oxidation of proline because its enzyme-bound FADH2 is reoxidised by membrane ubiquinone, and the ModelSEED equation replaces that acceptor with free FAD/FADH2, removing the irreversibility and inverting the predicted direction.

reactions.name: carboxyphosphonopyruvate carboxy-lyase
pathways: MetaCyc: Antibiotic-Biosynthesis (Antibiotic Biosynthesis); PWY-6322 (phosphinothricin tripeptide biosynthesis); PWY-7769 (phosalacine biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
KEGG: rn00440 (Phosphonate and phosphinate metabolism); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Carboxyvinyl-carboxyphosphonate phosphorylmutase (CPEP phosphonomutase)
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus SF1293 and other bialaphos/phosphinothricin producers.
reactions.rationale: Same single-activity enzyme as rxn13819 (duplicate ModelSEED entry: cpd17932 and cpd03803 share formula C4H2O7P and KEGG C17946/C06367); the purified protein catalyses only the decarboxylative phosphonomutase rearrangement to (hydroxyphosphinyl)pyruvate.

direction_conflict.note: Loss of CO2 makes the rearrangement effectively irreversible in the direction the LLM council chose.

reactions.name: 3'-phosphoadenylyl-sulfate:desulfo-p-hydroxybenzylglucosinolate sulfotransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00966 (Glucosinolate biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites); rn01210 (2-Oxocarboxylic acid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: PAPS:desulfoglucosinolate sulfotransferase (SOT16/SOT17/SOT18 type)

reactions.enzyme_name: Aflatoxin B1 aldehyde reductase (AFAR; AKR7A1/AKR7A2/AKR7A3)
reactions.organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
reactions.rationale: Second reduction by the same AFAR enzyme, converting the AFB1 monoalcohol to the dialcohol; recombinant AKR7A1/AKR7A3 reduce the dialdehyde to both mono- and dialcohols, one catalytic activity acting twice.

direction_conflict.note: NADPH, the species that makes this reduction irreversible, is absent from the equation.

reactions.name: R09415
pathways: KEGG: rn00980 (Metabolism of xenobiotics by cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: Aflatoxin B1 aldehyde reductase (AFAR; AKR7A1/AKR7A2/AKR7A3)
reactions.organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
reactions.rationale: Same AFAR aldo-keto reductase reducing the alternative monoalcohol regioisomer to the common AFB1 dialcohol; single catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: NADPH is stripped from the equation, leaving only two H+, so the direction call rests on nothing; the enzymatic reduction runs left-to-right.

reactions.name: microsomal epoxide hydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00980 (Metabolism of xenobiotics by cytochrome P450)
reactions.enzyme_name: Microsomal epoxide hydrolase (EPHX1)
reactions.organism_context: mammalian liver microsomes (rat/human)
reactions.rationale: EC 3.3.2.9 / EPHX1 is a single-activity alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold enzyme that opens arene oxides such as DMBA-5,6-oxide to trans-dihydrodiols; its reported bile-acid-transport role is non-catalytic moonlighting, and the genuinely bifunctional family member is the soluble EH EPHX2 (N-terminal lipid phosphatase + C-terminal hydrolase), which is not this enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: Epoxide hydration is irreversible; there is no enzymatic dehydration of a trans-dihydrodiol back to the arene oxide.

reactions.name: germacradienol geosmin-lyase (acetone forming)
pathways: KEGG: rn00909 (Sesquiterpenoid and triterpenoid biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Geosmin synthase (germacradienol/geosmin synthase, ScGS / SCO6073)
distinct_activities: N-terminal domain: Mg2+-dependent ionisation/cyclisation of (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate to germacradienol (+ germacrene D) with PPi release - germacradienol synthase, EC 4.2.3.22
C-terminal domain: protonation-dependent retro-Prins fragmentation/Prins cyclisation of germacradienol to geosmin + acetone - EC 4.1.99.16
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces coelicolor and other actinobacteria; a bifunctional alpha-alpha terpene synthase. Fungal geosmin producers also use a bifunctional cyclase.
reactions.rationale: Crystallographic and mutagenesis work shows ScGS has two distinct metal-dependent active sites on one polypeptide: the N-terminal domain cyclises FPP to germacradienol, and the C-terminal domain fragments germacradienol to geosmin and acetone - two genuine catalytic activities, not a moonlighting role or a subunit complex.

direction_conflict.note: This entry is the C-terminal domain's retro-Prins fragmentation, which expels acetone and is irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call (geosmin + acetone to germacradienol) has no enzymatic counterpart, and the bifunctionality is precisely why the committed step upstream (FPP ionisation) never appears in this equation.

reactions.name: sulfite:O-phospho-L-serine sulfotransferase (phosphate-hydrolysing, L-cysteate-forming)
pathways: MetaCyc: Coenzyme-M-Biosynthesis (Coenzyme M Biosynthesis); Cofactor-Biosynthesis (Cofactor, Prosthetic Group, Electron Carrier, and Vitamin Biosynthesis); PWY-6643 (coenzyme M biosynthesis II)
reactions.enzyme_name: Cysteate synthase (O-phospho-L-serine:sulfite 2-amino-2-carboxyethyltransferase; MA3297)
reactions.organism_context: Methanosarcina acetivorans (Methanosarcinales/Methanomicrobiales coenzyme M pathway); the protein evolved from an ancestral threonine synthase by gene duplication
reactions.rationale: The MA3297 PLP protein specifically catalyses the beta-replacement of L-phosphoserine + sulfite to L-cysteate + Pi and does NOT complement an E. coli thrC mutant or run the threonine synthase reaction - the ancestral activity was lost, so this is a monofunctional enzyme and not a bifunctional cysteate/threonine synthase.

direction_conflict.note: Nucleophilic addition of sulfite to a PLP-bound dehydroalanine with phosphate release is a committed biosynthetic step toward coenzyme M, i.e. left-to-right as written; ModelSEED's reverse direction would have the cell making phosphoserine from cysteate.

reactions.name: hesperetin 7-(6-O-alpha-L-rhamnopyranosyl-beta-D-glucopyranoside) 6-O-alpha-rhamnopyranosyl-beta-glucohydrolase
reactions.enzyme_name: Hesperidin 6-O-alpha-L-rhamnosyl-beta-D-glucosidase (rutinosidase / alpha-rhamnosyl-beta-glucosidase diglycosidase)
reactions.organism_context: fungal: Aspergillus oryzae (AoRut), A. niger, Acremonium sp. DSM 24697
reactions.rationale: Rutinosidases are single-catalytic-domain glycoside hydrolases that release the intact rutinose disaccharide from hesperidin in one step (the crystal structure of A. oryzae AoRut shows one active site); their transglycosylation is the same chemistry with a non-water acceptor, not a second activity. Crude commercial 'hesperidinase' is a mixture of separate alpha-rhamnosidase and beta-glucosidase proteins, which is a preparation, not a bifunctional enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: Glycoside hydrolysis is strongly favoured in vivo; the condensation direction is only accessible in vitro at high sugar/acceptor concentration, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is wrong.

reactions.name: 2,3-dihydro-2,3-dihydroxybenzoyl-CoA 3,4-didehydroadipyl-CoA semialdehyde-lyase (formate-forming)
reactions.enzyme_name: Benzoyl-CoA-dihydrodiol lyase / 2,3-epoxybenzoyl-CoA dihydrolase (BoxC)
reactions.organism_context: Azoarcus evansii and other bacteria using the aerobic CoA-dependent 'box' benzoate pathway (~4-5% of sequenced bacteria)
reactions.rationale: BoxC is a homodimeric crotonase (enoyl-CoA hydratase/isomerase) superfamily protein that performs one overall ring-cleavage: it uses two waters to open the 2,3-epoxide/oxepin ring and then hydrolyse ring C2 off as formate, all in one active site, so this is a single catalytic activity (the term 'dihydrolase' refers to the two waters, not to two enzymes' worth of activity).

direction_conflict.note: The published stoichiometry (dihydrodiol/epoxide + 2 H2O -> 3,4-dehydroadipyl-CoA semialdehyde + formate) matches the equation read left-to-right; recondensing formate onto the semialdehyde to rebuild the ring is not an activity BoxC has.

reactions.name: streptothricin-F hydrolase
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) Streptothricin F[0] <= (1) streptothricin F acid[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Streptothricin hydrolase (SttH)
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces spp.; an isochorismatase-like hydrolase (ILH) superfamily resistance/self-protection enzyme
reactions.rationale: SttH is a single-activity ILH-superfamily hydrolase that opens the streptolidine lactam ring of streptothricin antibiotics, inactivating them; no second catalytic activity is reported for it.

direction_conflict.note: Lactam hydrolysis to the ring-opened acid is the antibiotic-inactivating step and runs one way; no lactam-forming (ring-closing) activity is known for SttH.

pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); Nitroaromatic-Degradation (Nitroaromatic Compound Degradation); PWY-7044 (5-nitroanthranilate degradation)

reactions.organism_context: Bradyrhizobium sp. strain JS329 (5-nitroanthranilic acid degradation); a metalloprotease-family (amidohydrolase-like) protein repurposed for aromatic deamination
reactions.rationale: 5NAA-A catalyses the single hydrolytic deamination of 5-nitroanthranilate to 5-nitrosalicylate by transition-metal-dependent nucleophilic aromatic substitution; the structural/mechanistic work describes one active site and one activity.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolytic release of ammonia from the ring is irreversible; re-amination of 5-nitrosalicylate is not an enzymatic reaction.

reactions.name: 4,4'-diapophytoene:FAD oxidoreductase
reactions.enzyme_name: 4,4'-Diapophytoene (dehydrosqualene) desaturase CrtN
reactions.organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus (staphyloxanthin pathway) and other C30-carotenogenic Firmicutes/Lactobacillaceae
reactions.rationale: A single CrtN polypeptide, an FAD-dependent amine-oxidase-fold desaturase, introduces the successive double bonds; iterative use of one active site on a series of substrates is not a second catalytic activity. This entry is the summed four-desaturation (dehydrosqualene -> 4,4'-diapolycopene) that IUBMB assigns to the one EC 1.3.8.2.

direction_conflict.note: The flavin is CrtN's prosthetic group, not a free cosubstrate; writing four free FAD/FADH2 and omitting the terminal oxidant makes the desaturation look uphill, whereas in vivo reoxidation of the bound flavin pulls the reaction one way into carotenoid biosynthesis.

reactions.name: 2-oxepin-2(3H)-ylideneacetyl-CoA hydrolyase
pathways: MetaCyc: AMINE-DEG (Amine and Polyamine Degradation); AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); PWY-6071 (superpathway of phenylethylamine degradation); PWY0-321 (phenylacetate degradation I (aerobic)); Phenolic-Compounds-Degradation (Phenolic Compound Degradation); Phenylacetate-Degradation (Phenylacetate Degradation)
KEGG: rn00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: Oxepin-CoA hydrolase / 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase (PaaZ)
distinct_activities: oxepin-CoA hydrolase, C-terminal (R)-specific enoyl-CoA hydratase/MaoC-like ring-cleaving domain (EC 3.3.2.12)
NADP+-dependent 3-oxo-5,6-didehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase, N-terminal ALDH domain (EC 1.2.1.91)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli and other aerobic phenylacetate degraders; a natural ALDH+MaoC gene fusion. In bacteria lacking the fusion the two activities are encoded by separate genes (an NAD+-ALDH in the paa cluster plus a hydratase outside it).
reactions.rationale: Teufel et al. characterised PaaZ explicitly as a bifunctional fusion protein: the C-terminal hydratase domain cleaves the oxepin ring to a highly reactive aldehyde and the N-terminal NADP+-ALDH domain oxidises that aldehyde to 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA.

direction_conflict.note: This ModelSEED entry covers only the hydrolase half of the bifunctional enzyme; the reactive semialdehyde it produces is immediately consumed by PaaZ's own ALDH domain (otherwise it cyclises to a dead-end tropone precursor), so the ring-opening is pulled forward in vivo and never runs backwards.

reactions.name: farnesal reductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00900 (Terpenoid backbone biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: NAD(P)-dependent farnesol dehydrogenase / farnesal reductase (SDR-family)
reactions.organism_context: Characterised as NADP+-farnesol dehydrogenase in Helicoverpa armigera (juvenile-hormone pathway) and NAD(P)+-farnesol dehydrogenase in Polygonum minus; the reductase running the opposite direction is a separate SDR
reactions.rationale: The ModelSEED entry carries no EC and no cofactor, so the catalyst is inferred from the chemistry; the characterised farnesol/farnesal oxidoreductases are single-activity short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase enzymes.

direction_conflict.note: The equation drops NAD(P)+/NAD(P)H entirely (ModelSEED flags charge imbalance -2, i.e. the missing hydride), so the direction here is set by the pyridine-nucleotide pool and by which of the two distinct enzymes (dehydrogenase vs reductase) is present, not by any one protein.

reactions.name: carbamoyl-phosphate:ansamitocinoside-P-3 carbamoyltransferase
reactions.reaction: (1) Carbamoylphosphate[0] + (1) Ansamitocinoside P-3[0] <= (1) Phosphate[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) 4''-O-Carbamoyl ansamitocinoside P-3[0]
pathways: KEGG: rn01051 (Biosynthesis of ansamycins); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: Ansamitocin carbamoyltransferase Asm21
reactions.organism_context: Actinosynnema pretiosum (ansamitocin/ansamitocinoside post-PKS tailoring)
reactions.rationale: Asm21 carbamoylates two different hydroxyls (C-7 of the polyketide core and the 4''-OH of the glucosyl moiety), but that is one carbamoyl-transfer activity used iteratively on two acceptors, which is promiscuity/iteration rather than a second catalytic activity (compare the homodimeric iterative CTase GdmN).

direction_conflict.note: Carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl phosphate releases inorganic phosphate from a high-energy mixed anhydride, so the biosynthetic (carbamoylating) direction is effectively irreversible.

reactions.name: UDP-glycogen synthase
pathways: MetaCyc: Carbohydrates-Biosynthesis (Carbohydrate Biosynthesis); Cell-Structure-Biosynthesis (Cell Structure Biosynthesis); GLYCOGEN-BIOSYN (Glycogen and Starch Biosynthesis); Glycan-Biosynthesis (Glycan Biosynthesis); Glycan-Pathways (Glycan Pathways); PLANT-CELL-STRUCTURE (Plant Cell Structures); PRIMARY-CELL-WALL (Primary Cell Wall); PWY-1001 (cellulose biosynthesis); PWY-5067 (glycogen biosynthesis II (from UDP-D-Glucose)); PWY-5936 (xyloglucan biosynthesis); PWY-6773 (1,3-β-D-glucan biosynthesis); Polysaccharides-Biosynthesis (Polysaccharide Biosynthesis); SECONDARY-CELL-WALL (Secondary Cell Wall)
reactions.enzyme_name: Glycogen (starch) synthase, UDP-glucose:glycogen 4-alpha-D-glucosyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Bacteria (GlgA) and eukaryotes (GYS). Note the ModelSEED entry lumps four ECs - 2.4.1.11 glycogen synthase, 2.4.1.12 cellulose synthase, 2.4.1.34 1,3-beta-glucan synthase, 2.4.1.168 xyloglucan glucosyltransferase - each of which is itself a separate single-activity glucosyltransferase.
reactions.rationale: Glycogen synthase is a single-activity retaining glycosyltransferase; chain branching is done by a different protein (GlgB/GBE) and glycogenin's self-glucosylation is a different gene product, so neither makes GlgA/GYS bifunctional. Called from established biochemistry rather than a dedicated literature search.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED reduced the reaction to 'UDP-glucose -> UDP' and lost the glucan acceptor (status MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5), so the stored dG is for a half-reaction; glucosyl transfer from UDP-glucose onto the growing glucan is strongly exergonic and one-way (glycogen breakdown goes via phosphorylase, not by reversal).

reactions.name: (S)-coclaurine-N-methyltransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: ALKALOIDS-SYN (Alkaloid Biosynthesis); ISOQUINOLINE-ALKALOIDS (Isoquinoline and Benzylisoquinoline Alkaloid Biosynthesis); N-CONTAINING-SECONDARY-CMPD-SYN (Nitrogen-Containing Secondary Compound Biosynthesis); PWY-3581 ((S)-reticuline biosynthesis I); S-Reticuline-Biosynthesis ((S)-reticuline biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: (S)-Coclaurine N-methyltransferase (CNMT)
reactions.organism_context: Coptis japonica, Papaver somniferum and other benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid-producing plants
reactions.rationale: CNMT is a single-activity SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase; cloning/purification and the crystal structure describe one catalytic site and one (broad-substrate) methyl-transfer activity, with no demethylase or other second activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent N-methylation with release of S-adenosylhomocysteine is essentially irreversible; the reverse (SAH + N-methylcoclaurine -> SAM + coclaurine) is not an activity of this enzyme.

reactions.name: phytochelatin synthase
pathways: MetaCyc: Detoxification (Detoxification); PWY-6745 (phytochelatins biosynthesis); PWY-6841 (homophytochelatin biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: Phytochelatin synthase (glutathione gamma-glutamylcysteinyltransferase, PCS1/CAD1)
distinct_activities: gamma-glutamylcysteine transpeptidation onto glutathione/phytochelatin acceptors (phytochelatin synthesis, EC 2.3.2.15)
papain-like cysteine-peptidase processing (deglycination) of glutathione S-conjugates
reactions.organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis PCS1/CAD1), algae, some invertebrates and Schistosoma mansoni; the cyanobacterial homologue NsPCS (Nostoc) retains only the peptidase activity and cannot make phytochelatins
reactions.rationale: One papain-like catalytic-Cys domain carries both the gamma-Glu-Cys transpeptidation that builds phytochelatins and a distinct hydrolytic processing of glutathione S-conjugates in xenobiotic metabolism; both are genuine catalysis (not moonlighting), though they share the same nucleophile, which is why I call this medium rather than high.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED collapsed the reaction to 'GSH -> glycine' and dropped the gamma-Glu-Cys acceptor (status MI:C:-8/H:-10/N:-2/O:-4/S:-1), so no direction can be read from the stored thermodynamics; the enzyme runs in the glycine-releasing, phytochelatin-forming direction.

reactions.name: Peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase
pathways: MetaCyc: Antibiotic-Resistance (Antibiotic Resistance); Cell-Structure-Biosynthesis (Cell Structure Biosynthesis); Cell-Wall-Biosynthesis (Cell Wall Biosynthesis); Detoxification (Detoxification); PWY-5265 (peptidoglycan biosynthesis II (staphylococci)); PWY-6385 (peptidoglycan biosynthesis III (mycobacteria)); PWY-6470 (peptidoglycan biosynthesis V (β-lactam resistance)); PWY-6471 (peptidoglycan biosynthesis IV (Enterococcus faecium)); Peptidoglycan-Biosynthesis (Peptidoglycan Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: Peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase of a class A penicillin-binding protein (PBP1a/PBP1b)
reactions.organism_context: Class A PBPs of E. coli, S. aureus, enterococci etc. carry both activities on one chain. The same EC 2.4.1.129 step is also catalysed by genuinely monofunctional GT51 glycosyltransferases (MtgA/MGT) and by the unrelated SEDS polymerases RodA/FtsW, so the reaction is not intrinsically bifunctional.
reactions.rationale: The dominant catalysts of lipid II polymerisation in most bacteria are class A PBPs, single polypeptides with an N-terminal GT51 glycosyltransferase domain and a C-terminal transpeptidase domain - two distinct catalytic activities, not a multi-subunit complex.

direction_conflict.note: The growing glycan acceptor is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-39/H:-63/N:-8/O:-19), leaving only 'lipid II -> undecaprenyl-PP'; polymerisation with release of undecaprenyl-pyrophosphate is irreversible, and depolymerisation is done by unrelated lytic transglycosylases.

reactions.name: dolichylpyrophosphate:polyphosphate phosphotransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: Dolichyl-diphosphate:polyphosphate phosphotransferase (EC 2.7.4.20) - catalysing protein not identified
reactions.rationale: I could find no literature identifying a protein for EC 2.7.4.20 in PubMed or Europe PMC; the well-characterised activity that converts Dol-PP to Dol-P is a dolichyl-pyrophosphate phosphatase (DOLPP1/CWH8-type) that releases free Pi rather than transferring it onto polyphosphate, so the enzyme behind this specific entry is genuinely unknown and I am not defaulting it to monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The polyphosphate phosphate acceptor is absent (status MI:H:-1/O:-3/P:-1), which is why both estimators return a ~208 kJ/mol dG; whatever runs it, dolichyl-PP is dephosphorylated to dolichyl-P to recycle the glycan carrier, never the reverse.

reactions.name: RXN-11086.c
pathways: MetaCyc: AURONE-SYN (Aurone Biosynthesis); FLAVONOID-SYN (Flavonoid Biosynthesis); PHENYLPROPANOID-SYN (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Biosynthesis); PWY-6401 (hispidol and hispidol 4'-O-β-D-glucoside biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)

reactions.name: CYSTATHIONASE-RXN.c
reactions.enzyme_name: PLP-dependent gamma-family cystathionine lyase/synthase running gamma-replacement with water (cystathionine gamma-lyase CTH/CGL, or cystathionine gamma-synthase MetB)
reactions.rationale: The stoichiometry here (cystathionine + H2O -> cysteine + homoserine) is a gamma-replacement by water, not the canonical gamma-lyase reaction (which gives 2-oxobutanoate + ammonia), so the catalyst is inferred from chemistry rather than confirmed; every gamma-family PLP enzyme that could run it (CGL, CGS, CBL) is a single-activity homotetramer with one PLP site per subunit.

direction_conflict.note: The real reaction is O2-dependent (sterol + O2 + NAD(P)H -> 22-ene sterol + 2 H2O + NAD(P)+); writing it as a bare, mass-balanced NADP+ dehydrogenation removes the O2 that makes it irreversible and lets the DeltaG favour the (nonexistent) reductive direction.

reactions.name: RXN-5984
reactions.enzyme_name: Biotin synthase (BioB)
reactions.organism_context: Radical SAM [4Fe-4S]/[2Fe-2S] homodimer; characterised in E. coli, conserved in plants (Arabidopsis BIO2).
reactions.rationale: 9-Mercaptodethiobiotin is the established, kinetically competent intermediate of the single BioB active site, formed by 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical abstraction at C9 of dethiobiotin and sulfur donation from the enzyme's own auxiliary cluster; one catalytic activity only.

direction_conflict.note: SAM, 5'-deoxyadenosine, methionine and the sacrificial [2Fe-2S] sulfur are all absent, with free elemental S standing in for the cluster sulfide; the irreversible SAM cleavage that fixes the direction is exactly what the equation deletes.

reactions.name: RXN-8037
reactions.enzyme_name: None assigned - lactonization of cis-2-hydroxycinnamate (2-coumarinate) to coumarin; the enzymatic route in plants runs through COUMARIN SYNTHASE (COSY) on the CoA thioester, not the free acid
reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis (DF_Athaliana model). COSY is a BAHD-family protein that performs trans-cis isomerization followed by lactonization on o-hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA thioesters; the free-acid lactonization written here proceeds partly spontaneously and is light-catalysed.
reactions.rationale: No enzyme is assigned to the free-acid cyclisation of 2-coumarinate to coumarin; Vanholme et al. show the conversion happens partially spontaneously and that the enzymatic (COSY) route uses the CoA thioester, so there is no mono/bi/poly answer for this entry.

direction_conflict.note: Lactonization releases water, which the equation omits (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:1); with no enzyme at all the direction is set by the irreversible ring closure, not by enzymology.

reactions.name: RXN-8335
reactions.enzyme_name: None assigned - lactonization of 3,4,6-trihydroxy-cis-cinnamate to esculetin; enzymatic counterpart is COUMARIN SYNTHASE (COSY) acting on the CoA thioester
reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis (DF_Athaliana model). Recombinant COSY makes umbelliferone, esculetin and scopoletin from the corresponding o-hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA thioesters; the free-acid cyclisation is partly spontaneous and light-catalysed.
reactions.rationale: Same chemistry as rxn30941 with the 3,4,6-trihydroxy substrate giving esculetin; the free-acid lactonization carries no EC assignment and proceeds non-enzymatically, so functionality cannot honestly be called mono- or bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The water released on lactone formation is missing (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:1), so the +45 to +89 kJ/mol used to call the reaction reverse is not the DeltaG of the real cyclisation.

reactions.name: RXN-8352
reactions.enzyme_name: Sterol C-22 desaturase (cytochrome P450 CYP710A)
reactions.organism_context: Plant microsomal P450; the 24-epi-campesterol -> brassicasterol C22 desaturation is the CYP710A reaction on the C28 sterol, paralleling sitosterol -> stigmasterol. Its NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase partner is a separate polypeptide.
reactions.rationale: Single-activity cytochrome P450 sterol 22-desaturase; the second protein it requires is a distinct reductase, so the multi-subunit exclusion applies rather than bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: As in rxn30827, O2 and the two product waters are deleted and the reaction is written as a reversible NADP+ dehydrogenation, which is what lets eQuilibrator score the physiologically impossible reductive direction as favourable.

reactions.name: RXN0-723
reactions.enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
reactions.organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-723 (E. coli NrdD). NrdD needs the separate activase NrdG to install its glycyl radical - two polypeptides, a complex rather than a fused bifunctional enzyme. Class Ia RNR (R1/R2) is likewise two chains and works at the diphosphate level.
reactions.rationale: CTP -> dCTP is the nucleoside-triphosphate-level ribonucleotide reduction run by class II/III RNRs; the catalytic polypeptide carries one activity, with radical generation delegated to a separate activase subunit.

direction_conflict.note: The external reductant (formate for NrdD, thioredoxin/NrdH for NrdJ) and the water product are both absent (status MI:O:-1); ribonucleotide reduction is irreversible, so the reverse call is an artefact of the missing redox partner.

reactions.name: RXN0-724
reactions.enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
reactions.organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-724 (E. coli NrdD, UTP -> dUTP). NrdD plus its separate NrdG activase is a two-protein system, not a fused bifunctional chain.
reactions.rationale: Same single-activity ribonucleotide reductase chemistry as rxn30989 on the uridine nucleotide; no second catalytic activity on the polypeptide.

direction_conflict.note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1); the 2'-deoxygenation is irreversible in vivo.

reactions.name: RXN0-745
reactions.enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
reactions.organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-745 (E. coli NrdD, ATP -> dATP). NrdD/NrdG are separate polypeptides.
reactions.rationale: Single-activity ribonucleotide reductase acting at the triphosphate level; allosteric specificity and activity sites are regulatory, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1); dNTP formation never runs backwards.

reactions.name: RXN0-746
reactions.enzyme_name: Ribonucleoside-triphosphate reductase (class III anaerobic NrdD; class II NrdJ in other lineages)
reactions.organism_context: EcoCyc reaction RXN0-746 (E. coli NrdD, GTP -> dGTP). NrdD/NrdG are separate polypeptides.
reactions.rationale: Same single-activity NTP-level ribonucleotide reduction as the other three RXN0-72x/74x entries.

direction_conflict.note: Reductant and water product stripped (status MI:O:-1), removing the irreversibility that fixes the forward direction.

reactions.name: THYKI-RXN
reactions.enzyme_name: Thymidine kinase (TK1/tdk)
reactions.organism_context: Cellular (plant/bacterial/human) thymidine kinases are single-activity. Herpesviral TKs are the exception: HSV-1 TK and HHV-8 ORF21 carry both thymidine kinase and thymidylate kinase activity on one chain, i.e. genuinely bifunctional in that viral lineage.
reactions.rationale: The substrate pair (ATP + thymidine) identifies thymidine kinase; cellular TK1-type enzymes have one catalytic activity, and the dual TK/TMP-kinase chain is restricted to herpesviruses.

direction_conflict.note: The product is mis-mapped to thiamine phosphate (cpd00793) instead of thymidine 5'-monophosphate, a 2C/2N/1S error (status MI:C:2/H:2/N:2/O:-4/S:1); ATP-driven phosphoryl transfer is effectively irreversible forward regardless of what the bogus DeltaG says.

reactions.name: COX10 (CYTOCHROME C OXIDASE 10); prenyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: Heme O synthase / protoheme IX farnesyltransferase (COX10, CyoE/CtaB)
reactions.organism_context: Polytopic inner-membrane/mitochondrial-inner-membrane prenyltransferase of the UbiA superfamily; COX10 in eukaryotes, CyoE/CtaB in bacteria.
reactions.rationale: A single intramembrane prenyl-transfer activity (EC 2.5.1.141) that farnesylates the C2 vinyl of heme B; its role in cytochrome oxidase assembly is a pathway role, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Both co-substrates (farnesyl diphosphate, H2O) and the diphosphate product are missing - KEGG R07411 is Heme + H2O + FPP <=> Heme O + PPi, while ModelSEED has only Heme <=> Heme O (status MI:C:15/H:26/O:1); PPi release is what makes the prenyl transfer irreversible.

reactions.name: R_2_Hydroxyethylenedicarboxylate_carboxy_lyase__pyruvate_forming_
reactions.enzyme_name: Oxaloacetate (enol form) decarboxylase - EC left at 4.1.1.- by KEGG R00219; enol-oxaloacetate decarboxylation is largely spontaneous/metal-catalysed
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R00219. The named oxaloacetate decarboxylases are either a soluble Mg2+-dependent single-activity enzyme (EC 4.1.1.3) or the Na+-pumping OadABC membrane complex - separate polypeptides, so the complex exclusion applies there.
reactions.rationale: KEGG assigns no EC beyond 4.1.1.- to the enol-oxaloacetate (2-hydroxyethylenedicarboxylate) decarboxylation, and the uncatalysed reaction is fast, so the catalysing protein for this specific entry cannot be identified.

direction_conflict.note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide (KEGG C00237), not the CO2 (C00011) of KEGG R00219 - status MI:O:-1 - so the DeltaG that produced the carboxylating reverse call is computed on the wrong product; decarboxylation of oxaloacetate is strongly downhill and carboxylation of pyruvate requires ATP or PEP.

reactions.name: R_R01652_c
reactions.enzyme_name: None - KEGG flags R01652 as spontaneous decarboxylation of 2-isopropyl-3-oxosuccinate following 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (LeuB, EC 1.1.1.85)
reactions.organism_context: Leucine biosynthesis; soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R01652. The oxidative step before it is run by monofunctional 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase.
reactions.rationale: KEGG's own COMMENT reads 'spontaneous (following EC 1.1.1.85 or R04426 reaction)' - the beta-keto acid decarboxylates without a catalyst, so there is no enzyme to classify.

direction_conflict.note: KEGG disowns the step as non-enzymatic, and ModelSEED additionally writes the product as CO (cpd00204) rather than CO2 (status MI:O:-1); spontaneous beta-keto decarboxylation runs only toward 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoate.

reactions.name: R__R__Mevalonate_NADP__oxidoreductase__CoA_acylating_
reactions.reaction: (2) NADPH[0] + (27) H+[0] + (9) HMG-CoA[0] <= (2) NADP[0] + (9) CoA[0] + (2) Mevalonic acid[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase (HMGR, EC 1.1.1.34)
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563): plant class-I HMGR is a single-activity reductase (its membrane sterol-sensing anchor is regulatory, not catalytic - a moonlighting-type role that is excluded). In Enterococcus faecalis and related Gram-positives the orthologue MvaE is a genuinely fused dual-function acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase/HMG-CoA reductase polypeptide, i.e. bifunctional in that lineage.
reactions.rationale: The plant/animal enzyme carries only the NADPH-dependent four-electron reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate; the bifunctional thiolase/reductase fusion is a bacterial variant (Hedl et al.).

direction_conflict.note: The stoichiometry is garbled - 9 HMG-CoA and 9 CoA against 2 mevalonate, 2 NADPH and 27 H+ (status MI:C:-42/H:-70/O:-28, CI:-18) - so the ~640-1263 kJ/mol used to call it reverse is meaningless; HMGR is the committed, physiologically irreversible step toward mevalonate.

reactions.name: R_zeta_Carotene__hydrogen_donor_oxygen_oxidoreductase
reactions.enzyme_name: zeta-Carotene desaturase (ZDS/CrtQ in plants and cyanobacteria; CrtI-type phytoene desaturase in bacteria and fungi)
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) - plant plastid ZDS, a single FAD-dependent desaturase that passes electrons to plastoquinone. Bacterial/fungal CrtI performs three or four successive desaturations, but these are iterations of the same activity, not distinct catalytic activities.
reactions.rationale: Purified higher-plant zeta-carotene desaturase carries out the zeta-carotene -> neurosporene -> lycopene desaturations as one activity with a quinone/O2 acceptor; iterative turnover is not polyfunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: KEGG R04798 is zeta-carotene + reduced acceptor + O2 <=> neurosporene + 2 H2O + acceptor; ModelSEED replaces the acceptor/O2 couple with free H2, deleting the oxidative driving force that makes desaturation irreversible.

reactions.name: R_R04885_c
reactions.enzyme_name: None assigned - KEGG R04885 leaves the EC at 4.1.1.-; in eumelanogenesis 5,6-dihydroxyindole arises by spontaneous decarboxylative rearrangement of dopachrome, while dopachrome tautomerase (DCT/TYRP2) diverts the flux to DHICA instead
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R04885. Dopachrome tautomerase, the one characterised enzyme on this branch, is a monofunctional binuclear-copper/zinc tyrosinase-family protein - but it makes DHICA, not the DHI written here.
reactions.rationale: No enzyme is assigned to decarboxylation of leucodopachrome (cyclodopa) to DHI; the comparable step in melanin synthesis is the spontaneous decarboxylative tautomerization of dopachrome, so the catalysing protein for this entry cannot be named.

direction_conflict.note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide, not the CO2 of KEGG R04885 (status MI:H:-1/O:-1, CI:2); loss of CO2 with aromatization is irreversible either way.

reactions.name: R_R05376_c
reactions.enzyme_name: None assigned - decarboxylation of bis(4-chlorophenyl)acetate (DDA) to bis(4-chlorophenyl)methane (DDM) in DDT catabolism; KEGG R05376 leaves the EC at 4.1.1.-
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG R05376, a DDT-degradation step with no characterised protein; DDA is normally reported as a terminal DDT metabolite rather than as a substrate of a named decarboxylase.
reactions.rationale: No decarboxylase has been assigned to this step in the literature or in KEGG, so neither the protein nor its functionality can be established.

direction_conflict.note: cpd00204 is carbon monoxide rather than the CO2 of KEGG R05376 (status MI:H:2/O:-1, CI:2); the dGPredictor +46 kJ/mol behind the reverse call is therefore for the wrong reaction.

reactions.name: R_R07733_c
reactions.enzyme_name: Isoflavone 7-O-glucoside beta-glucosidase (isoflavone conjugate-hydrolysing beta-glucosidase, GH1/GH3)
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563); the apoplast-localised soybean ICHG hydrolyses isoflavone 7-O-glucosides such as ononin and daidzin to the aglycones. KEGG's COMMENT on R07733 reads 'isoflavone glucoside glucosidase'.
reactions.rationale: A single-activity retaining glycoside hydrolase removing the 7-O-glucose from ononin to give formononetin; glycoside hydrolases of this family carry one catalytic activity (broad substrate tolerance is not bifunctionality).

direction_conflict.note: Both the water substrate and the glucose product are absent and the stoichiometry is garbled (8 ononin against 11 formononetin + 11 H+; status MI:H:-44/O:-28), so the ~614-1097 kJ/mol driving the reverse call is not the DeltaG of a glucoside hydrolysis - which is irreversible in the hydrolytic direction.

reactions.name: R_R07916_c
reactions.enzyme_name: Phytoene synthase (PSY/CrtB, EC 2.5.1.32)
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) - plant plastid PSY is a standalone single-activity synthase. In many fungi the orthologue is a fused bifunctional phytoene synthase/lycopene cyclase on one chain (Xanthophyllomyces/Phaffia CrtYB, Rhodosporidium crtYB, Neurospora AL-2), which would be bifunctional in that lineage.
reactions.rationale: PSY condenses two GGPP via prephytoene diphosphate to 15-cis-phytoene; the two chemical steps run in one active site and are a single activity, whereas the fungal CrtYB fusion adds a genuinely separate cyclase activity.

direction_conflict.note: Both diphosphate products are missing (status MI:H:-2/O:-14/P:-4, CI:6), which is what inflates DeltaG to ~885 kJ/mol and flips the call; PPi release makes prenyl condensation irreversible. KEGG also tags R07916 'multistep reaction (see R02065+R07270)', but both steps belong to the one PSY polypeptide.

reactions.name: R_R08122_c
reactions.enzyme_name: None firmly assigned - aromatization of 2-fluoro-cis,cis-1,2-dihydroxycyclohexa-3,5-diene-1-carboxylate to catechol with loss of CO2 and fluoride; the upstream 2-halobenzoate 1,2-dioxygenase is a multi-component oxygenase/reductase system and KEGG leaves R08122 at EC 1.3.1.-
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) via KEGG's fluorobenzoate degradation map; the characterised bacterial 2-halobenzoate 1,2-dioxygenases of Pseudomonas cepacia 2CBS and P. aeruginosa 142 are two- or three-component systems (separate oxygenase and reductase polypeptides), so the complex exclusion applies to them in any case.
reactions.rationale: The dihydrodiol-carboxylate produced by halobenzoate dioxygenation eliminates CO2 and halide to catechol spontaneously or via an unassigned dehydrogenase; no single protein can be named for this entry.

direction_conflict.note: CO2 and fluoride are both absent and the stoichiometry is garbled (6 diol-carboxylate against 7 catechol; status MI:F:-6/O:-10); aromatization with CO2 and HF loss is irreversible.

reactions.name: R_R08589_c
reactions.enzyme_name: 1,4-Dihydroxy-6-naphthoate synthase (MqnD; also called 5,8-dihydroxy-2-naphthoate synthase, EC 4.1.99.29)
reactions.organism_context: Futalosine/modified-futalosine pathway to menaquinone in Helicobacter, Campylobacter, Streptomyces and Thermus; the entry reaches the soybean model (iRS1563) through KEGG R08589.
reactions.rationale: MqnD performs the single retro-aldol/aromatization step converting cyclic dehypoxanthine futalosine to the dihydroxynaphthoate with release of dihydroxyacetone; one catalytic activity on one chain.

direction_conflict.note: The dihydroxyacetone (glycerone) co-product is dropped and the stoichiometry is garbled (12 substrate against 14 product + 25 H+; status MI:C:-14/H:-33/O:-28, CI:23), so the ~753-1387 kJ/mol behind the reverse call is not this reaction's DeltaG; aromatization makes it irreversible forward.

reactions.name: R_Light_rxn_1
reactions.enzyme_name: No single enzyme - lumped photosynthetic linear electron flow (photosystem II, cytochrome b6f, photosystem I, ferredoxin and ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase)
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) thylakoid light reaction; each participating photosystem is itself a many-subunit pigment-protein complex, so even per complex the multi-subunit exclusion applies.
reactions.rationale: Water oxidation to O2, transthylakoid proton translocation and NADP+ reduction are carried out by four separate membrane complexes driven by photons; no single polypeptide catalyses the written reaction, so no mono/bi/poly call is possible.

direction_conflict.note: The equation is mass-balanced but omits its energy source - light - so the +90 to +108 kJ/mol all three thermodynamic sources report is exactly the photon input, and reading that as 'reverse' would have the chloroplast consuming O2 and NADPH to make water.

reactions.name: R_Glyceroltripalmitate_synthesis_c
reactions.enzyme_name: No single enzyme - model lump for triacylglycerol assembly, which in vivo runs on acyl-CoA via GPAT, LPAAT, phosphatidate phosphatase and acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase (DGAT); direct esterification of free palmitate with glycerol is only a lipase reaction run in reverse
reactions.organism_context: Soybean model (iRS1563) storage-lipid pseudo-reaction; DGAT, the committed step of the real route, is a monofunctional membrane acyltransferase but it acylates diacylglycerol with palmitoyl-CoA, not glycerol with free palmitate.
reactions.rationale: Four distinct acyltransferase/phosphatase steps on CoA thioesters are collapsed into one condensation of free fatty acid with glycerol, so no single enzyme catalyses the equation as written.

direction_conflict.note: Only one palmitate is written for a tri-palmitoyl product (status MI:C:32/H:65/O:4, CI:1), which is what produces dGPredictor's +496 kJ/mol and the reverse call; net flux in an oilseed is toward triacylglycerol, but note that the only enzyme that really acts on this substrate set, a lipase, would run the hydrolytic direction ModelSEED chose.

reactions.name: pyruvate carboxy-lyase (acetaldehyde-forming)
reactions.enzyme_name: Pyruvate decarboxylase (thiamine-diphosphate-dependent)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae PDC1/5/6; Zymomonas mobilis pdc; widespread in fungi, plants and fermentative bacteria
reactions.rationale: KEGG R00224 (EC 4.1.1.1) is plain ThDP-dependent pyruvate decarboxylase, a single catalytic activity; its acyloin/carboligase side reaction is active-site promiscuity at the same ThDP centre, not a second domain. Called from established knowledge plus the KEGG entry (COMMENT: 'TPP-dependent enzymatic reaction').

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED carries an orphan ADP on the pyruvate side (status MI:C:-10/H:-12/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2 = one ADP, CI:3); that phantom nucleotide is what inflates dG to ~450 kJ/mol and produces the reverse call, while the real decarboxylation is irreversible forward.

reactions.name: phenylpyruvate carboxy-lyase (phenylacetaldehyde-forming)
reactions.enzyme_name: Phenylpyruvate decarboxylase (ThDP-dependent 2-oxo-acid decarboxylase)
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Aro10p (Ehrlich pathway); Azospirillum/Enterobacter ipdC-type decarboxylases; KEGG ortholog K12732
reactions.rationale: KEGG R01377 (EC 4.1.1.43 / 4.1.1.-, ortholog K12732 'phenylpyruvate decarboxylase') is a single-activity ThDP decarboxylase of the PDC/IPDC family; no fused second catalytic domain is described for this family. Identity taken from the KEGG ortholog assignment rather than a dedicated characterisation paper.

direction_conflict.note: Same orphan-ADP artefact as rxn31646 (MI = one ADP); CO2-releasing 2-oxo-acid decarboxylation does not run backwards.

reactions.name: Monophenol,L-dopa:oxygen oxidoreductase
reactions.enzyme_name: Tyrosinase / polyphenol oxidase (monophenol monooxygenase)
reactions.organism_context: Fungal (Agaricus bisporus PPO), plant and animal (mammalian TYR) tyrosinases; KEGG assigns ortholog K00505 (tyrosinase) to R02383, COMMENT 'tyramine monooxygenase'
reactions.rationale: The ModelSEED name is literally the EC 1.14.18.1 systematic name and KEGG maps R02383 to tyrosinase; a single tyrosinase polypeptide carries two distinct catalytic activities at one binuclear-copper centre - hydroxylation of monophenols and two-electron oxidation of o-diphenols to quinones. Bifunctional by catalysis, not by moonlighting; the two activities are routinely assayed and inhibited separately.

direction_conflict.note: Both tyrosinase activities are O2-consuming oxidations, so the reverse direction would require the enzyme to evolve O2 - impossible; the reverse call comes from the orphan ADP (MI = one ADP) inflating dG, and NADH here is only a balancing stand-in for the o-diphenol that actually reduces the copper centre.

reactions.name: R02669_c
reactions.enzyme_name: 3-Hydroxyanthranilate decarboxylase (unidentified carboxy-lyase)
reactions.organism_context: KEGG places R02669 in tryptophan metabolism (rn00380); fungal 3-hydroxyanthranilate branches (e.g. Aspergillus terreus salicylate catabolism) are the usual context
reactions.rationale: KEGG R02669 carries only the unassigned EC 4.1.1.-, no ORTHOLOGY entry and no COMMENT, and no characterised protein for 3-hydroxyanthranilate -> 2-aminophenol + CO2 surfaced in the literature search. Honest 'unknown' rather than a guessed mono call.

direction_conflict.note: Orphan ADP again (MI = one ADP, CI:3); whichever protein runs it, aromatic decarboxylation with CO2 release is the biologically observed direction.

reactions.name: R04984_c
reactions.enzyme_name: Coq7 / CLK-1, 5-demethoxyubiquinone (DMQ) hydroxylase
reactions.organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Coq7p (hexaprenyl chain = Q6, matching the substrate named here); C. elegans CLK-1; a flavin-dependent DMQ hydroxylase substitutes in Arabidopsis and UbiF in E. coli
reactions.rationale: The C5 hydroxylation of 2-hexaprenyl-3-methyl-6-methoxy-1,4-benzoquinone is diagnostically the Coq7 step of Q6 biosynthesis; Coq7/CLK-1 is a single carboxylate-bridged di-iron monooxygenase with one catalytic activity. Enzyme identity inferred from the chemistry and prenyl-chain length - KEGG no longer serves R04984 (the entry returns empty), so there is no ortholog assignment to confirm against.

direction_conflict.note: Orphan ADP (MI:C:-10/H:-13/N:-5/O:-10/P:-2, CI:2) drives the reverse call; an O2/NAD(P)H-consuming hydroxylation is irreversible forward.

reactions.name: 3-octaprenyl-4-hydroxybenzoate carboxy-lyase
reactions.enzyme_name: UbiD, 4-hydroxy-3-polyprenylbenzoate decarboxylase (prenylated-FMN dependent)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli UbiD (octaprenyl chain matches); prFMN cofactor is supplied in trans by the separate flavin prenyltransferase UbiX (EC 2.5.1.129, KEGG K03186)
reactions.rationale: KEGG R04986 assigns EC 4.1.1.98 / K03182 (UbiD). UbiD carries one catalytic activity; UbiX is a distinct polypeptide that only matures the prFMN cofactor, so this is a two-protein cofactor relationship, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.

reactions.reaction: (1) NADH[0] + (1) O2[0] + (1) ADP[0] + (1) Phenylacetic acid[0] <= (1) H2O[0] + (1) NAD[0] + (1) 2-Hydroxyphenylacetate[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: PhacA, cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (phenylacetate 2-hydroxylase, EC 1.14.14.54)

reactions.name: coproporphyrinogen I oxidase
reactions.reaction: (1) NADP[0] + (1) CoproporphyrinogenI[0] <= (1) NADPH[0] + (6) H+[0] + (1) Coproporphyrin I[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: no dedicated enzyme known; coproporphyrinogen I is a type-I shunt product that aromatises to coproporphyrin I, and the characterised oxidase CgoX/HemY is defined on the III isomer
reactions.organism_context: type-I porphyrinogen shunt; no organism has a described coproporphyrinogen I-specific oxidase
reactions.rationale: Coproporphyrinogen I is the dead-end isomer of the porphyrin pathway and its conversion to coproporphyrin I is not assigned to any characterised protein (it occurs largely by autoxidation), so the catalysing enzyme cannot be named; whether the Firmicute CgoX accepts the I isomer has not been established.

direction_conflict.note: Both the enzymatic (CgoX) and spontaneous routes use O2 as the oxidant and are irreversible aromatisations; ModelSEED substitutes NADP for O2 (and uses one NADP for what is a six-electron oxidation, hence status CI:4), and that substitution is what makes the computed thermodynamics point backwards.

reactions.name: coproporphyrinogen III oxidase
reactions.reaction: (6) NADP[0] + (1) CoproporphyrinogenIII[0] <= (6) NADPH[0] + (6) H+[0] + (1) Coproporphyrin III[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: coproporphyrinogen III oxidase, oxygen-dependent (CgoX, formerly HemY; EC 1.3.3.15)
reactions.organism_context: Firmicutes/Bacillaceae coproporphyrin-dependent heme branch (Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus); an oxygen-independent alternative, CgoN (YtpQ), performs the same step in some species
reactions.rationale: CgoX is a single-chain FAD-dependent oxidase that aromatises coproporphyrinogen III to coproporphyrin III using O2; its reported ability to also oxidise protoporphyrinogen IX is broadened substrate specificity for the identical six-electron aromatisation chemistry, not a second distinct catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The physiological oxidant is O2 (reduced to H2O2), which makes the aromatisation irreversible forward; ModelSEED replaces it with six NADP for a six-electron (three-acceptor) oxidation, leaving status CI:-6, and that bogus redox partner is what produced the reverse call.

reactions.name: Dimethylallyltransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: dimethylallyltranstransferase (geranyl/farnesyl diphosphate synthase; short-chain trans-prenyltransferase), EC 2.5.1.1
reactions.organism_context: plastidial entry (abbreviation rxn365_p) in a plant/algal model; the step is shared by bacterial IspA and plant GPP/FPP synthases
reactions.rationale: The DMAPP + IPP head-to-tail condensation is run by a short-chain trans-prenyltransferase whose successive elongation steps (the EC 2.5.1.1 and EC 2.5.1.10 labels) occur processively in one active site, i.e. one catalytic activity with chain-length scope, not two; genuinely bifunctional terpene synthases are those fusing a prenyltransferase domain to a separate cyclase domain, which this is not.

direction_conflict.note: The product is written as (E)-geranyl monophosphate instead of geranyl diphosphate, so a whole phosphate is missing (ModelSEED status MI:H:-2/O:-3/P:-1); the real condensation releases PPi, which is then hydrolysed, making the forward direction effectively irreversible and ModelSEED's reverse call wrong.

reactions.name: phenylacetyl-CoA dehydrogenase
reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) Phenylacetyl-CoA[0] + (2) Vitamin K1[0] <= (1) Phenylglyoxylyl-CoA[0] + (2) Phytonadiol[0]
pathways: MetaCyc: AROMATIC-COMPOUNDS-DEGRADATION (Aromatic Compound Degradation); BENZCOA-PWY (anaerobic aromatic compound degradation (Thauera aromatica)); Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); PWY-1341 (phenylacetate degradation II (anaerobic)); Phenolic-Compounds-Degradation (Phenolic Compound Degradation); Phenylacetate-Degradation (Phenylacetate Degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: phenylacetyl-CoA dehydrogenase / phenylacetyl-CoA:acceptor oxidoreductase (PadBCD), EC 1.17.5.1
reactions.organism_context: Thauera aromatica and Aromatoleum aromaticum; anaerobic (denitrifying) phenylalanine/phenylacetate catabolism to benzoyl-CoA
reactions.rationale: The purified enzyme is a membrane-bound molybdenum-iron-sulfur complex of three separate subunits (93, 27 and 26 kDa), so under the multi-subunit exclusion it counts as monofunctional rather than bifunctional; preparations additionally hydrolyse CoA off phenylglyoxylyl-CoA, but that thioesterase activity was not assigned to a single polypeptide and lies beyond the step written here.

direction_conflict.note: The four-electron alpha-oxidation inserts a water-derived oxygen and is a committed catabolic step with no observed reverse; the reverse call comes from the generic MetaCyc "acceptor" being instantiated as the plant quinone phylloquinone (vitamin K1) rather than the physiological ubiquinone, which is what set the eQuilibrator dG.
