reactions.organism_context: Artemisia annua glandular trichomes (plant ALDH family enzyme of the artemisinin pathway)
reactions.rationale: This is MetaCyc's class-level reaction ALDEHYDE-DEHYDROGENASE-NADORNOP+-RXN expanded combinatorially, so the substrate (11R)-dihydroartemisinic aldehyde (C15H24O, a cyclic sesquiterpenoid) is paired with the unrelated straight-chain fatty acid Pentadecylic acid (C15H29O2-) and the equation is also one hydrogen short - no single protein catalyses it as written. The enzyme that performs the intended aldehyde oxidation, A. annua ALDH1, is a standalone single-activity NAD+ aldehyde dehydrogenase used as a one-step pathway enzyme in every heterologous reconstruction; no second catalytic domain has been reported for it.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED's '<' would make this an NAD(P)H-driven reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde, which no NAD(P)+ aldehyde dehydrogenase does (acid reduction needs an activated acyl group or an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase); the large positive dG that drove the '<' call is an artifact of the mis-paired product, because oxidation of an aldehyde to its own carboxylate is strongly exergonic and mechanistically irreversible.

reactions.name: aldehyde dehydrogenase [NAD(P)+]
reactions.enzyme_name: no enzyme as written; nearest real activity is the soluble NAD+-dependent abietadienal (diterpene aldehyde) dehydrogenase of conifer diterpene resin acid biosynthesis
reactions.organism_context: conifers - soluble ALDH activity demonstrated in Abies grandis and Pinus contorta stem extracts; in Pinus taeda the same C18 oxidation is instead run by the P450 CYP720B1/PtAO
reactions.rationale: Combinatorial expansion of MetaCyc's class-level ALDH reaction has paired the conifer diterpene aldehyde Abietal (C20H30O, tricyclic) with the unrelated straight-chain C20 fatty acid 8,11,14-Icosatrienoate (C20H33O2-), and the equation is one hydrogen short, so no protein catalyses it as written. The nearest genuine catalyst, the soluble NAD+-dependent abietadienal dehydrogenase of Abies grandis, was only ever demonstrated as an activity in cell-free extracts and never cloned, while in pine the same net oxidation is carried out by the multisubstrate P450 CYP720B1 (consecutive oxidations at one active site, not a fused bifunctional enzyme), so the domain architecture of the actual catalyst cannot be settled.

The conifer alternative (CYP720B1) is an O2/NADPH-dependent monooxygenase that is likewise strictly oxidative.

reactions.rationale: Combinatorial expansion of MetaCyc's class-level ALDH reaction has paired the conifer diterpene aldehyde dehydroabietadienal (C20H28O, tricyclic) with the unrelated straight-chain C20 fatty acid 8,11,14-Icosatrienoate (C20H33O2-), and the equation is one hydrogen short, so no protein catalyses it as written. The nearest genuine catalyst, the soluble NAD+-dependent abietadienal dehydrogenase of Abies grandis, was only ever demonstrated as an activity in cell-free extracts and never cloned, while in pine the same net oxidation is carried out by the multisubstrate P450 CYP720B1 (consecutive oxidations at one active site, not a fused bifunctional enzyme), so the domain architecture of the actual catalyst cannot be settled.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED's '<' would make this an NAD(P)H-driven reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde, which no NAD(P)+ aldehyde dehydrogenase does (acid reduction needs an activated acyl group or an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase); the large positive dG that drove the '<' call is an artifact of the mis-paired product, because oxidation of an aldehyde to its own carboxylate is strongly exergonic and mechanistically irreversible. The conifer alternative (CYP720B1) is an O2/NADPH-dependent monooxygenase that is likewise strictly oxidative.

reactions.rationale: No enzyme catalyses this pairing: the entry is a combinatorial instance ("metaexp") of MetaCyc's generic ALDEHYDE-DEHYDROGENASE-NADORNOP+-RXN that turns the tricyclic diterpene aldehyde levopimaradienal (C20H30O) into the unrelated straight-chain fatty acid 11Z, 13Z-eicosadienoate (C20H35O2-), a skeleton change no dehydrogenase performs. The genuine catalysts of levopimaradienal-type oxidation in conifers are a soluble NAD+-dependent diterpene aldehyde dehydrogenase (characterised only in cell-free extracts, never cloned, so its domain architecture is unknown) and the multisubstrate P450 CYP720B1/CYP720B4, whose "multifunctionality" is iterative oxidation of one carbon at a single active site rather than two fused catalytic domains.

direction_conflict.note: Both candidate catalysts run aldehyde -> carboxylate essentially irreversibly and NAD(P)H reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde requires an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call has no enzymological basis, though the mismatched product makes the direction largely moot.

direction_conflict.note: NQO1/WrbA-type enzymes reduce quinones with NADH in a ping-pong mechanism and do not oxidise quinols with NAD(P)+, so ModelSEED's '<' is the non-enzymatic direction.

reactions.name: zeta-carotene desaturase
pathways: MetaCyc: C40-Carotenoids-Biosynthesis (C40 Carotenoid Biosynthesis); CAROTENOID-PWY (superpathway of carotenoid biosynthesis in plants); CAROTENOID-SYN (Carotenoid Biosynthesis); Lycopene-Biosynthesis (Lycopene Biosynthesis); PWY-6475 (trans-lycopene biosynthesis II (oxygenic phototrophs and green sulfur bacteria)); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis); TETRATERPENOID-SYN (Tetraterpenoid Biosynthesis); Terpenoid-Biosynthesis (Terpenoid Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: zeta-carotene desaturase (ZDS / CrtQb), EC 1.3.5.6
reactions.organism_context: Plants (Capsicum annuum, Arabidopsis, maize) and cyanobacteria (Anabaena PCC 7120, Synechocystis PCC 6803).
reactions.rationale: Purified recombinant ZDS from Capsicum and from Anabaena carries one FAD-dependent, quinone-coupled desaturase activity; this entry is 9,9'-di-cis-zeta-carotene -> 7,9,9'-tri-cis-neurosporene (first of the two ZDS desaturations), i.e. the same activity used twice, not two distinct ones. reactions.name: RXN-8289.c.metaexp.CPD-12575

reactions.enzyme_name: flavonol 3-O-glucoside 2''-O-beta-D-glucosyltransferase (UGT79B6 in Arabidopsis, UGT79B31 in Petunia), EC 2.4.1.239
reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (AraCyc RXN-8289, kaempferol glycoside biosynthesis); orthologue UGT79B31 in Petunia hybrida; the pea (Pisum sativum) triglucoside route uses three separate glucosyltransferases.
reactions.rationale: Arabidopsis ugt79b6 mutants lack exactly this product (kaempferol/quercetin 3-O-glucosyl(1->2)glucosides) and are complemented by Petunia UGT79B31, a single-domain family-1 UGT with one glycosyl-transfer activity; in pea the successive glucosylations are run by three separate enzymes rather than one multifunctional protein. The written equation is otherwise sound, carrying only a spurious product-side H+ (1 H / 1 charge unit), which does not affect the direction call.

direction_conflict.note: UDP-sugar glycosyl transfer is pulled forward by UDP release and is effectively irreversible toward the glucoside, so ModelSEED's '<' (diglucoside + UDP regenerating UDP-glucose) is not the enzymatic direction.

reactions.name: phenylacetaldoxime hydrolase
reactions.reaction: (2) H2O[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) (Z)-Phenylacetaldehyde oxime[0] <= (1) NH3[0] + (1) H2O2[0] + (1) alpha-Tolualdehyde[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified - no characterised 'phenylacetaldoxime hydrolase' exists
reactions.organism_context: AraCyc RXN-13537 (Arabidopsis thaliana); the only enzymes KEGG associates with (Z)-phenylacetaldoxime (C16075) are aldoxime dehydratase (EC 4.8.1.4, giving phenylacetonitrile) and CYP79/CYP71 P450s.
reactions.rationale: No protein has been shown to hydrolyse phenylacetaldoxime to phenylacetaldehyde: in planta PAOx is consumed by aldoxime dehydratase / CYP71 enzymes to the nitrile en route to phenylacetic acid, and KEGG lists no reaction matching this entry. The written products are also chemically fabricated - ammonium plus H2O2 generated from water is a disproportionation no enzyme performs; a genuine oxime hydrolysis would release hydroxylamine, and an oxidase-type deamination would consume O2.

direction_conflict.note: Aldoximes are made from amino acids by CYP79s and consumed downstream, never assembled from an aldehyde plus ammonium and peroxide, so ModelSEED's '<' is biologically impossible whatever the written dG says; the +54 to +62 kJ/mol comes entirely from the fictitious water -> H2O2 oxidation standing in for O2.

reactions.name: RXNBWI-10.c
reactions.reaction: (1) L-Glutamine[0] + (1) Glycerone-phosphate[0] + (1) D-Ribulose5-phosphate[0] <= (1) Pyridoxal phosphate[0] + (1) L-Glutamate[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: pyridoxal 5'-phosphate synthase, synthase subunit Pdx1/PdxS (EC 4.3.3.6), working with the glutaminase subunit Pdx2/PdxT (EC 3.5.1.2)
reactions.organism_context: DXP-independent vitamin B6 pathway of most bacteria, archaea, fungi, plants and apicomplexans; Pdx1 and Pdx2 assemble into a 12:12 complex (Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, Methanosarcina acetivorans, Plasmodium).
reactions.rationale: The definition (glutamine + a triose phosphate + a pentose phosphate -> PLP + glutamate) is the PLP synthase reaction, and Pdx1 accepts Ru5P/DHAP as well as R5P/G3P; the glutaminase activity sits on the separate Pdx2 polypeptide of the complex, which per protocol is a multi-subunit complex and not a fused bifunctional chain. Pdx1 itself runs a long multi-step imine chemistry across two sites (P1/P2) but has a single overall catalytic activity, and the entry's EC 2.4.2.- is a mis-assignment.

direction_conflict.note: PLP synthase is a committed biosynthetic enzyme whose glutamine hydrolysis and imine chemistry make it irreversible, so ModelSEED's '<' (PLP + glutamate regenerating glutamine, DHAP and Ru5P) has no enzymatic basis; the product side is also missing Pi and 3 H2O (8 H, 7 O, 1 P short).

reactions.name: RXNBWI-17.d
reactions.enzyme_name: NAD+ kinase (NadK / PpnK; human NADK and mitochondrial NADK2), EC 2.7.1.23
reactions.organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli NadK, Mycobacterium tuberculosis homotetramer), archaea (Pyrococcus, Archaeoglobus) and human cytosolic NADK / mitochondrial NADK2.
reactions.rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the definition - ATP + NAD+ -> NADP+ (+ ADP) is the NAD kinase reaction, the sole route to NADP+ de novo - and NadK/PpnK enzymes are single-activity homotetrameric kinases; the polyphosphate-utilising forms merely accept a different phosphoryl donor rather than carrying a second catalytic activity. This unnamed ModelSEED entry omits ADP entirely (10 C, 5 N, 3 P of the equation unaccounted for), so no real reaction is described.

direction_conflict.note: NAD kinase is physiologically irreversible (ATP-driven phosphoryl transfer; NADP+ is dephosphorylated by separate phosphatases, not by running the kinase backwards), so ModelSEED's '<' is wrong - but with ADP missing the written equation cannot carry a meaningful direction at all.

reactions.name: Nucleoside-triphosphate diphosphatase
reactions.enzyme_name: nucleoside-triphosphate diphosphatase (NTP pyrophosphohydrolase; ITPA/HAM1- or MazG-family)
reactions.organism_context: EC 3.6.1.19 is served by unrelated protein families: ITPA/HAM1-type pyrophosphatases (eukaryotes, incl. green algae) and MazG-type NTP pyrophosphohydrolases (bacteria).
reactions.rationale: No single protein owns this activity: ITPA/HAM1 enzymes are monofunctional, whereas the Thermotoga maritima MazG protein carries both NTP pyrophosphohydrolase and inorganic pyrophosphatase activities on one chain, and this synthetic '.chlamyexp' entry has no gene assignment to discriminate. IUBMB also deleted EC 3.6.1.19 in 2016 (transferred to EC 3.6.1.9).

direction_conflict.note: The equation hydrolyses dGTP but yields AMP (adenine for guanine; the product must be dGMP), yet the only physiological sense of any NTP pyrophosphohydrolase is hydrolytic (left-to-right here) — ModelSEED's '<' would condense AMP + PPi back into a triphosphate.

reactions.name: Dehydropeptidase II
reactions.enzyme_name: aminoacylase-1 (N-acyl-aliphatic-L-amino acid amidohydrolase; 'dehydropeptidase II', acylase I)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic ACY1 (human, porcine); homodimeric zinc amidohydrolase. Microbial counterparts (Streptomyces mobaraensis aminoacylase) are likewise single-activity.
reactions.rationale: EC 3.5.1.14 is aminoacylase-1/ACY1, a zinc amidohydrolase whose only catalytic activity is hydrolysis of the N-acyl bond of N-acyl-L-amino acids; its synthetic N-acylation under non-physiological conditions is the same reaction run backwards, not a second activity. No bi- or polyfunctional ACY1 form is reported.

direction_conflict.note: The products are combinatorial nonsense (L-serine + 2-oxobutyrate instead of acetate + L-glutamate), but the only enzymatically meaningful sense of an aminoacylase is the one consuming N-acetyl-L-glutamate + H2O, which is the left-to-right direction the LLM council picked.

reactions.name: Dehydropeptidase II

reactions.organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic ACY1 (human, porcine); homodimeric zinc amidohydrolase.

reactions.name: Deoxycytidine kinase
reactions.enzyme_name: deoxycytidine kinase (dCK)
reactions.organism_context: Human/mammalian cytosolic dCK of the deoxyribonucleoside kinase family.
reactions.rationale: dCK is a single-activity NTP:deoxycytidine 5'-phosphotransferase; its very broad donor range (all natural NTPs except dCTP) and acceptor range (dC, dA, dG, araC, gemcitabine) is promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity. No fused second domain is reported for DCK.

direction_conflict.note: dGTP is a legitimate donor for dCK but the co-product must be dGDP, not ADP; even so, NTP-driven deoxynucleoside phosphorylation is irreversible in vivo, so the left-to-right (kinase) sense is right and ModelSEED's '<' would have dCMP phosphorylate ADP.

reactions.name: lactate oxidation
reactions.enzyme_name: L-lactate dehydrogenase, FMN-dependent (LldD; yeast flavocytochrome b2/CYB2)
reactions.organism_context: Bacterial LldD (quinone-linked, membrane-associated) and S. cerevisiae flavocytochrome b2; the latter's cytochrome b5 haem domain is an electron-transfer module, not a second catalytic activity.
reactions.rationale: The MetaCyc template (L-LACTDEHYDROGFMN-RXN) is the FMN-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenase, whose single activity is the two-electron oxidation of L-lactate to pyruvate; the fused haem domain of flavocytochrome b2 only relays electrons to cytochrome c. Multi-subunit Lld complexes are separate polypeptides, which the protocol excludes from bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: beta-Tocopherol and 2,3-dimethyl-5-phytylquinol are both C28H48O2 cyclisation isomers, not a redox couple, so the two electrons from lactate oxidation go nowhere (charge is off by 2) and the real quinone/cytochrome acceptor that makes this reaction irreversible is absent; lactate-to-pyruvate oxidation is nonetheless the enzyme's only physiological sense.

reactions.name: NTPase
reactions.enzyme_name: nucleoside-triphosphate phosphatase (unspecific NTPase, EC 3.6.1.15)
reactions.organism_context: KEGG notes EC 3.6.1.15 occurs in eukaryotes and thermophilic bacteria; the plant (Pisum sativum) enzyme is calmodulin-regulated. Candidates include apyrase/NTPDase-family proteins.
reactions.rationale: EC 3.6.1.15 is an unspecific catch-all class (it also hydrolyses NDPs, thiamine diphosphate and FAD) with no single assigned protein, and this synthetic '.chlamyexp' entry carries no gene association, so the catalysing polypeptide cannot be identified. Calling it monofunctional would be a guess rather than a finding.

direction_conflict.note: The equation hydrolyses dGTP to ADP + Pi (the product must be dGDP), but every phosphoanhydride hydrolase runs irreversibly in the hydrolytic (left-to-right) sense; ModelSEED's '<' would synthesise a triphosphate from ADP + Pi without an energy source.

reactions.name: RXN-7763.c.chlamyexp.ADP_DGTP
reactions.reaction: (1) H+[0] + (1) dGTP[0] + (1) phytolmonophosphate[0] <= (1) ADP[0] + (1) Phytyl diphosphate[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: phytyl-phosphate kinase (VTE6)
reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana chloroplast phytol-salvage pathway; VTE5 (phytol kinase) makes phytyl-P, VTE6 phosphorylates it to phytyl-PP. These are two separate genes, not a fused enzyme.
reactions.rationale: MetaCyc RXN-7763 is the phytyl-phosphate kinase step, assigned to VTE6, a single-activity CTP/NTP-dependent kinase; the preceding phytol kinase step is a different protein (VTE5, with FOLK as a partially redundant paralogue). No bifunctional phytol/phytyl-P kinase is reported.

direction_conflict.note: dGTP as donor should give dGDP, not ADP; nevertheless the kinase (left-to-right) sense is the only physiological one, since phytyl-PP is committed to tocopherol/phylloquinone prenylation.

reactions.name: gamma-Amino-gamma-cyanobutanoate aminohydrolase
pathways: KEGG: rn00460 (Cyanoamino acid metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: nitrilase (nitrile aminohydrolase, EC 3.5.5.1)
reactions.organism_context: KEGG R01887 carries only the generic nitrilase ortholog K01501. In plants, NIT1-NIT3 are monofunctional arylacetonitrilases while the NIT4 subfamily handling cyanoamino acids is a genuine bifunctional beta-cyano-L-alanine hydratase/nitrilase.
reactions.rationale: The chemistry is unambiguous (nitrile + 2 H2O -> carboxylate + NH3) but nothing in KEGG or the literature fixes which nitrilase subfamily hydrolyses this gamma-aminonitrile, and the cyanoamino-acid context is exactly where the bifunctional NIT4 type operates. Choosing 'monofunctional' would be an unsupported default.

direction_conflict.note: Nitrile hydrolysis to the free carboxylate plus ammonia is irreversible — no nitrilase re-forms a C-N triple bond from glutamate and NH3 — so ModelSEED's '<' is untenable.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: dTDP-4-keto-2,6-dideoxy-D-glucose 4-ketoreductase (UrdR/OleU-type NAD(P)H short-chain reductase)
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces deoxysugar pathways: UrdR (urdamycin, S. fradiae) gives dTDP-D-olivose; OleU/AknQ are the equivalent 4-ketoreductases in oleandomycin/aclarubicin clusters.
reactions.rationale: KEGG R06446 gives no EC and only the comment '4-oxoreductase'; the step is run by a single-activity SDR-family sugar 4-ketoreductase (UrdR/OleU), identified from gene-cluster expression rather than purified mechanism, so the enzyme assignment is inferred. The bifunctional aromatase/ketoreductase LanV of the same pathways acts on the angucycline aglycone, not on the dTDP sugar, and is not this enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: Two bare H+ stand in for the NAD(P)H hydride (charge is off by 2), so the couple that sets irreversibility is missing; biosynthetic flux nevertheless runs toward the reduced sugar dTDP-D-olivose, i.e. left-to-right.

reactions.name: 3'-phosphoadenylyl-sulfate:glycochenodeoxycholate 7-sulfotransferase
reactions.enzyme_name: glycochenodeoxycholate 7alpha-sulfotransferase (bile salt sulfotransferase, cytosolic SULT)
reactions.organism_context: Defined as a hamster/rat hepatic cytosolic activity (Barnes et al.); the human liver counterpart is bile salt sulfotransferase of the cytosolic hydroxysteroid (SULT2) family.
reactions.rationale: Cytosolic sulfotransferases are single-domain, single-activity PAPS-dependent transferases, and EC 2.8.2.34 is a positional (7alpha) specificity of that family rather than a distinct architecture. The specific gene has not been cloned, so the protein identity rests on purified liver-cytosol activity.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and sulfotransfer is effectively irreversible in vivo, so the sulfate-forming (left-to-right) sense is the only physiological one.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
pathways: KEGG: rn00100 (Steroid biosynthesis); rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: sterol Delta7-reductase / 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DWF5 in plants, DHCR7 in animals)
reactions.organism_context: Plant phytosterol pathway (Arabidopsis DWF5, Marchantia polymorpha MpDWF5A); human DHCR7, loss of which causes Smith-Lemli-Opitz syndrome. KEGG assigns K00213 / EC 1.3.1.21.
reactions.rationale: DWF5/DHCR7 is a single-activity NADPH-dependent polytopic membrane reductase of the C7-C8 sterol double bond; no second catalytic activity is reported (the related DHCR24 Delta24-reductase is a separate gene). Delta5-avenasterol is the plant-pathway equivalent of the DHCR7 product.

direction_conflict.note: The EC 1.3.1.21 reaction requires NADPH, but both KEGG R07487 and the ModelSEED entry carry only 2 H+ (charge off by 2), stripping the couple that makes the reduction irreversible; sterol biosynthesis nevertheless runs toward the reduced Delta5 sterol, i.e. left-to-right.

reactions.name: 4,4'-diapophytoene:FAD oxidoreductase
pathways: KEGG: rn00906 (Carotenoid biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: 4,4'-diapophytoene desaturase (CrtN)
reactions.organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus staphyloxanthin pathway; CrtM (dehydrosqualene synthase) and CrtP/AldH/CrtQ are separate proteins.
reactions.rationale: CrtN is one flavoprotein desaturase with a single catalytic activity; the three successive desaturations collapsed into this entry (KEGG R09719+R09744+R09745) are its own processive chemistry, not separate enzymes, so the entry is not multi-enzyme. EC 1.3.8.2 defines free FAD as the acceptor, so the flavin couple here is the official statement rather than an abstraction.

direction_conflict.note: CrtN is a committed biosynthetic desaturase feeding staphyloxanthin; the FAD-reducing (left-to-right) sense is the physiological one and the reverse would require FADH2 to hydrogenate a polyene.

reactions.name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine:cobalt-precorrin-7 C5-methyltransferase
pathways: KEGG: rn00860 (Porphyrin and chlorophyll metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: cobalt-precorrin-7 (C5)-methyltransferase CbiE, fused as the bifunctional CbiET / CobL in many bacteria
distinct_activities: cobalt-precorrin-7 C5-methyltransferase (EC 2.1.1.289; CbiE domain) — the reaction in this entry
cobalt-precorrin-8 (C15)-methyltransferase with decarboxylation of the C12 acetate side chain (EC 2.1.1.196; CbiT domain; aerobic counterpart EC 2.1.1.132)
reactions.organism_context: Fused: Pseudomonas denitrificans CobL and the CbiET proteins covered by KEGG ortholog K00595 (which carries EC 2.1.1.132 + 2.1.1.289 + 2.1.1.196). Split: other bacteria/archaea encode a standalone CbiE (K03399) and CbiT, e.g. Methanocaldococcus jannaschii.
reactions.rationale: Blanche et al. purified a single P. denitrificans polypeptide, the cobL product, that performs methylation at C-5 AND at C-15 plus decarboxylation of the C-12 acetate side chain, and the IUBMB entry for EC 2.1.1.289 itself states the equivalent aerobic activity sits on 'the bifunctional enzyme EC 2.1.1.132'. The two methylations are on distinct domains (CbiE-like and CbiT-like) of one chain, so this is genuine fusion bifunctionality, lineage-dependent.

direction_conflict.note: The two domains run sequential, not opposed, SAM->SAH methylations committed to corrin ring assembly, so the bifunctionality does not license ModelSEED's reverse call; SAM methyl transfer onto a ring carbon is irreversible.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
pathways: KEGG: rn01110 (Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites)
reactions.enzyme_name: no single enzyme — the first committed step is levopimaradiene synthase (GbLPS), followed by several cytochrome P450 oxidations
reactions.organism_context: Ginkgo biloba terpene trilactone (ginkgolide) pathway.
reactions.rationale: KEGG R08402 is flagged 'multi-step reaction' and reads levopimaradiene <=> ginkgolide A; ModelSEED has further mis-mapped the substrate to copalyl diphosphate, so the entry spans a diterpene cyclisation plus multiple P450 oxidations/lactonisations and no single enzyme catalyses it. 'unknown' is the honest functionality call for a lumped sequence.

direction_conflict.note: GbLPS is itself a bifunctional class II/class I diterpene synthase whose internal intermediate is exactly the copalyl diphosphate ModelSEED put on the substrate side, and the whole sequence is committed biosynthesis toward ginkgolide A, so the forward sense is right even though the entry is unusable as a single reaction.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
pathways: KEGG: rn00360 (Phenylalanine metabolism)
reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified NAD(P)H-dependent cathinone (keto)reductase
reactions.organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) phenylpropylamino alkaloid pathway; the same reduction also occurs in mammalian metabolism of cathinone to (-)-norephedrine and (-)-norpseudoephedrine.

Nothing can be said about mono- vs bifunctionality.

pathways: KEGG: rn00523 (Polyketide sugar unit biosynthesis)

reactions.organism_context: MetaCyc RXN-14497; no EC number and no protein assigned
reactions.rationale: A GSH-mediated disulfide reduction with no enzyme attached; such exchanges run spontaneously or are accelerated by glutaredoxins, and I found no characterised GSH-dependent D-cystine reductase. GSSG is missing from the products (status MI matches C20H32N6O12S2).

direction_conflict.note: Restoring GSSG makes this a near-isoenergetic thiol-disulfide exchange whose direction is set by the cellular GSH/GSSG ratio rather than by any enzyme, so neither a forward-only nor a reverse-only bound is defensible.

reactions.name: eugenyl beta-primeverosidase
pathways: MetaCyc: Degradation (Degradation/Utilization/Assimilation); PWY-7114 (tea aroma glycosidic precursor bioactivation); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-DEGRADATION (Secondary Metabolite Degradation)
reactions.enzyme_name: beta-primeverosidase (GH1 diglycosidase)
reactions.organism_context: Camellia sinensis (tea) leaf; releases aroma aglycones such as eugenol during oolong/black tea manufacture
reactions.rationale: The tea GH1 diglycosidase beta-primeverosidase hydrolyses the intact beta-primeveroside off aroma aglycones in one step; substrate-specificity work and crystal structures show a single glycoside-hydrolase active site and no second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: A retaining glycosidase cannot condense free eugenol with free primeverose in water, so ModelSEED's reverse-only assignment has no enzymatic counterpart.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: S-glutathionyl-hydroquinone reductase (Xi-class glutathione transferase)
reactions.organism_context: E. coli YqjG, yeast Ecm4/Gto, Sphingobium PcpF, Phanerochaete chrysosporium PcGHR
reactions.rationale: GS-hydroquinone + GSH -> hydroquinone + GSSG is the defining reaction of the Xi-class glutathionyl-hydroquinone reductases, which work through a single catalytic cysteine and carry one activity. The MetaCyc entry names no protein, so enzyme assignment is from the chemistry.

direction_conflict.note: GSSG is missing from the products; the enzyme is a deglutathionylating reductase and does not run the glutathionylation of hydroquinone that ModelSEED's reverse direction implies.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
pathways: MetaCyc: COUMARIN-SYN (Coumarin Biosynthesis); PHENYLPROPANOID-SYN (Phenylpropanoid Derivative Biosynthesis); PWY-7186 (superpathway of scopolin and esculin biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: none identified (spontaneous lactonisation of the free acid; the catalysed route runs on the CoA thioester)
reactions.organism_context: Plant scopoletin/scopolin biosynthesis (Arabidopsis, tobacco)
reactions.rationale: Free (Z)-6'-hydroxyferulate lactonises to scopoletin without a catalyst; the enzymatic route in planta is the BAHD-family coumarin synthase COSY, which isomerises and lactonises the 6'-hydroxyferuloyl-CoA thioester, not the free acid. No protein is assigned to this free-acid step.

direction_conflict.note: The water released by lactonisation is missing (status MI:H:-1/O:-1|CI:1), so the dG estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call was computed on an unbalanced equation; pathway flux runs toward the coumarin.

reactions.enzyme_name: none (multi-step segment of tabtoxinine-beta-lactam biosynthesis)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas syringae pv. tabaci, MetaCyc PWY-7954
reactions.rationale: Tabtoxinine-beta-lactam is built from the lysine/DAP intermediate tetrahydrodipicolinate through several steps including acetylated intermediates and beta-lactam ring closure, so no single enzyme performs this conversion. The ModelSEED product formula (C7H11N2O4) is also not tabtoxinine-beta-lactam (C11H18N2O5) and the entry is mass-imbalanced (MI:H:4/N:1).

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthetic flux unambiguously runs tetrahydrodipicolinate -> toxin, but with several enzymes collapsed into one entry there is no single enzymology on which to base any direction bound.

pathways: MetaCyc: POLYKETIDE-SYN (Polyketide Biosynthesis); PWY-7673 (fusarin C biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: fusarin C O-methyltransferase (FUS9)
reactions.organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi / F. verticillioides fusarin gene cluster
reactions.rationale: The fusarin cluster deletion study assigns the carboxy-fusarin -> fusarin C methyl esterification to the stand-alone SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase FUS9, a single-domain MT with one activity. Identity rests on cluster genetics rather than a purified-enzyme assay, hence medium confidence.

direction_conflict.note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way; the +27.7 kJ/mol dGPredictor value driving ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for this cofactor pair.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
pathways: MetaCyc: Antibiotic-Biosynthesis (Antibiotic Biosynthesis); PWY-7419 (FR-900098 and FR-33289 antibiotics biosynthesis); SECONDARY-METABOLITE-BIOSYNTHESIS (Secondary Metabolite Biosynthesis)
reactions.enzyme_name: (R)-2-phosphonomethylmalate synthase (FrbC), EC 2.3.3.19
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus, FR-900098 / FR-33289 antibiotic pathway; homocitrate/citrate synthase family
reactions.rationale: FrbC is a citrate/homocitrate-synthase-family condensing enzyme that joins acetyl-CoA to 3-phosphonopyruvate at a single Claisen-condensation active site; it was characterised by heterologous expression of the frb cluster and shows no second activity.

direction_conflict.note: Acetyl-CoA condensations of this family are pulled irreversibly forward by hydrolysis of the thioester, so the retro-aldol/CoA-ligating direction ModelSEED assigns is not a physiological activity.

reactions.name: Lactate deyhdrogonase, FAD reducing
reactions.enzyme_name: NAD-independent (flavin-dependent) L-lactate dehydrogenase, LldD
reactions.organism_context: E. coli / Pseudomonas stutzeri LldD (FMN, quinone-coupled); yeast flavocytochrome b2 (CYB2). In some bacteria the activity is the three-protein LutABC complex, which is a complex, not a fused multifunctional chain.
reactions.rationale: L-lactate oxidation to pyruvate at the expense of a flavin is done by FMN-dependent L-lactate dehydrogenases that pass electrons to quinone or cytochrome c; each is a single-activity flavoprotein. No enzyme is known that reduces pyruvate with free FADH2.

direction_conflict.note: Substituting free FAD/FADH2 (Em' about -219 mV) for enzyme-bound FMN plus the downstream quinone acceptor inverts the computed thermodynamics and is precisely why both eQuilibrator and dGPredictor, and hence ModelSEED, call this reaction reverse-only.

reactions.enzyme_name: hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyl transferase (HQT/HCT, BAHD family), EC 2.3.1.99
reactions.organism_context: Plants: tomato and coffee HQT, poplar/Arabidopsis HCT
reactions.rationale: BAHD acyltransferases such as HQT/HCT transfer the hydroxycinnamoyl group from CoA to quinate in a single active site with no second catalytic activity. The 4-O-feruloyl regiochemistry is not pinned to a specific named protein, hence medium confidence.

direction_conflict.note: HCT/HQT are demonstrably reversible and the reverse direction (chlorogenate -> caffeoyl-CoA) carries real in-planta flux; all three dG estimates here sit within ~20 kJ/mol of zero, so neither a forward-only nor ModelSEED's reverse-only bound is justified.

reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) isothiocyanate[0] <= (1) NH3[0] + (1) Carbonyl sulfide[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: thiocyanate hydrolase (SCNase), EC 3.5.5.8
reactions.organism_context: Thiobacillus thioparus THI115 and related sulfur-oxidising bacteria; cobalt-containing nitrile-hydratase relative
reactions.rationale: Thiocyanate + H2O -> carbonyl sulfide + ammonia is thiocyanate hydrolase; the enzyme is an (alpha-beta-gamma)4 assembly with one catalytic cobalt centre, and a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional under this protocol. Note ModelSEED names cpd32581 'isothiocyanate' but its formula and aliases (CNS-, thiocyanate ion) identify thiocyanate.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolytic C-S/C-N cleavage releasing a gas (COS) is irreversible in vivo; no enzyme assembles thiocyanate from COS and ammonia.

reactions.enzyme_name: cobalt-precorrin-5B (C1)-methyltransferase, CbiD (EC 2.1.1.195)
reactions.organism_context: Anaerobic cobalamin pathway of Salmonella enterica and Bacillus megaterium
reactions.rationale: CbiD performs the single C-1 methylation converting cobalt-precorrin-5B to cobalt-precorrin-6A in the fully reconstituted anaerobic corrin pathway; it is a one-activity SAM methyltransferase with no second domain.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible; the +32.4 kJ/mol dGPredictor estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for the SAM/SAH pair.

reactions.enzyme_name: cytosolic sulfotransferase (thyroid-hormone sulfotransferase)
reactions.organism_context: Human and rat liver cytosolic SULTs; SULT1A1 and SULT1B1 dominate T4/T3 sulfation
reactions.rationale: Thyroxine sulfation is carried out by cytosolic SULTs, each a single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase with one catalytic activity. The Rhea entry names no isoform, so the specific protein is inferred from substrate preference.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and one-way; running it in reverse would mean regenerating PAPS from PAP, which sulfotransferases do not do.

reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) streptothricin D[0] <= (1) streptothricin D acid[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: streptothricin hydrolase, SttH
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces albulus; streptothricin-resistance enzyme (ST non-producer)
reactions.rationale: SttH hydrolyses the amide bond of the streptolidine lactam of streptothricins, converting streptothricin D into streptothricin D acid and conferring resistance; the purified enzyme was shown to have this single hydrolytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Lactam hydrolysis is irreversible; re-forming the streptolidine lactam would require ATP-dependent activation that this equation does not contain, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not an enzymatic possibility.

reactions.enzyme_name: PaaZ, oxepin-CoA hydrolase / 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase
distinct_activities: 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase, NADP+-dependent (N-terminal ALDH domain), EC 1.2.1.91
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli and other bacteria carrying the paa phenylacetate catabolic pathway
reactions.rationale: PaaZ is one polypeptide carrying an N-terminal NADP+-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase domain and a C-terminal MaoC-like hydratase domain; the hydratase domain performs exactly the oxepin-CoA ring hydrolysis of this reaction. Cryo-EM shows both active sites on the same chain with substrate channelling between them.

direction_conflict.note: This is the clearest bifunctionality-explains-direction case in the chunk: the ALDH domain immediately and irreversibly oxidises the semialdehyde made by the hydratase domain, pulling the ring hydrolysis forward, so ModelSEED's reverse-only bound is wrong.

reactions.enzyme_name: none (futalosine pathway segment MqnA -> MqnE -> MqnB collapsed into one entry)
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces, Helicobacter, Campylobacter, Thermus (futalosine route to menaquinone)
reactions.rationale: The three-substrate summary chorismate + inosine + PEP -> futalosine comes from the 2008 isotope-labelling study that defined the futalosine pathway, not from one enzyme; the real route runs MqnA (chorismate dehydratase), MqnE (radical-SAM aminofutalosine synthase) and MqnB (futalosine hydrolase). The entry is also mass-imbalanced, with C4H5O10P missing from the products.

direction_conflict.note: Biosynthetic flux runs chorismate -> futalosine, but with three enzymes lumped there is no single enzymology on which to set a direction.

reactions.enzyme_name: catalase HPII (KatE)
reactions.organism_context: Escherichia coli HPII; autocatalytic conversion of its own protoheme IX prosthetic group to heme d
reactions.rationale: HPII converts its own bound protoheme IX into cis-heme d using H2O2 during turnover, with heme d cis-diol as the intermediate; the catalyst is the catalase itself, which has one peroxide-utilising active site, so this is prosthetic-group self-processing and not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Oxidative heme maturation is a one-way event: heme d is never reduced back to protoheme plus hydrogen peroxide, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not an enzymatic reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Delta24-sterol C-methyltransferase (ERG6 / SMT), EC 2.1.1.41
reactions.organism_context: Fungi (Erg6) and plants/protists (SMT1/SMT2); this substrate pair, cholesta-5,7,24-trien-3beta-ol -> ergosta-5,7,24(28)-trien-3beta-ol, is the late-methylation branch of the ergosterol pathway
reactions.rationale: C-24 methylation of a Delta24 sterol with SAM is the single activity of sterol 24-C-methyltransferase; the substrate/product pair identifies the late-branch Erg6 reaction. Enzyme identity is inferred from chemistry and pathway position rather than an assay on these exact sterols.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-alkylation of an unactivated olefin is irreversible; the +43.9 kJ/mol dGPredictor value behind ModelSEED's reverse call has the wrong sign for the SAM/SAH pair.

reactions.organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana seed GAMT1/GAMT2 and angiosperm orthologues; GA deactivation by C-6 carboxyl methylation
reactions.rationale: SABATH-family GA methyltransferases carry one SAM-dependent carboxyl methyltransferase active site and no second activity; the GAMT clade is the only characterised catalyst of GA methyl-ester formation. Note that ModelSEED's substrate name 'GA41' is a naming artefact: the formula C19H23O5- and the product (O-methyl gibberellin A4) identify gibberellin A4.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent carboxyl methyl esterification is strongly exergonic and one-way; this and the other four gibberellin methylations in this chunk all rest on the identical dGPredictor value of +29.04 +/- 16.56 kJ/mol, a single group-contribution number for the whole O-methylation class whose sign is wrong for a SAM/SAH couple.

reactions.rationale: Methylation of the C-6 carboxyl of gibberellin A1 to its methyl ester is the GAMT reaction; SABATH carboxyl methyltransferases are single-active-site enzymes with one catalytic activity.

reactions.enzyme_name: Hypophosphite/2-oxoglutarate dioxygenase (HtxA)
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas stutzeri WM88; htxA also horizontally transferred to Alcaligenes faecalis WM2072
reactions.rationale: HtxA is a mononuclear Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate dioxygenase purified from P. stutzeri WM88 whose only reported activity is oxidation of hypophosphite (phosphinate) to phosphite (phosphonate) coupled to 2-oxoglutarate decarboxylation; the downstream phosphite oxidation is a separate protein (PtxD). Note the MSDB equation puts H2O2 where the dioxygenase uses O2, and MSDB's phosphinate record carries formula O2P (mass 65 implies H2PO2-), so the two missing P-H hydrogens exactly cancel the O2-to-H2O2 substitution and the balance check passes spuriously.

direction_conflict.note: Oxidative decarboxylation of 2-oxoglutarate makes hypophosphite oxidation irreversible left-to-right; nothing reduces phosphite back to hypophosphite, so ModelSEED's reverse call cannot be enzymology.

reactions.enzyme_name: Glycopeptide aglycone sulfotransferase StaL
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces toyocaensis NRRL 15009 (A47934 biosynthetic cluster)
reactions.rationale: StaL is a small single-domain cytosolic-type PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase; its crystal structures with PAP and with desulfo-A47934 show one sulfuryl-transfer active site and no second catalytic function, and it is the final tailoring step that converts desulfo-A47934 into A47934.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and the transfer completes the mature antibiotic, so the written reverse (PAP + A47934 regenerating PAPS) is not a reaction StaL runs.

reactions.enzyme_name: Unidentified aminonitrile-hydrolysing nitrilase (EC 3.5.5.-)
reactions.rationale: The chemistry (R-CN + 2 H2O to R-COOH + NH3) is textbook nitrilase chemistry, but I could not find any named protein that hydrolyses 2-amino-2-phenylacetonitrile to L-phenylglycine; the entry has no EC, KEGG lists no hydrolytic reaction on L-phenylglycine (only R13515 / EC 2.3.1.331), and whether a single nitrilase or a nitrile-hydratase plus amidase pair is intended is undetermined. Calling this monofunctional would be a guess, so it stays unknown.

direction_conflict.note: Nitrile hydrolysis is irreversible in water; the written reverse (L-phenylglycine + NH3 to the aminonitrile + 2 H2O) has no enzymatic precedent, so the LLM direction is right whichever protein does it.

reactions.enzyme_name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD, ACADM) acting on nonanoyl-CoA (C9)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation; chain length C9 falls in the MCAD (C4-C12) window
reactions.rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases are homotetrameric (MCAD/SCAD/LCAD) or homodimeric (VLCAD) flavoproteins with a single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity per chain; the specific family member is inferred from chain length, not confirmed for this Rhea entry. ACAD9's role in complex I assembly is non-catalytic moonlighting and does not count.

direction_conflict.note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the ETF/ETF-QO couple, which is why the written forward step has dG'o near +19 kJ/mol and ModelSEED calls it reverse; in vivo the electrons go to the quinone pool and the dehydrogenation is irreversible forward.

reactions.enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD, ACADVL) acting on icosanoyl-CoA (C20)
reactions.organism_context: Inner mitochondrial membrane; C20 saturated acyl-CoA is a VLCAD/ACAD9 substrate
reactions.rationale: VLCAD is a membrane-bound homodimer carrying one acyl-CoA dehydrogenase active site per subunit. ACAD9, the closest paralogue, additionally serves as a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor, but that is a structural/chaperone role and is excluded as moonlighting, so the enzyme stays monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: The irreversibility comes from ETF coupling, which the free FAD/FADH2 pair in this equation does not represent.

reactions.enzyme_name: Long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD, ACADL) / VLCAD acting on pentadecanoyl-CoA (C15)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
reactions.rationale: A single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity on a homotetrameric (LCAD) or homodimeric (VLCAD) flavoprotein; family membership is certain from the FAD chemistry, the particular paralogue is inferred from the C15 chain length.

direction_conflict.note: Free FAD/FADH2 replaces the ETF acceptor, which is what makes the written forward direction look thermodynamically uphill.

reactions.enzyme_name: Medium/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on undecanoyl-CoA (C11)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
reactions.rationale: Standard acyl-CoA dehydrogenase chemistry with one catalytic activity per subunit. Note the MSDB product record cpd34021 is named '(3E)-undec-2-enoyl-CoA', an internally contradictory locant string that is almost certainly a mangled (2E)-undec-2-enoyl-CoA; the chemistry is the normal 2-enoyl product.

direction_conflict.note: ETF coupling, absent from this equation, is what drives the dehydrogenation forward in vivo.

reactions.enzyme_name: Very-long-chain/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on palmitoleoyl-CoA (16:1 delta-9)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of monounsaturated fatty acids
reactions.rationale: One dehydrogenation activity per polypeptide; the distal 9Z double bond is untouched and is later handled by the separate enoyl-CoA isomerase, so no second activity is involved here.

direction_conflict.note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for ETF; the enzyme runs oxidation only.

reactions.enzyme_name: Long-chain/very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on heptadecanoyl-CoA (C17)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids
reactions.rationale: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family, one catalytic activity per subunit; the particular paralogue is inferred from the C17 chain length rather than confirmed for this Rhea entry.

direction_conflict.note: The ETF acceptor that makes the step irreversible is replaced here by free FAD/FADH2.

reactions.enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on elaidoyl-CoA ((9E)-octadecenoyl-CoA)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of trans-18:1 fatty acid
reactions.rationale: VLCAD is a homodimeric flavoprotein with a single acyl-CoA dehydrogenase site; the trans-9 double bond of the substrate is a spectator in this step.

direction_conflict.note: Free FAD/FADH2 in place of ETF is what inverts the apparent thermodynamic direction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD, ACADVL) acting on oleoyl-CoA
reactions.organism_context: Human/mammalian mitochondrial beta-oxidation; oleoyl-CoA is a canonical VLCAD substrate
reactions.rationale: VLCAD carries one alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity per subunit; its regulation by SIRT3/SIRT5 and cardiolipin binding are not catalytic activities.

direction_conflict.note: ETF coupling, abstracted away here as free FADH2, is what makes the oxidation irreversible in vivo.

reactions.enzyme_name: Very-long-chain/long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on linoleoyl-CoA (18:2)
reactions.organism_context: Mitochondrial beta-oxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acids
reactions.rationale: Single dehydrogenation activity per chain; the auxiliary enzymes needed for the 9Z/12Z bonds (enoyl-CoA isomerase, 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase) are separate proteins and are not part of this step.

direction_conflict.note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the ETF couple that drives the reaction forward.

reactions.enzyme_name: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase acting on docosahexaenoyl-CoA (22:6 n-3)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian beta-oxidation of DHA; physiologically the first DHA oxidation is largely peroxisomal (ACOX1), but that enzyme uses O2/H2O2 rather than the FAD/FADH2 written here
reactions.rationale: The FAD/FADH2 stoichiometry identifies this as the dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.8.-) family rather than the acyl-CoA oxidase family, and those enzymes are monofunctional homodimers/homotetramers; which paralogue handles a C22:6 substrate is not established, hence low confidence.

direction_conflict.note: As with the rest of this block, the ETF (or O2, for the peroxisomal route) acceptor that enforces the forward direction is missing from the equation.

reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) O2[0] + (1) BET[0] <= (1) H2O2[0] + (1) Formaldehyde[0] + (1) Dimethylglycine[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Glycine betaine monooxygenase / demethylase GbcA-GbcB (Rieske-type oxygenase system)
reactions.organism_context: Chromohalobacter salexigens DSM 3043; homologous GbcAB systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa and marine Rhodobacteraceae
reactions.rationale: The oxidative N-demethylation of glycine betaine to dimethylglycine plus formaldehyde is run by a two-component Rieske oxygenase: GbcA carries the single monooxygenase active site and GbcB is the separate reductase partner, so this is a multi-protein system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.

direction_conflict.note: The real system consumes NAD(P)H and O2; the equation substitutes H2O/H2O2 for the reductant, yet the demethylation is still irreversible forward - betaine is regenerated from dimethylglycine only by SAM-dependent methyltransferases, never by the written reverse.

reactions.enzyme_name: Phospholipid N-methyltransferase (PEMT / yeast Opi3 / bacterial PmtA), second methylation PMME to PDME
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian PEMT performs all three methylations at one site; in yeast Cho2 does the first and Opi3 the second and third, so this step is Opi3/PEMT2-type
reactions.rationale: These are single-active-site SAM-dependent methyltransferases that iterate the same methyl-transfer chemistry on successive substrates; repeating one activity is not bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible; the written reverse would be an SAH-dependent demethylation, which these enzymes do not catalyse.

reactions.enzyme_name: Exo-alpha-sialidase (ganglioside sialidase), GQ1b to GT1b
reactions.organism_context: Human plasma-membrane ganglioside sialidase NEU3 (also NEU4/NEU1 and microbial GH33 sialidases)
reactions.rationale: GH33 sialidases are single-domain glycoside hydrolases with one retaining/inverting active site that removes the terminal alpha-2,8-linked Neu5Ac; the specific human paralogue acting on GQ1b is inferred from NEU3's known ganglioside preference rather than confirmed for this Rhea entry.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis releasing free Neu5Ac is irreversible; re-sialylation needs CMP-Neu5Ac and a sialyltransferase, so the written reverse is not a reaction any sialidase performs.

reactions.enzyme_name: Exo-alpha-sialidase (ganglioside sialidase), GT1b to GD1b
reactions.organism_context: Human plasma-membrane ganglioside sialidase NEU3 (also NEU4/NEU1 and microbial GH33 sialidases)
reactions.rationale: Same single-active-site GH33 exo-sialidase chemistry as the GQ1b step, removing the next alpha-2,8-linked Neu5Ac; no second catalytic activity is involved.

direction_conflict.note: Glycoside hydrolysis with release of free sialic acid is irreversible; the reverse requires an activated CMP-Neu5Ac donor.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-12(1) methyltransferase BchR
reactions.organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum and other green sulfur bacteria (chlorosome pigment homologue series)
reactions.rationale: This step converts the C-12 methyl into an ethyl group, the activity assigned to BchR, a radical-SAM methyltransferase; BchQ and BchR are separate single-activity proteins (BchQ methylates C-8(2), BchR C-12(1)).

direction_conflict.note: Radical-SAM C-methylation consumes SAM irreversibly; the homologue series only ever grows in the forward direction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-8(2) methyltransferase BchQ (ethyl to propyl)
reactions.organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum; BchQ is required for low-light adaptation via C-8(2) homologue formation
reactions.rationale: BchQ iteratively methylates the C-8(2) position (ethyl to propyl to isobutyl to neopentyl); repeating one radical-SAM methyl-transfer activity on successive homologues is not bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible forward.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bacteriochlorophyllide d C-8(2) methyltransferase BchQ (propyl to isobutyl)
reactions.organism_context: Chlorobaculum tepidum; third round of C-8(2) methylation in the chlorosome pigment homologue series
reactions.rationale: Same BchQ active site, one more round of the same radical-SAM methylation; no second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is irreversible forward.

reactions.enzyme_name: Cytosolic catechol-estrogen sulfotransferase (SULT1A1 / SULT1E1), 2-hydroxyestradiol 3-O-sulfonation
reactions.organism_context: Human cytosolic SULTs; catecholestrogen sulfonation is a documented SULT1A1/SULT1E1 activity
reactions.rationale: Cytosolic SULTs are homodimeric single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases with one sulfuryl-transfer active site; which paralogue dominates for 2-hydroxyestradiol varies by tissue but none of them is bifunctional.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is a conjugation/detoxication step and runs forward; desulfation in vivo is done by separate sulfatases, not by reversal of this reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Benzylisoquinoline alkaloid N-methyltransferase (coclaurine N-methyltransferase type, EC 2.1.1.140), giving (R)-laudanosine
reactions.organism_context: Plant BIA pathways (Papaver, Coptis); (R)-enantiospecific BIA N-methylation is documented in Nelumbo nucifera
reactions.rationale: (R)-N-methyltetrahydropapaverine is (R)-laudanosine, and the only known enzymes performing BIA tertiary-amine N-methylation are the single-domain SAM-dependent CNMT/TNMT family, all monofunctional; the specific protein for the (R) substrate is inferred rather than confirmed.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-to-SAH N-methylation is irreversible; no SAH-dependent N-demethylase runs the written reverse.

reactions.enzyme_name: L-cystine C-S lyase (cystine beta-lyase; C-DES/Slr0077-type PLP enzyme); the same elimination on cystine is also run by cystathionine gamma-lyase
reactions.organism_context: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 C-DES (sulfur mobilisation for Fe-S cluster assembly); analogous cystine-directed activity in mammalian CTH/CSE and plant C-S lyases
reactions.rationale: C-DES is a single PLP active site that performs a C-S beta-elimination on L-cystine, releasing cysteine persulfide (thiocysteine) and leaving the aminoacrylate; Slr0077 also shows cysteine desulfurase activity, but that is the same PLP chemistry on a different substrate at the same site, i.e. promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains. Note that the MetaCyc/Rhea entry writes only the elimination half-step: free 2-aminoacrylate (dehydroalanine) is really the enzyme-bound intermediate, and its hydration to pyruvate + NH3 is omitted.

direction_conflict.note: A PLP beta-elimination that discards an aminoacrylate is irreversible; the written reverse would be a spontaneous Michael addition of thiocysteine to dehydroalanine, not an enzyme-catalysed step.

reactions.enzyme_name: 2-phosphonomethylmalate synthase FrbC (homocitrate synthase homologue)
reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces rubellomurinus, FR-900098 (antimalarial phosphonate) biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: FrbC was cloned and characterised as the enzyme that condenses acetyl-CoA with 3-phosphonopyruvate to give 2-phosphonomethylmalate; like other citrate/homocitrate synthase-family TIM-barrel enzymes it has one aldol-condensation active site and no second activity.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis of the acetyl-CoA thioester is what pays for the condensation, making the written forward direction irreversible for every member of this synthase family.

reactions.enzyme_name: Mn(II) oxidase MnxG, catalytic multicopper-oxidase subunit of the Mnx complex
reactions.organism_context: Bacillus sp. PL-12 / SG-1 spore Mn-oxidising complex (MnxE-MnxF-MnxG heteromultimer)
reactions.rationale: The active species is a multi-subunit complex (MnxE/MnxF accessory subunits plus the MnxG multicopper oxidase), which per the exclusion is not a bifunctional enzyme; MnxG performs two sequential one-electron oxidations, Mn(II)-to-Mn(III) and Mn(III)-to-Mn(IV), at one multicopper site, which is one iterated oxidase activity rather than two distinct ones.

direction_conflict.note: The written reverse would evolve O2 from water while reducing MnO2, which in biology happens only at the light-driven PSII Mn4CaO5 cluster; microbial Mn(IV) reduction uses unrelated respiratory cytochromes, so no enzyme runs this equation backwards.

reactions.enzyme_name: Sterol 24-C-methyltransferase (Erg6 / SmtA)
reactions.organism_context: Fungi; in Aspergillus fumigatus and A. flavus Erg6 methylates lanosterol to eburicol (in yeast the preferred substrate is zymosterol)
reactions.rationale: Erg6 is a single-activity SAM-dependent sterol C-24 methyltransferase; the Aspergillus enzyme performs exactly the lanosterol to eburicol methylation of this entry and no second catalytic activity is reported for it.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent C-methylation releasing SAH is effectively irreversible left-to-right; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate eburicol with SAH, which Erg6 does not do.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
reactions.rationale: The ModelSEED entry reduces to 'UTP = UDP' with no other species, and the pinned snapshot flags status MI:O:-3/P:-1, i.e. exactly one PO3 missing: the Rhea half-reaction's phosphoryl carrier (a protein phospho-histidine or a polyphosphate chain) was dropped because ModelSEED has no compound for it, so no enzyme can honestly be assigned to the equation as written.

direction_conflict.note: With the phosphoryl donor/acceptor absent this is not a reaction, so neither '<' nor '>' describes anything an enzyme does.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
reactions.rationale: Same artifact as rxn53888: 'CTP = CDP' alone, snapshot status MI:O:-3/P:-1, one PO3 unaccounted for because the Rhea half-reaction's phospho-carrier was not mapped; Rhea 55404/55408/55412 are a consecutive UDP/CDP/GDP triplet of one enzyme's half-reactions.

direction_conflict.note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
reactions.rationale: 'GTP = GDP' with nothing else; snapshot status MI:H:-1/O:-3/P:-1 confirms a whole phosphoryl group is missing. MetaCyc RXN-20670 and its neighbour RXN-20671 (rxn54354) belong to one phosphotransferase whose phospho-carrier ModelSEED could not represent.

direction_conflict.note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

reactions.enzyme_name: 2-amino-2-deoxyisochorismate (ADIC) synthase, PhzE (MST-family chorismate-utilising enzyme)
reactions.organism_context: Phenazine-producing Pseudomonas and Burkholderia; the homologous anthranilate synthase is split into separate TrpE and TrpG chains in many bacteria, so the fusion is lineage-specific
reactions.rationale: PhzE is one polypeptide carrying an N-terminal MST (ADIC synthase) domain and a C-terminal glutamine amidotransferase domain connected by a substrate-induced ammonia channel, i.e. two genuine catalytic activities on one chain rather than an associating complex.

direction_conflict.note: The physiological reaction consumes L-glutamine, hydrolysed by the fused GATase domain and channelled as NH3; that coupling is what makes ADIC formation irreversible forward and it is invisible in the free-ammonia equation ModelSEED holds, which is why the near-zero measured dG pushed ModelSEED the wrong way.

reactions.reaction: (1) S-Adenosyl-L-methionine[0] + (1) nocamycin E[0] <= (1) S-Adenosyl-homocysteine[0] + (1) nocamycin I[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: NcmP, carboxylate O-methyltransferase of the nocamycin pathway
reactions.organism_context: Saccharothrix syringae NRRL B-16468 (nocamycin biosynthetic gene cluster)
reactions.rationale: Deletion of ncmP accumulates nocamycin E and the recombinant protein was characterised as a SAM-dependent carboxylate O-methyltransferase producing nocamycin I; a single tailoring methylation activity with no second catalytic function reported.

direction_conflict.note: A biosynthetic SAM-dependent methyl esterification runs forward; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate the pathway end-product back to the shunt intermediate.

reactions.enzyme_name: EqxD, equisetin N-methyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Fusarium heterosporum ATCC 74349 (eqx cluster); the homologous silent cluster in F. fujikuroi lacks eqxD and therefore stops at trichosetin
reactions.rationale: Trichosetin is the N-desmethyl congener of equisetin, and the F. fujikuroi cluster differs from the F. heterosporum eqx cluster precisely by the absence of the N-methyltransferase gene eqxD, assigning this methylation to a stand-alone SAM-dependent methyltransferase.

direction_conflict.note: SAM to SAH methyl transfer onto the tetramic acid nitrogen is a committed biosynthetic step, not a reversible one.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
reactions.rationale: 'ADP = AMP' with nothing else; snapshot status MI:O:-3/P:-1 shows one PO3 missing. MetaCyc RXN-20671 sits next to RXN-20670 (the GDP/GTP entry), so both are half-reactions of one phosphotransferase whose phospho-carrier ModelSEED dropped.

direction_conflict.note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

reactions.enzyme_name: 12-oxophytodienoate reductase OPR2 / OPR3 (Old Yellow Enzyme family ene-reductase)
reactions.organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis thaliana, Solanum lycopersicum); the OPR3-independent jasmonate route
reactions.rationale: Chini et al. showed 4,5-didehydrojasmonate is reduced to jasmonic acid by OPR2 (and OPR3), FMN-dependent OYE-family ene-reductases with a single C=C reduction activity; the flavin is a tightly bound prosthetic group, not a second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: NADPH-driven flavin ene-reduction is effectively irreversible; no OPR oxidises jasmonate back to 4,5-didehydrojasmonate, so ModelSEED's '<' is the wrong sense.

reactions.reaction: (1) FMN[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) Coenzyme F420-0[0] <= (1) FMNH2[0] + (1) dehydro coenzyme F420-0[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: FbiB (F420-0:gamma-glutamyl ligase with C-terminal FMN-dependent dehydro-F420-0 reductase domain)
distinct_activities: FMNH2-dependent dehydro-F420-0 reductase (C-terminal FMN-binding nitroreductase-like domain)
reactions.organism_context: Mycobacterium smegmatis and M. tuberculosis and other F420-producing actinobacteria; in Thermomicrobia the reductase is a stand-alone nitroreductase-superfamily protein
reactions.rationale: Bashiri et al. showed the C-terminal domain of FbiB uses FMNH2 to reduce dehydro-F420-0 to F420-0 while the N-terminal domain is the gamma-glutamyl ligase, so one polypeptide carries two distinct catalytic activities.

direction_conflict.note: The documented reaction is FMNH2 + dehydro-F420-0 -> FMN + F420-0, which is right-to-left as ModelSEED writes the entry; ModelSEED's '<' is therefore the correct direction and the council's '>' would run the maturation step backwards.

reactions.reaction: (1) UDPglucuronate[0] + (1) Candesartan[0] <= (1) UDP[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) candesartan O-beta-D-glucuronoside[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Human UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A3, with UGT2B7/UGT1A10 contributing)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and intestine; ER-membrane UGT1A/2B family
reactions.rationale: UGT1A3 is the principal human UGT glucuronidating candesartan (characterised as highly selective for the tetrazole N2, with the acyl/O-glucuronide also formed); UGTs are single-activity glycosyltransferases, and homo/hetero-oligomerisation is not a second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: Glucuronyl transfer from UDP-glucuronate with UDP release is a committed conjugation step; ModelSEED's '<' would have UDP plus the glucuronide regenerate UDP-glucuronate, which no UGT does.

reactions.reaction: (1) UDPglucuronate[0] + (1) zolasartan[0] <= (1) UDP[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) zolarsartan O-beta-D-glucuronoside[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Human UDP-glucuronosyltransferase UGT1A3
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and intestine; zolasartan (zolarsartan) is one of the sartans assayed with recombinant UGT1A3
reactions.rationale: Alonen et al. showed recombinant UGT1A3 glucuronidates losartan, candesartan and zolarsartan; UGT1A3 is a single-activity membrane glycosyltransferase with no second catalytic function.

direction_conflict.note: UDP-glucuronate-dependent conjugation is effectively irreversible forward, so the ModelSEED '<' is the wrong sense.

reactions.enzyme_name: MelA, aspulvinone E synthetase (NRPS-like aryl alpha-keto acid dimerising synthetase)
distinct_activities: furanone-forming thioesterase (TE) domain: Claisen-type C-C condensation and cyclisation
reactions.organism_context: Aspergillus terreus; the same A-T-TE architecture with a quinone-forming TE gives atromentin synthetases
reactions.rationale: MelA is a single-chain NRPS-like enzyme that non-oxidatively homodimerises 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate; two catalytic domains sit on the one polypeptide (adenylation, and a furanone-forming TE whose catalytic triad cysteine was shown to be essential), while the T domain is a carrier, not a catalyst.

direction_conflict.note: The snapshot flags MI:C:-1/H:-1/O:-2 - the one-carbon leaving group lost in forming the C17 butenolide is missing, and the 2 ATP consumed by the adenylation domain are absent too, so the stored dG that drove ModelSEED to '<' is computed on an equation that is not the enzyme's reaction; the biosynthetic sense is nevertheless condensation (left-to-right).

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified fungal dioxolanone synthetase (phenylpyruvate homodimerisation)
reactions.organism_context: Guignardia (Phyllosticta) bidwellii, the grape black-rot pathogen, which secretes phenguignardic and guignardic acid as phytotoxins
reactions.rationale: Phenguignardic acid is a dioxolanone formed by dimerisation of two phenylpyruvate units derived from phenylalanine, but I found no publication naming or characterising the protein that makes it, so the catalyst and its domain content are genuinely unknown; by analogy to the NRPS-like aryl alpha-keto acid synthetases it would be multidomain, but that is inference, not evidence.

direction_conflict.note: Phenguignardate is a secreted end-product, so the condensation direction is the biological one; no enzyme is known that cleaves a dioxolanone back to two phenylpyruvates. If the catalyst is NRPS-like, ATP is also missing from this equation.

reactions.enzyme_name: Atromentin synthetase (NRPS-like quinone synthetase; AtrA / GreA / InvA1 type)
distinct_activities: quinone-forming thioesterase (TE) domain: Claisen-type C-C condensation and cyclisation
reactions.organism_context: Basidiomycetes (Paxillus involutus, Suillus grevillei, Hapalopilus, Tapinella) and Aspergillus section Nigri; polyporic acid and atromentin synthetases evolved independently but share the mechanism
reactions.rationale: Atromentin synthetases are single-chain NRPS-like A-T-TE proteins that non-oxidatively homodimerise 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate; the adenylation domain and the quinone-forming thioesterase domain are two distinct catalytic activities on the one polypeptide, and swapping only the TE domain changes the product class.

direction_conflict.note: The 2 ATP hydrolysed to AMP + diphosphate by the adenylation domain are absent from the ModelSEED equation; that is the energy coupling which makes the condensation irreversible, so a dG computed without it pushed ModelSEED to the wrong direction.

reactions.enzyme_name: MftD, mycofactocin-biosynthesis FMN-dependent oxidative deaminase (lactate-oxidase family)
reactions.organism_context: Mycobacterium smegmatis mc2155 and other mycobacteria/actinobacteria carrying mftABCDEF
reactions.rationale: MftD catalyses the oxidative deamination of AHDP to pre-mycofactocin and is a single-activity FMN-dependent oxidase; this ModelSEED entry is only the second half of that transformation, the hydrolysis of the C-3 imine, which in flavin oxidative deaminations is normally spontaneous rather than separately catalysed.

direction_conflict.note: Hydrolysis of an imine to the ketone with ammonia release is effectively irreversible in water; ModelSEED's '<' would condense free NH3 onto pre-mycofactocin, undoing the step that creates the cofactor's redox centre.

reactions.enzyme_name: 1-testosterone hydratase/dehydrogenase (AtcABC molybdoenzyme)
distinct_activities: 1-testosterone hydratase: water addition across the delta-1 bond at C-1
1-hydroxy-steroid dehydrogenase: C-1 oxidation toward the ring-A 1,3-diketone
reactions.organism_context: Steroidobacter denitrificans and Thauera spp.; 2,3-seco pathway of anaerobic androgen degradation, atcA is the pathway's marker gene
reactions.rationale: Yang et al. isolated and characterised the 'bifunctional 1-testosterone hydratase/dehydrogenase', the molybdoenzyme essential for anaerobic steroid A-ring degradation; it is a multi-subunit complex, but the two activities are attributed to the one catalytic molybdopterin subunit rather than to separate associating chains, and the substrate assignment here is inferred from the pathway chemistry.

direction_conflict.note: This is the bifunctionality-explains-the-conflict case: the hydratase half adds water to 1-testosterone and is immediately pulled forward by the dehydrogenase half en route to androstane-1,3,17-trione and the beta-diketone ring-A hydrolase, so the hydration sense (the council's '>') is physiological and ModelSEED's dehydration '<' is not.

reactions.enzyme_name: none - spontaneous thermal [1,7]-sigmatropic hydrogen shift
reactions.organism_context: Vertebrate skin after UVB photolysis of 7-dehydrocholesterol; also occurs in vitro and in foods
reactions.rationale: The previtamin D3 to vitamin D3 conversion is a non-enzymatic thermal isomerisation, accelerated by the membrane environment or by beta-cyclodextrin complexation but not by any protein; 'unknown' is used because there is no catalysing enzyme to classify, not because one could not be found.

direction_conflict.note: The isomerisation is a temperature-dependent equilibrium, but at body temperature in membranes it lies strongly on the vitamin D3 side and is pulled further by export and DBP binding, so the net direction is previtamin D3 to vitamin D3, the opposite of ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.reaction: (1) 3-phosphoadenylylsulfate[0] + (1) Bisphenol A[0] <= (1) Adenosine 3-5-bisphosphate[0] + (1) H+[0] + (1) bisphenyl A sulfate[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Human cytosolic sulfotransferase SULT1A1 (SULT1E1 also active on bisphenol A)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver and intestine; bisphenol A is a standard substrate of the phenol-sulfating cytosolic SULTs
reactions.rationale: Bisphenol A phenolic sulfation is carried out by cytosolic SULT1 enzymes, single-activity PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases; the obligate homodimer is two copies of the same chain, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS with release of PAP is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would resynthesise PAPS from PAP and an aryl sulfate, which SULTs do not do.

reactions.reaction: (1) S-Adenosyl-L-methionine[0] + (1) chermesin D[0] <= (1) S-Adenosyl-homocysteine[0] + (1) chermesin D methyl ester[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: NvfJ, methyltransferase of the novofumigatonin pathway (carboxyl methyl esterification)
reactions.organism_context: Aspergillus novofumigatus, nvf cluster; DMOA-derived meroterpenoid biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: Matsuda et al. placed NvfJ as the methyl esterifying methyltransferase acting after cyclisation; in the branch where methylation precedes Baeyer-Villiger oxidation, chermesin D is methylated to its methyl ester by NvfJ. A single SAM-dependent methyl transfer, with the methyl group serving as a carboxylate protecting group.

direction_conflict.note: A pathway-committed methyl esterification runs forward; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate and expose the beta-keto acid the methylation exists to protect.

reactions.reaction: (1) S-Adenosyl-L-methionine[0] + (1) asnovolin I[0] <= (1) S-Adenosyl-homocysteine[0] + (1) asnovolin K[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: NvfJ, methyltransferase of the novofumigatonin pathway (carboxyl methyl esterification)
reactions.organism_context: Aspergillus novofumigatus, nvf cluster; the nvfJ deletion strain accumulates asnovolin I, identifying it as the NvfJ substrate
reactions.rationale: In the main branch, chermesin D is Baeyer-Villiger oxidised to asnovolin I, which NvfJ then methylates to asnovolin K before NvfM reduces the enoyl bond; a single SAM-dependent methyltransferase activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM to SAH methyl ester formation is the committed forward step of this branch, the opposite of ModelSEED's '<'.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified dipeptidase acting on L-alanyl-L-cysteine
reactions.rationale: No publication tied a named peptidase to L-alanyl-L-cysteine; any of several broad-specificity cytosolic dipeptidases (CNDP2-, PepD- or PepV-type metallopeptidases) could do it, so naming one would be fabrication.

direction_conflict.note: Only hydrolysis is thermodynamically accessible as written; the ModelSEED '<' direction would condense free L-alanine and L-cysteine into a peptide bond with no ATP in the equation, which no enzyme does.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
reactions.organism_context: Mouse liver Sult2a8 is the characterised 7alpha-hydroxyl-preferring bile acid sulfotransferase; the human bile salt sulfotransferase SULT2A1 sulfates mainly at 3alpha, with 7-sulfates as minor products
reactions.rationale: Feng et al. identified Sult2a8 as a PPARalpha-regulated cytosolic sulfotransferase preferring the 7alpha-hydroxyl of bile acids, which is the activity this entry needs; cytosolic SULTs are single-activity PAPS-dependent transferases.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would regenerate PAPS from PAP and a bile acid sulfate.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
reactions.organism_context: Mouse liver (Sult2a8); taurine-conjugated cholate is within the 7alpha-hydroxyl substrate preference described for this enzyme
reactions.rationale: Same enzyme class as rxn56344: a cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase with a single catalytic activity, acting on the 7alpha-hydroxyl of a conjugated bile acid.

direction_conflict.note: Sulfoconjugation runs forward; the reverse is not a sulfotransferase reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
reactions.organism_context: Mouse liver (Sult2a8); taurochenodeoxycholate is a 7alpha-hydroxy conjugated bile acid of the preferred class
reactions.rationale: Same enzyme class as rxn56344/rxn56345; a single-activity cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase. Classical work on chenodeoxycholate conjugates found 3-sulfate as the major and 7-sulfate as a minor enzymatic product, consistent with a distinct 7alpha-preferring isoform.

direction_conflict.note: Sulfoconjugation runs forward; the reverse is not a sulfotransferase reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Bile acid 7-O-sulfotransferase (mL-STL / SULT2A8), a cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase
reactions.organism_context: Mouse liver Sult2a8 is the characterised 7alpha-hydroxy-bile-acid-preferring enzyme; human SULT2A1 is the nearest orthologue
reactions.rationale: Feng et al. characterised Sult2a8 (mL-STL) as the PPARalpha-regulated mouse hepatic cytosolic sulfotransferase that 7-O-sulfonates 7alpha-hydroxy bile acids, which is exactly the tauro-alpha-muricholate 7-sulfate chemistry here; cytosolic SULTs are single-domain enzymes with one sulfuryl-transfer activity (homodimerisation is not bifunctionality).

direction_conflict.note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS to the bile acid is the physiological direction; no sulfotransferase resynthesises PAPS from a bile-acid sulfate in vivo, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is not supported by the enzymology.

reactions.enzyme_name: Dopamine (catecholamine) sulfotransferase SULT1A3
reactions.organism_context: Human; SULT1A3/1A4 is the human-specific catecholamine sulfotransferase, highly expressed in gut and platelets
reactions.rationale: SULT1A3 is the dedicated human catecholamine sulfotransferase that sulfonates dopamine on its catechol hydroxyls (3-O major, 4-O minor); it is a single ~34 kDa cytosolic sulfotransferase domain with one catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent conjugation runs forward in vivo; aryl sulfotransferases show reverse sulfuryl transfer only in vitro with artificial donors such as p-nitrophenyl sulfate, never by consuming PAP plus dopamine sulfate at physiological pools.

reactions.enzyme_name: Iodothyronine sulfotransferase (SULT1A1, with SULT1E1 and SULT1B1)
reactions.organism_context: Human liver/placenta; rat orthologues characterised in parallel
reactions.rationale: Kester et al. systematically assigned sulfonation of 3,3',5'-triiodothyronine (reverse T3) and other iodothyronines to human SULT1A1, SULT1A2, SULT1B1 and SULT1E1; each is a single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferase with one catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Thyroid-hormone sulfation is a committed inactivation/clearance step driven by PAPS; the reverse (PAP + rT3 sulfate -> PAPS) is not a physiological reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Iodothyronine sulfotransferase (SULT1A1, with SULT1B1 and SULT1E1)
reactions.organism_context: Human; 3,3'-T2 is the preferred iodothyronine substrate of SULT1A1/1B1
reactions.rationale: 3,3'-diiodothyronine is the best iodothyronine substrate of the human phenol sulfotransferases SULT1A1 and SULT1B1 in the Kester/Visser surveys; all are single-domain cytosolic SULTs with one sulfuryl-transfer activity.

direction_conflict.note: Same as the other iodothyronine sulfotransferase entries: PAPS-driven conjugation is unidirectional in vivo.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase acting on 17beta-estradiol 17-O-glucuronide
reactions.rationale: No literature could be found for a sulfotransferase that sulfonates the glucuronate moiety of an estrogen glucuronide (the ChEBI name places the sulfate on C3 of the glucuronate, not on the steroid A-ring), so the catalysing protein is genuinely unidentified; the only safe statement is that the chemistry is a PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer.

direction_conflict.note: Whatever the enzyme, PAPS -> PAP sulfuryl transfer is the direction all PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases run; ModelSEED's reverse call would require PAPS synthesis from a sulfated conjugate.

reactions.enzyme_name: unidentified PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase acting on estriol 16-O-glucuronide

direction_conflict.note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is unidirectional in vivo regardless of which SULT isoform carries it.
