direction_conflict.note: Nucleotidyl transfer with PPi release is pulled forward by inorganic pyrophosphatase and produces a stable released metabolite; reverse-only flux (PPi + guanylylstreptomycin -> GTP) is not a described activity.

reactions.enzyme_name: Lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (LPH), phlorizin-hydrolase (glycosylceramidase) catalytic site
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian small-intestinal brush-border membrane; the mature enzyme is one polypeptide carrying both sites
reactions.rationale: Phlorizin hydrolysis to phloretin plus glucose is the defining activity of the phlorizin-hydrolase site of LPH; mechanism-based labelling showed the two activities sit on two separate catalytic glutamates (Glu1273 and Glu1749) of a single polypeptide, which is a genuine fused bifunctional enzyme rather than a complex.

direction_conflict.note: Both LPH sites are hydrolases, so its bifunctionality does not explain the conflict; glycoside hydrolysis at cellular water activity is effectively irreversible forward, and the eQuilibrator +14 kJ/mol that drives ModelSEED's reverse call is implausible for O-glucoside hydrolysis.

reactions.enzyme_name: Benzoate-CoA ligase (BadA / BclA / BoxL), adenylation half-reaction
reactions.organism_context: Anaerobic and aerobic aromatic-degrading bacteria (Rhodopseudomonas palustris BadA, Burkholderia xenovorans box-pathway paralogues)
reactions.rationale: Benzoyl-AMP is the enzyme-bound adenylate intermediate of benzoate-CoA ligase, an ANL-superfamily adenylate-forming enzyme; the domain-alternation that performs adenylation then thioesterification is one overall ligase activity (EC 6.2.1.25), not two distinct catalytic activities, so this is monofunctional.

direction_conflict.note: CoA, the acceptor that makes the overall ligation irreversible, is absent from this half-reaction; the isolated adenylation step is freely reversible (it is the basis of the standard ATP-PPi exchange assay), so neither a forward-only nor a reverse-only bound reflects the enzymology - net forward flux comes only from thioesterification plus pyrophosphatase.

reactions.reaction: (1) H2O[0] + (1) NADP[0] + (1) Hypotaurine[0] <= (1) NADPH[0] + (2) H+[0] + (1) Taurine[0]
reactions.enzyme_name: Flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 (FMO1); the historic 'NAD(P)-dependent hypotaurine dehydrogenase, EC 1.8.1.3' is a misassignment
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian (human and mouse FMO1); Fmo1-null mice accumulate hypotaurine and are taurine-deficient
reactions.rationale: Veeravalli et al. showed in vivo and in vitro that FMO1, a single-domain flavin monooxygenase, is the enzyme that oxygenates hypotaurine to taurine, and that the 1962 assignment of this step to an NAD-dependent hypotaurine dehydrogenase was incorrect.

direction_conflict.note: The equation is the discredited dehydrogenase formulation with O2 omitted and NADP+ standing in as oxidant; the real reaction consumes O2 and NAD(P)H, which makes hypotaurine -> taurine strictly one-way, and reduction of the taurine sulfonate back to a sulfinate is not a known biological reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Anthranilate-CoA ligase PqsA, adenylation half-reaction
reactions.organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, first committed step of alkylquinolone (PQS/HHQ) quorum-signal biosynthesis
reactions.rationale: Coleman et al. identified PqsA as an anthranilate-coenzyme A ligase and Witzgall et al. solved its N-terminal domain with the anthraniloyl-AMP intermediate bound, matching this reaction exactly; like other ANL-superfamily ligases it performs one overall ligation in two half-reactions, which is not bifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: Anthraniloyl-AMP is an enzyme-bound intermediate and CoA, the acceptor that sets irreversibility, is missing from the entry; the adenylation half-reaction itself is reversible (ATP-PPi exchange), so the direction is set by the downstream thioesterification and pyrophosphatase, not by this step.

reactions.reaction: (1) Methanol[0] + (1) o-quinone methide[0] <= (1) hydroxyclavatol methyl ether[0]

reactions.organism_context: Penicillium crustosum / P. expansum clavatol pathway; the o-quinone methide arises by spontaneous dehydration of hydroxyclavatol made by the Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate oxygenase ClaD
reactions.rationale: Fan et al. showed the hydroxyclavatol-derived ortho-quinone methide forms by spontaneous dehydration and that its subsequent 1,4-Michael additions are explicitly nonenzymatic; Liao et al. demonstrated the same o-QM couples to a wide range of nucleophiles under mild aqueous conditions, so no protein catalyses this alcohol-trapping step.

direction_conflict.note: The o-quinone methide is a transient, highly electrophilic species, so trapping by solvent methanol runs only toward the ether; the reverse (retro-Michael regenerating free o-QM) has no net flux.

reactions.enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) 1,4-Michael addition of ethanol to the hydroxyclavatol-derived ortho-quinone methide
reactions.organism_context: Penicillium crustosum / P. expansum clavatol pathway
reactions.rationale: Same chemistry as rxn56852 with ethanol as the nucleophile; the ortho-quinone methide addition steps in this pathway were shown to be nonenzymatic, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.

reactions.enzyme_name: unknown - most likely an uncatalysed intramolecular cyclodehydration of 2-aminobenzoylacetaldehyde
reactions.rationale: No enzyme could be found for this step; the close structural analogue 2-aminobenzoylacetyl-CoA is documented to undergo spontaneous intramolecular cyclization to 2,4-dihydroxyquinoline in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and the same aniline-nitrogen attack on the aldehyde followed by dehydration and aromatisation accounts for quinolin-4-ol here.

direction_conflict.note: Cyclodehydration to an aromatic quinolinol is driven by aromatisation and is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse would be hydrolytic ring-opening of an aromatic 4-quinolinol, which does not occur.

reactions.enzyme_name: Sphingosine N-methyltransferase (SAM-dependent; activity demonstrated in mouse brain, gene not identified)
reactions.organism_context: Mouse brain cytosol/membranes (Igarashi & Hakomori); the protein has never been cloned
reactions.rationale: The only characterisation of this activity is the 1989 demonstration of a SAM-dependent sphingosine N-methyltransferase in mouse brain producing N-methyl- and N,N-dimethylsphingosine; because no protein or gene has been assigned, mono- vs bifunctional cannot be determined.

direction_conflict.note: The entry lumps two successive N-methylations, but both are run by the same activity, and SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is thermodynamically one-way, so the reverse-only call is untenable.

reactions.enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT; yeast Opi3/Pem2, plant phospholipid N-methyltransferase)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian liver PEMT performs all three methylations; in yeast Cho2/Pem1 does the first and Opi3/Pem2 the second and third
reactions.rationale: The conversion of a phosphatidyl-N-methylethanolamine to the N,N-dimethyl species is the second methylation of the PE -> PC methylation pathway, carried out by PEMT in mammals and Opi3 in yeast; performing three sequential methylations is one catalytic activity applied to successive substrates, not polyfunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer onto an amine is effectively irreversible; a reverse-only bound would mean SAH-dependent demethylation of the phospholipid headgroup, which no methyltransferase does.

reactions.enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT; yeast Opi3/Pem2, plant phospholipid N-methyltransferase)
reactions.organism_context: Same enzyme family as rxn56984; the di-18:3 species points at a plant/yeast PLMT rather than mammalian PEMT
reactions.rationale: Second headgroup methylation of a di-linolenoyl phosphatidyl-N-methylethanolamine, catalysed by the phospholipid N-methyltransferase of the PE -> PC pathway; a single SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase activity, so monofunctional despite acting iteratively.

direction_conflict.note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is one-way; reverse-only flux is not an enzymatic possibility here.

reactions.enzyme_name: Phosphatidylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (PEMT)
reactions.organism_context: Mammalian liver; the 16:0/22:6 species is the classic DHA-enriched PC that hepatic PEMT generates

direction_conflict.note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is one-way, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call cannot be right.

reactions.enzyme_name: gamma-renin (tissue kallikrein-family serine endopeptidase, EC 3.4.21.54)
reactions.organism_context: mouse submandibular gland; peptidase family S1 (trypsin family)
reactions.rationale: EC 3.4.21.54 is gamma-renin, which cleaves the Leu-Leu bond of the synthetic tetradecapeptide renin substrate to give angiotensin I plus the Leu-Val-Tyr-Ser tetrapeptide - exactly this equation; it is a single-domain S1 protease with one catalytic activity (and note the substrate is a synthetic assay peptide, not a physiological metabolite).

direction_conflict.note: Serine-protease peptide-bond hydrolysis is irreversible in dilute aqueous solution; ModelSEED's direction would have the protease ligate angiotensin I to a tetrapeptide.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydrolysis of the imine generated by ephedrine dehydrogenase (EC 1.5.1.18)
reactions.organism_context: Arthrobacter globiformis / Pseudomonas putida ephedrine catabolism
reactions.rationale: MetaCyc's EPHEDRINE-DEHYDROGENASE-RXN (EC 1.5.1.18) makes this imine from (1R,2S)-ephedrine + NAD+, and RXN-21559 is the uncatalysed hydrolysis half that releases 1-phenylacetylcarbinol + methylamine; no enzyme or EC is attached to it, matching the classical Arthrobacter/Pseudomonas ephedrine degradation route.

direction_conflict.note: In the catabolic pathway the step runs hydrolytically and is pulled forward by downstream consumption; imine formation from phenylacetylcarbinol + methylamine (ModelSEED's direction) is the industrial/chemo-enzymatic route to ephedrine, not what this MetaCyc entry describes.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: 3-keto-levoglucosan beta-eliminase (LgdB1) plus 3-ketoglucose hydratase/dehydratase (LgdB2, or LgdB3 in some lineages) - two separate enzymes
reactions.organism_context: Bacillus smithii S-2701M levoglucosan pathway (lgdA/lgdB1/lgdB2/lgdC); Paenarthrobacter spp. substitute LgdB3 for LgdB2
reactions.rationale: Kuritani et al. showed the apparent hydration of 3-keto-levoglucosan to 3-keto-D-glucose is two enzymatic steps - beta-elimination by LgdB1 then hydration by LgdB2 - so no single protein catalyses this MetaCyc entry; each of the two is a separate, monofunctional protein (preceded by LgdA, EC 1.1.1.425, MetaCyc RXN-20952).

direction_conflict.note: The beta-elimination that opens the strained 1,6-anhydro bridge is irreversible and commits the anhydrosugar to catabolism, so the net runs toward 3-keto-D-glucose; ModelSEED's reverse direction would have to re-form the bicyclic anhydrosugar.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPx4 / PHGPx)
reactions.organism_context: mammalian selenocysteine peroxidase; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to all of these lipid-hydroperoxide reductions
reactions.rationale: GPx4 is a single-domain selenoperoxidase with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reduction of a lipid hydroperoxide (here 17(S)-HpDHA -> 17(S)-HDHA); its sperm mitochondrial-capsule structural role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: Peroxidase reduction of a hydroperoxide by GSH is physiologically irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from an equation that dropped the GSSG product, which is exactly the term that makes it irreversible.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: AsqJ, Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase
distinct_activities: dehydro-benzodiazepinedione epoxidase, driving the quinolone / quinazolinone skeletal rearrangement
reactions.organism_context: Aspergillus nidulans, 4'-methoxyviridicatin / viridicatin pathway; the quinazolinone outcome is substrate-directed
reactions.rationale: Einsiedler et al. showed AsqJ excises H2CO from suitable benzo[1,4]diazepine-2,5-diones to give quinazolinones, exactly this reaction; the same polypeptide carries two chemically distinct alpha-KG-dependent oxidations (desaturation then epoxidation) in the quinolone route, so it is bifunctional, though both sit in one active site rather than on two fused domains.

direction_conflict.note: 2-oxoglutarate, O2, succinate and CO2 - the couple that makes an Fe(II)/alphaKG dioxygenase irreversible - are all absent from the equation, leaving a formally redox-neutral C-C cleavage with no thermodynamic handle; the enzymology is unambiguously forward, so ModelSEED's deltaG-derived reverse call is meaningless here.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase (class A penicillin-binding protein; PonA1 in mycobacteria, PBP1a/PBP1b in E. coli)
reactions.organism_context: most bacteria: class A PBPs fuse both domains in one chain; standalone monofunctional glycosyltransferases (MtgA) and SEDS proteins (RodA/FtsW) carry only the glycosyltransferase activity
reactions.rationale: The MetaCyc parent reaction is mycobacterial lipid II + nascent peptidoglycan(n) -> decaprenyl-PP + peptidoglycan(n+1), the GT51 transglycosylase step; in most bacteria that step is run by a class A PBP whose single polypeptide also carries a D,D-transpeptidase domain, which is genuine fused bifunctionality rather than a multi-subunit complex.

direction_conflict.note: ModelSEED reduced the transfer reaction to 'lipid II <=> decaprenyl diphosphate', dropping the entire glycan acceptor and product (status MI:C:-40/H:-56/N:-8/O:-21), and EC 2.4.1.129 was transferred to EC 2.4.99.28 in 2023; nonetheless transglycosylation consumes lipid II and releases decaprenyl-PP, so the left-to-right (LLM) direction is the right one.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: phenylalkylamine N-methyltransferase (PaNMT), SAM-dependent
reactions.organism_context: Ephedra sinica (shoots); sequence-related to the benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid NMT family of Ranunculales
reactions.rationale: Morris et al. isolated the E. sinica NMT that makes (pseudo)ephedrine from nor(pseudo)ephedrine and also N-methyl(pseudo)ephedrine from (pseudo)ephedrine - exactly this reaction; it is a single SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase activity with broad substrate scope, which is promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.

direction_conflict.note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible (SAH is a product inhibitor, not a methyl donor), so ModelSEED's demethylation direction has no enzyme.

reactions.name: (unnamed in ModelSEED)
reactions.enzyme_name: CyrJ, PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase of cylindrospermopsin biosynthesis
reactions.organism_context: Raphidiopsis (Cylindrospermopsis) raciborskii and other cylindrospermopsin-producing cyanobacteria
reactions.rationale: Mejean & Ploux characterised CyrJ biochemically as the sulfotransferase that transfers sulfate from PAPS onto the desulfo precursor, giving 7-deoxycylindrospermopsin; it is a single-activity PAPS sulfotransferase with no second catalytic domain reported.

direction_conflict.note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS is driven by the high group-transfer potential of the phosphosulfate anhydride and is not reversed by PAP in vivo, so ModelSEED's desulfation direction is wrong.

reactions.organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus and relatives; MetaCyc then glycosylates hyosamine (RXN-23143, EC 2.4.1.-)
reactions.rationale: Hyosamine is N-methyl-2-deoxystreptamine and MetaCyc assigns only a partial EC (2.1.1.-) with no gene; PubMed/Europe PMC searches returned no characterised enzyme for this methylation, so I cannot judge mono- vs multifunctionality.

direction_conflict.note: Whatever protein runs it, SAM-dependent N-methylation is irreversible, so ModelSEED's demethylation of hyosamine back to 2-deoxystreptamine is not a real reaction.

reactions.enzyme_name: Asm21, ansamitocin O-carbamoyltransferase
reactions.organism_context: Actinosynnema pretiosum; homodimeric carbamoyltransferase family (cf. GdmN in geldanamycin biosynthesis)
reactions.rationale: Li et al. showed Asm21 carbamoylates both the C-7 hydroxyl of the ansamitocin polyketide and the 4''-OH of the glycosyl moiety - the same carbamoyl-transfer chemistry used iteratively at two sites, not two distinct catalytic activities; its close homologue GdmN behaves the same way, and the active enzyme is a homodimer, not a fused multidomain chain.

direction_conflict.note: Carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl phosphate is pulled forward by inorganic-phosphate release and is not reversed in vivo, so ModelSEED's decarbamoylation direction has no enzyme.
